Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 23, verse 1:

In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

﴿Indeed, the believers have succeeded (1).﴾

When the Truth, blessed and exalted is He, said in the verse before the previous one in Surat al-Hajj, ﴿that you may succeed (77)﴾ [al-Hajj], and "la'alla" (perhaps, it may be that) indicates hope, He, glorified is He, wished here to affirm the success of the believers, so He said: ﴿Indeed, the believers have succeeded (1)﴾ [al-Mu'minun]. This means that the hope from Allah is certain and confirmed, and therefore He used the particle of confirmation "qad" (indeed), which indicates the certain occurrence of the act. Thus the beginning of Surat al-Mu'minun harmonizes with the end of Surat al-Hajj.

His saying there, ﴿you may succeed (77)﴾ [al-Hajj], and here, ﴿have succeeded (1)﴾ [al-Mu'minun]: the root (f-l-h) is taken from the tilling of the land (filaha al-ard), and al-falh is splitting (al-shaqq). Hence they said: iron is made to succeed by iron (al-hadid bil-hadid yufallah), and splitting the earth is stirring and loosening it by ploughing (al-harth). This process is the foundation of planting, and from here the crop was called harth (tilth) in His saying, glorified is He: ﴿And among the people is he whose speech about the worldly life impresses you, and he calls Allah to witness what is in his heart, yet he is the most stubborn of opponents (204). And when he turns away, he strives throughout the land to cause corruption therein and destroy crops and animals. And Allah does not like corruption (205)﴾ [al-Baqarah].

The meaning of aflaha is: he attained the utmost of what the soul aspires to of good.

When you plough the land, it is empty, with nothing in it to perish. Therefore, the meaning of harth here is the crop resulting from the process of ploughing, which is indispensable for the completion of cultivation, because by ploughing you stir the soil so that air penetrates it, which increases its fertility and its readiness to receive the seed. We have previously discussed the process of germination and how it occurs, and that the plant feeds on the two cotyledons of the seed until it has a strong root able to draw from the soil. If the seed is cast into hard, unturned ground, the root finds difficulty in breaking through the soil and absorbing from it.

So the Truth, blessed and exalted is He, gives us an image from our observed reality, and borrows from the tilling of the land to express the success of the believer and his winning of everlasting bliss in the Hereafter. The farmer ploughs his land, waters it and tends it, and it gives him a grain yielding seven hundred grains, and so will the reward be in the Hereafter: ﴿The example of those who spend their wealth in the way of Allah is like a grain that grows seven spikes; in each spike is a hundred grains. And Allah multiplies for whom He wills, and Allah is all-Encompassing and Knowing (261)﴾ [al-Baqarah].

If the earth, created by Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, gives all this bounty, then what of the direct bounty from your Creator and the Creator of the earth that provides for you? Just as the farmer, when he toils and strives, his produce increases, so the believer, whenever he labours in worship and strives, his reward increases and his recompense is multiplied in the Hereafter.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 23, verse 2:

﴿Those who are humble in their prayer.﴾

It seems that the first attribute of the successful ones is in the prayer, and the discussion of it remains connected to what our Lord said in the preceding verses: ﴿O you who have believed, bow and prostrate and worship your Lord﴾ [al-Hajj: 77], and after it He said: ﴿So establish prayer and give zakah...﴾ [al-Hajj: 78].

Here, the first description of the believers who have succeeded is ﴿those who are humble in their prayer﴾ [al-Mu'minun: 2]. He did not say, for example, "those who perform it," because the matter of performing the prayer is settled as far as the believers are concerned. The point here is the manner and the mode: the point is humility (khushu'), submission, the tranquillity of the heart, its calm, and the awareness of God before whom one stands.

It is like when you tell your son: sit before the teacher attentively and listen to him with attentiveness. You are not instructing him to go to school or attend the lesson, for that is settled, so you concern yourself with the essence of the matter and the state it ought to be in.

Khushu' is that the heart be at rest and still in this task of its, so that it is not preoccupied with anything other than the prayer, because God has not made for a man two hearts within his body. And as long as he is in the presence of his Lord, Mighty and Majestic, he should not be preoccupied with anything else. Indeed, some of the knowers of the meaning of khushu' say: whoever deliberately seeks to know who is on his right or his left in the row, his prayer is invalidated.(2)

When 'Umar, may Allah be pleased with him, came upon a man who was praying and playing with his beard, he struck his hand and said: "If your heart were humble, your limbs would be humble."(3) This is because the limbs draw their energy from the heart and from the blood it pumps into them; so if the heart is distracted from the limbs, they would not move.

Therefore, when one of the jurists asked a Sufi: what is the ruling on one who forgets in his prayer? He said: "Is the ruling according to us or according to you?" He said: "Is there a difference between yours and ours?" He said: "Yes. According to the jurists, whoever forgets in prayer, the prostration of forgetfulness makes it up; but according to us, whoever forgets in prayer, we kill him." That is, it is a grave matter.

Then, does your Lord and Creator not deserve that you devote yourself to Him, may He be glorified, at least at the time of your prayer, which is five minutes at each of the five times, while He has left you the rest of the time to do as you wish? Do you consider it too much for your Lord that you devote your heart to Him and remember Him, may He be glorified? And this act is for your benefit before anything else: it is for your benefit to be in communion with your Lord, drawing from Him the energy and help, and exposing yourself to His breaths and illuminations, and taking from His lights and secrets?

And from the eagerness of the people of piety for the soundness and completeness of the prayer, one of them said to his companion, who was keen to lead the people in prayer: "Why are you keen on leading when you know that one who seeks authority is not given it?" He said: "Yes, I am keen on it so that I may get out of the disagreement between al-Shafi'i, who said that the Fatihah is recited behind the imam, and Abu Hanifah, who said that the imam's recitation is a recitation for the one following. So I am keen on leading, so that I may recite myself, and not be preoccupied with this disagreement."

1 Occasion of revelation of the verse: Ibn Abi Hatim, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Jarir and 'Abd ibn Humayd related from Muhammad ibn Sirin who said: "The Companions of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) used to raise their gaze to the sky during prayer and turn to the right and to the left. So Allah revealed: ﴿Certainly the believers have succeeded, those who are humble in their prayer﴾ [al-Mu'minun: 1-2]. Then they nodded with their heads, and they did not raise their gaze in prayer after that, nor did they turn to the right or the left." [Cited by al-Suyuti in al-Durr al-Manthur 6/83].

2 Said by Mu'adh ibn Jabal, may Allah be pleased with him, as related from him by Abu Muhammad 'Abd al-Haqq al-Ishbili in "al-Salah wa'l-Tahajjud" (p. 193).

3 Abu Muhammad 'Abd al-Haqq mentioned this report in the book "al-Salah wa'l-Tahajjud" (p. 198), edited by me, published by Dar al-Wafa, Mansurah, but he attributed it to al-Hasan al-Basri. He also mentioned that al-Hasan once saw a man playing with pebbles during prayer, saying: "O Allah, marry me to the houris (al-hur al-'in)." So he said to him: "What a poor suitor you are: you propose to the houris while you play with pebbles."

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 23, verse 3:

﴿And those who turn away from idle talk.﴾

Al-lagw (idle talk, that which is vain): speech that has no benefit in it. The term is also applied to every action that has no use. In another place the Exalted says: ﴿And when they pass by idle talk, they pass by with dignity﴾ [al-Furqan 72]: they are not occupied with it, nor do they give it any heed. The Qur'an also relates the words of the disbelievers when they heard the Qur'an: ﴿Do not listen to this Qur'an, and talk idly during it, that perhaps you may prevail﴾ [Fussilat 26].

Therefore, Allah, blessed and exalted, made among the delights of Paradise: ﴿They hear therein no idle talk nor sinful speech, but only the saying "Peace, peace"﴾ [al-Waqi'ah 25-26]. As if among the defects of this world and its calamities is that we hear therein much idle talk that has no benefit. In another verse, He speaks of the wine of the Hereafter, which does not take away the intellect and does not make its drinker rave with idle speech: ﴿They pass around therein a cup wherein is no idle talk nor sinfulness﴾ [al-Tur 23].

And ﴿turning away﴾ [al-Mu'minun 3]: i'rad (turning away) in origin means avoiding a thing, and it is an image of the soul's movement of recoiling from something. The people of knowledge set a measure for idle talk, and they say: every action for which you do not gain reward from Allah is idle.

Therefore, be always keen that all your movement be for Allah, so that you are rewarded for it. Like our companion who had a man come to him seeking his help in some matter, while he did not possess that matter, but he wanted to take advantage of this opportunity of good, and to have reward even in the movement of refraining from it. So he raised his hand: "O Allah, this is a servant who came to a servant, and I take his hand and turn to a Lord. So make the correction of his error in my intention a correction of Your intention." Meaning: though I am not able to fulfil it, I enter upon Allah with it from this side.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 23, verse 4:

﴿And those who are active in giving zakat (4)﴾:

Zakat (purification, growth) is first used in the sense of purification, as the Truth, blessed and exalted is He, says: ﴿Take from their wealth a charity by which you purify them and cause them growth, and invoke blessings upon them﴾ [At-Tawbah]. This is because heedlessness may befall a person while gathering wealth, so that something doubtful, for example, mixes with his wealth, and it then needs purification; and the purification of wealth is by giving charity from it.

Zakat also means growth. After wealth has been purified, zakat makes it grow and increases it, as He, the Exalted, says: ﴿He has succeeded who purifies it (9)﴾ [Ash-Shams]. That is: it develops the faculty of goodness within it, elevates it and raises it up, by looking at an action which, apparently, will diminish you, but which will bring you good afterwards, so that the faculties of goodness in yourself are thereby elevated.

Therefore, when the Truth, glory be to Him, spoke of riba, which is increase, He gathered opposites in one verse. Riba increases wealth: the usurer takes a hundred for a hundred and ten, whereas zakat apparently reduces wealth: a hundred after zakat becomes ninety-seven and a half. Then the verse comes to set before you the true measure: ﴿Allah destroys interest and gives increase for charities (276)﴾ [Al-Baqarah]. So the riba which you think is an increase is in fact destruction, and that which you think is a loss is blessing, increase and growth.

In another verse He, the Exalted, says: ﴿And what you give in riba to increase within the wealth of people will not increase with Allah; but what you give in zakat, seeking the Face of Allah, those are the ones who receive multiplied reward (39)﴾ [Ar-Rum]. That is: those for whom Allah multiplies and increases.

Just as our Lord, blessed and exalted is He, commanded us to humility (khushu') in prayer, He likewise commanded us regarding zakat. He did not say "those who pay" (mu'addun), but ﴿those who are active﴾ (fa'iluna) [Al-Mu'minun] (4). This is from the cultivation of the stations of worship within a person. When you pray, you should be humble and submissive in your prayer to Allah; likewise, when you give zakat, you elevate the faculty of goodness in yourself. When you work and strive, you do not work only to the measure of your need, but to the measure of your capacity, so that you take from the fruit of your effort what you need, while intending to set aside from the remainder the zakat of your wealth and your charity. Thus zakat is, at the outset, in your mind and in your intention.

Then the Truthful, glory be to Him, says:

﴿And those who guard their private parts (5)﴾:

Al-furuj: plural of farj (private part). The intended meaning is the two private parts of both the man and the woman. Allah the Exalted has commanded that they be guarded for the purpose for which they were created. The function of these organs is either to expel the body's waste, urine or feces, or the sexual act, whose goal is the preservation of offspring. A person must guard his private part in what Allah has made lawful for him, in His words, the Exalted:

﴿Except upon their spouses or what their right hands possess, for indeed, they are not blamable (6)﴾

Commentary on Qur'an 23:6:

﴿Except with their wives or those their right hands possess, for indeed they are not blameworthy.﴾

That is: they guard their private parts except from their wives, because Allah has made them lawful. ﴿Or those their right hands possess﴾ [al-Mu'minun]: ownership by the right hand (milk al-yamin) is lawful, but it has no place now; it has no existence at present, and this human international law has prohibited it. There are no longer slave women as there were before Islam. This is a ruling that has been suspended (mu'attal) because its subject no longer exists, and there is a difference between a ruling being suspended for lack of its subject and a ruling being abrogated (mulgha). Ownership by the right hand is a ruling that has not been abrogated; the ruling remains in force, but it has no subject.

To clarify this matter: suppose you are in a society where everyone is wealthy, with no poor person and no one entitled to zakat. Then you would say that the ruling on zakat is suspended. It is an obligation that exists, but it has no subject.

Some superficial thinkers say: "'Umar ibn al-Khattab (may Allah be pleased with him) abolished the share of those whose hearts are to be reconciled (al-mu'allafa qulubuhum)(1)." The truth is that he did not abolish it, nor could he abolish a ruling of Allah's rulings. Rather, he did not find anyone from the mu'allafa qulubuhum to give it to. So the ruling remains, but it has no subject. The proof is that the ruling on reconciling hearts still remains in effect in the lands of the Muslims until now, and we often try to reconcile the hearts of some writers and some groups so as to incline them towards Islam, especially since others exert their utmost efforts in this. Thus the share of those whose hearts are to be reconciled still exists and is acted upon.

Likewise we hear someone say: "'Umar (may Allah be pleased with him) suspended the hadd punishment for theft in the Year of Ramada." This claim contradicts the truth, because he did not suspend this hadd; rather he suspended one text and revived another text, since the legal principle says: "Avert the hudud by doubts (ishbuhat)." And since the thief stole to satisfy his hunger, he did not reach the minimum amount (nisab) of theft, and theft is only [punishable] after an amount sufficient for necessity.

One might say: if war breaks out between the believers and the disbelievers and they take some of ours captive and we take some of theirs, does ownership by the right hand not exist then? We say: yes, ownership by the right hand exists, but you will face international laws to which you have bound yourself and accepted, which call for the prohibition of slavery, and you must abide by them. But if slavery exists, then ownership by the right hand is established and present. This is a matter they take as a disgrace against Islam, and how it permits the master such-and-such from his right hand's possession.

This objection arises from these people's failure to understand the wisdom behind ownership by the right hand, and that the dignity of the captive woman is raised by this permission. The captive woman is taken in war or otherwise, and it was within the power of whoever takes her to kill her, but Allah, glorified is He, protected her blood and cultivated in the soul the matter of benefit, so He permitted the one who captures her to benefit from her and made her lawful to him as well.

Imagine this female slave or captive in the house of her master, with him having one or more wives, and she witnesses these marital relations in the society around her. It is among the wisdom of Allah that He permitted her master to have intercourse with her, because she will no longer see any superiority of the mistress of the house over her, since they have become equal. So if she bears a child from her master, she becomes free through her child, and it is as if Allah, glorified is He, moves affairs towards manumission and freedom. Do you not see that after this He opens the door of manumission and enumerates its causes, making it one of the recipients of zakat, a door of charity, and an expiation for some transgressions a person commits?

Then He, glorified is He, says: ﴿for indeed they are not blameworthy﴾ [al-Mu'minun]: meaning, we neither praise them nor blame them, as if the matter is confined to the narrowest scope.

(1) Abd al-Rahman ibn Muhammad al-Muharibi narrated from Hajjaj ibn Dinar, from Ibn Sirin, from Ubayda, who said: "'Uyayna ibn Hisn and al-Aqra' ibn Habis came to Abu Bakr and said: 'O Successor of the Messenger of Allah, we have a salty land with no pasture and no benefit in it. If you see fit to give it to us, then grant it to them.' He wrote a document for them about it and had witnesses to it, and 'Umar was not among the people. They went to 'Umar to have him witness it for them. When 'Umar heard what was in the document, he took it from their hands, spat on it and erased it. They became angry and said an evil statement. He said: 'The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) used to reconcile your hearts when Islam was still few, but now Allah has made Islam independent. Go, and strive your utmost; Allah will not look kindly upon you if you look upon others [with favour].'" [Cited by Abu Bakr al-Jassas in Ahkam al-Qur'an 3/160].

Then the Truthful Lord says:

﴿So whoever seeks beyond that, they are the transgressors.﴾ (23:7)

﴿Ibtaghā﴾ means sought (ṭalaba), and ﴿beyond that﴾ means other than what We have mentioned: the wives and what the right hand possesses.

We have previously mentioned that the word ﴿warāʾ﴾ (beyond, behind) is used in the Qur'an with several meanings. Here it means other than the wives and what the right hand possesses. Among its uses is also His saying, glorified is He: ﴿...and lawful for you is what is beyond that...﴾ (4:24), meaning: such-and-such has been forbidden to you, and I have made lawful for you other than what has been mentioned.

Warāʾ is also used to mean "after," because otherness may coincide in time, so that two things exist at the same time, whereas "afterness" has a different time. As in His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And his wife was standing, and she laughed, so We gave her good news of Isaac, and after Isaac, Jacob﴾ (11:71), meaning: after him, because the time is different.

Warāʾ also comes in the sense of "behind," as in His saying: ﴿And when Allah took the covenant of those who were given the Scripture, [saying], "You shall make it clear to the people and not conceal it," but they threw it behind their backs and exchanged it for a small price. And wretched is what they purchased﴾ (3:187), meaning: they placed it behind their backs.

Warāʾ also comes in the sense of "in front of," as in His saying: ﴿And there was behind them a king who seized every boat by force﴾ (18:79). It is known that the king was in front of them, waiting for every boat that passed by him and seizing it by force.

And His saying: ﴿Behind him is Hell...﴾ (14:16): Hell is in front of him, and it will come later; it has not yet passed, so it would be behind him.

The meaning of ﴿So they are the transgressors﴾ (23:7) is: they are the aggressors who exceed what has been prescribed for them. Our Lord, blessed and exalted is He, when He warns us against transgression, distinguishes between transgression in commands and transgression in prohibitions. If it concerns commands, He says: ﴿So do not transgress them﴾ (2:229). And if it concerns prohibitions, He says: ﴿So do not approach them﴾ (2:187).

1 Al-Azhari narrated from al-Farra' in the interpretation of this verse: "She laughed only out of joy at security, because she had feared as Ibrahim had feared." Al-Farra' said: "This is what the speech may bear, and Allah knows best. As for their saying that 'fa-ḍaḥikat' means she menstruated, I have not heard it from a trustworthy source." Ibn Manzur cited it in Lisan al-Arab, entry: ḍaḥika.

Then Allah, glorified is He, says:

﴿And those who are, to their trusts and their covenant, shepherds (who safeguard them) (8)﴾:

﴿Ra'un﴾ (those who safeguard): meaning they guard them and watch over them by carrying them out. Amanah (trust) is everything that one has been entrusted with. The first thing one is entrusted with is the covenant of faith in Allah, which Allah has taken from you. As long as you have believed in the God, it is incumbent upon you to carry out His commands.

So there is a trust of the Truth (al-Haqq) and a trust of creation. The trust of the Truth is what Allah, exalted is He, spoke of when He said:

﴿Indeed, We offered the Trust to the heavens and the earth and the mountains, but they declined to bear it and feared it; but man bore it. Indeed, he was ever unjust and ignorant (72)﴾ [al-Ahzab]. So, since you have accepted to bear the trust, you are obligated to discharge it.

As for the covenant ('ahd): it is everything a person pledges to do that is not sinful, and he is bound to fulfil what he has pledged. For when you make a covenant with a person concerning something, you have tied his movement and restricted it within the sphere of carrying out this covenant. When you say to me, "I will meet you tomorrow at such-and-such a place, at such-and-such a time, to do such-and-such," I will arrange the movement of my life based on this promise. If you break your promise, you have released yourself in your own time and acted according to your own comfort, while you have restricted my movement in my time, wasted my interests, and disrupted the movement of my day. Therefore, Islam has emphasized the matter of breaking promises.

ِ﴿And those who are constant in guarding their prayers.﴾ (23:9)

In the preceding verses He spoke of prayer in terms of the state of humility and submission within it. Here He mentions prayer in terms of its performance and its preservation, because guarding (ḥifẓ) means that you take each time of the prayers at its appointed moment, and the times of prayer are known by the call to prayer (adhān). But some say: the time is extended. The Ẓuhr prayer, for example, extends from the call to Ẓuhr until just before the call to ʿAṣr, and likewise for the rest of the prayers.

We say: Yes, this is correct, and the time is extended. But who guarantees you life until the end of the time? Who guarantees that you will pray ʿIshāʾ, for instance, before the call to Fajr? Yes, you remain free of sin until the last moment if you were able to pray and you prayed. But do you have this guarantee? It is like one who is able to perform Ḥajj but postpones it until the last days of his life: if he performs it, there is nothing upon him, but he cannot guarantee remaining alive until he performs it. Therefore it is obligatory to hasten to Ḥajj at the first opportunity, so that you do not incur sin if you miss it while you were able.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1–53, fragments of 54–66) on surah 23, verse 10:

﴿Those are the inheritors.﴾ (10)

﴿Those﴾ [al-Mu'minun]: meaning, the possessors of the qualities mentioned earlier, and they are six categories: those who are humble in their prayer; those who turn away from idle talk; those who are active in giving zakat; those who guard their private parts; those who keep their trusts and their covenants; and those who guard their prayers.

These are the inheritors. Inheritance (al-irth) is the taking of a right without a contract or a gift, because taking the property of another must be either by sale and contract, or by a gift from the owner of the property. Therefore, they asked the heir: "Is this your right?" He said: "Yes." They said: "What is your deed (sakk) for it?" That is: "Where is the contract by which you took it?" He said: "My contract and my deed is: ﴿Allah enjoins you concerning your children: for the male, what is equal to the share of two females﴾ [an-Nisa]." So it is a contract more firm and more exalted than the contracts of human beings.

And since my contract is from the Truth, may He be blessed and exalted, do not say that inheritance is taken without a contract, for it rests upon the most firm of contracts, which is the contract from Allah.

Many people depart from what Allah has legislated in matters of inheritance, out of love for wealth and monopolizing it, or out of stinginess toward those whom the Shari'ah has given a share. So whoever has sons and daughters gives the sons and deprives the daughters, and whoever has daughters writes over to them all that he owns so as to deprive his brothers and paternal uncles of their right in his property. This frequently happens in society.

It is incumbent upon you to be mindful of the matter of inheritance, to respect the Shari'ah of Allah concerning it and His division of wealth. Allah has given you wealth and left you to dispose of it throughout your life, and it is not for you to dispose of it also after your death. You must leave wealth to its owner and giver to dispose of it. Therefore Allah, exalted is He, said concerning inheritance: ﴿an obligation from Allah﴾ [an-Nisa] — that is, not from anyone else. And since it is an obligation from Allah, you must comply with it and implement it, and when you refuse it, you refuse Allah and reject His division.

Whoever reflects on the matter of inheritance finds all good in what Allah has legislated. Whoever loves sons should give daughters so that he does not corrupt the relations of his children after him. Some men who took all of their father's wealth and deprived the daughters come to us, saying: "We want to correct this error and redo the division according to what Allah has legislated."

Among some people we find flashes of faith: if some brothers refuse to redo the division according to the Shari'ah of Allah, one says: "I will bear my sisters' inheritance from my own property." Such people, Allah opens for them and blesses for them in what remains, because they have made their reliance upon Allah, so He increases them from His bounty and makes the little grow for them until it becomes much. As for one who relies on what is in his hand, Allah leaves him to it.

We marvel at one who makes his wealth for the daughters so as to deprive his brothers of it. We say to him: "You are not just in this disposition. You must treat them equally. For if you leave your daughters poor with no wealth, who will support and care for them after you? Their paternal uncles will support them." So let the treatment be equal.

The Truth, may He be blessed and exalted, when He causes these categories to inherit, causes them to inherit by His grace and generosity. The Prophet (ﷺ) explained this by his saying: "None of you will enter Paradise by his deeds." They said: "Not even you, O Messenger of Allah?" He said: "Not even I, unless Allah covers me with His mercy." (2)

As for His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Enter Paradise by what you used to do﴾ [an-Nahl] — this is specific to the mere entry into Paradise; as for the increase, it is from the bounty of Allah: ﴿and He will increase them from His bounty﴾ [an-Nisa].

Among His names, exalted is He, is (al-Warith, the Inheritor), and He said: ﴿And You are the best of inheritors﴾ [al-Anbiya]. So what does the Truth, glory be to Him, inherit from us?

Allah created creation and gave people the means of ownership, and distributed this ownership among His servants: this one owns such-and-such, and that one owns such-and-such, by the bounty of Allah, exalted is He. When the Day of Resurrection comes, all ownership returns to its owner, and the Truth, glory be to Him, will be the sole Inheritor on the day He says: ﴿To whom belongs the kingdom today? To Allah, the One, the Subduer﴾ [Ghafir].

Allah is the best of inheritors, because the inheritor takes what he inherits to benefit himself by it, but the Truth, glory be to Him, inherits what He left to others so that its good returns to them and He increases them, giving them manifold multiples. If He gives them in this world by means, then in the Hereafter He inherits these means and gives them from His bounty without means, where you live in Paradise at ease, with no toil, no fatigue, and no striving, and whatever occurs to your mind you find before you without moving a finger.

So: human beings inherit in order to take, but the Truth, glory be to Him, inherits in order to give. Therefore He is the best of inheritors.

1 Al-Qurtubi said in his tafsir (6/4641): "That is: they inherit the dwellings of the People of the Fire from Paradise. And in a report from Abu Hurayrah, from the Prophet (ﷺ): 'Allah, exalted is He, has made for every person a dwelling in Paradise and a dwelling in the Fire. As for the believers, they take their dwellings and inherit the dwellings of the disbelievers, and He makes the disbelievers in their dwellings in the Fire.' Ibn Majah narrated it with a similar meaning."

2 A hadith agreed upon (muttafaq 'alayh). Al-Bukhari recorded it in his Sahih (6463), and likewise Muslim in his Sahih (2816), from the hadith of Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 23, verse 11:

So what is it that the believers, who possess these qualities, inherit? The Truth, glorified is He, answers:

﴿Those who inherit Paradise (al-Firdaws); therein they will abide forever.﴾ (23:11)

Thus: Allah, glorified is He, made them inherit in this perishable world so that He might give them the everlasting Firdaws in the Hereafter. Firdaws is the highest part of Paradise. Allah inherits in order to benefit His servants, and the benefit ascends to them. In this world we benefit through means (asbab), but in the Hereafter we benefit without means. Allah inherits in order to give, not an equal to what He took, but more than what He took, because in inheritance we take what perishes, whereas Allah, exalted is He, gives us in His inheritance what endures.

But from whom do they inherit Firdaws?

They said: When Allah, blessed and exalted is He, created creation and placed in them the choice between faith and disbelief, and between obedience and disobedience, He ordained certain matters upon that. He made Paradise on the assumption that all creatures are believers, such that if they all entered Paradise there would be no shortage of places and no crowding. Likewise He made Hell on the assumption that all creatures are disbelievers, so that if all people disbelieved, each one would have his own place in Hell.

Accordingly, when the people of Paradise enter Paradise, they leave their places in Hell vacant, and when the people of Hell enter Hell, they leave their places in Paradise vacant. Thus the people of Hell inherit the vacant places in Hell, and the people of Paradise inherit the vacant places in Paradise.

Firdaws is the highest place in Paradise. For this reason the Prophet (ﷺ) used to say: "When you ask Allah, ask Him for Firdaws, for it is the highest of Paradise and the middle of Paradise" (1). That is because Firdaws is a garden upon the highest hill of Paradise, meaning a distinguished place within it. Elevation in matters of dwelling and gardens is something loved in this world: people love to live in high places, where the air and water are pure. Do you not see that they plant on elevated ground, and if the land is level they make low drainage channels that absorb the excess water which spoils the crops? For this reason He, glorified is He, says:

﴿Like a garden on a hill: a heavy rain strikes it, and it yields its produce twofold.﴾ (2:265)

Likewise, elevated land is not irrigated by standing water; rather it is watered by rain from the sky, which washes the leaves before it waters the roots, so that the plant is in its best condition. For this reason the Lord of Might says of it: ﴿it yields its produce twofold﴾ (2:265).

It is known that the leaves are the lungs of the plant, and upon them takes place the process of photosynthesis by which the plant makes its food. If the pores of the leaves are blocked and dust accumulates on them, this reduces the plant's ability to breathe, just as a person who suffers something in his lungs is troubled and his efficiency is reduced.

Another distinction of Firdaws is that Allah, glorified and exalted is He, Himself planted its trees with His own hand, just as He honored Adam, peace be upon him, by creating him with His hand, glorified is He, when He said: ﴿O Iblis, what prevented you from prostrating to what I created with My hands...﴾ (38:75).

It is narrated that Allah, blessed and exalted is He, when He created Firdaws and planted its trees with His hand, said to Firdaws: "Speak." When Firdaws spoke, it said: ﴿The believers have succeeded﴾ (23:1).

Then He, exalted is He, says: ﴿They therein abide forever﴾ (23:11), because the bliss of Paradise is lasting and enduring, never cut off. We know that the bliss of this world is limited, however much a person is given of it; it is cut off and perishing: either it leaves you through poverty and need, or you leave it through death. For this reason He, exalted is He, says of the bliss of the Hereafter: ﴿neither cut off nor forbidden﴾ (56:33).

Thus we observe at the opening of this surah that Allah, glorified is He, began by speaking of success in the Hereafter, as if He had presented the fruit of faith first and placed the reward at the beginning before you, as if He, glorified is He, were saying to you: this is the reward of one who believed in Me and followed My method. As He said at the opening of the surah (al-Rahman):

﴿The Most Merciful (1), taught the Qur'an (2), created man (3), taught him eloquence (4).﴾ (55:1-4) How is it that Allah created man first and then taught him the Qur'an?

They said: Because the one who makes a craft lays down its rules and determines its purpose first, before he begins making it. For example, and to Allah belongs the highest comparison, the one who makes a refrigerator, before making it, determines its function, its purpose, its maintenance rules and its aim.

The Qur'an is the method of man and the law of his maintenance in the movement of life. Therefore Allah created the method and laid down the law of maintenance before He created man.

(1) Narrated by Ahmad in his Musnad (2/335, 339), and by al-Bukhari in his Sahih (7423), from the hadith of Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him.

(2) Narrated by al-Hakim in his Mustadrak (2/392) from the hadith of Anas ibn Malik, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Allah created the Garden of Eden and planted its trees with His hand, then said to it: Speak. It said: ﴿The believers have succeeded.﴾" Al-Hakim said: this hadith has a sound chain but they did not record it. Al-Dhahabi said in his Talkhis: rather, it is weak.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1–53, fragments of 54–66) on surah 23, verse 12:

﴿And We certainly created man from an extract of clay.﴾ (23:12)

We have already spoken about the creation of man, and we know that the Creator, Mighty and Majestic is He, created the first man, Adam (peace be upon him), from clay, and from a part of him He created his spouse. Then, through intermarriage, the generality of mankind came into being, as He, exalted is He, said: ﴿And He spread from them both many men and women﴾ (4:1).

The matter of the creation of the heavens, the earth and mankind is one that God has kept to Himself, and no one has been shown it, as He, glorified is He, said: ﴿I did not make them witness the creation of the heavens and the earth, nor the creation of themselves, nor was I one to take misleading ones as helpers﴾ (18:51).

So do not give ear to these misleading people in every time and place, who claim knowledge and understanding, and whom we hear saying: the world was a single mass rotating rapidly, and parts broke off from it which formed the earth... etc. And concerning man they say: his origin was an ape, and so on through these superstitions that have no basis of truth whatsoever.

Therefore God, exalted is He, has given us faith-based immunity that protects us from being swept along behind these theories. He, glorified is He, has informed us of these people and warned us against them, because they witnessed none of the creation, and God did not take them as helpers, so they say such things. Therefore: this is a matter God has reserved for His own knowledge, so do not take His knowledge except from what God has told you.

The word al-insan (the human being) is a generic noun (ism jins) applied to the singular, the dual and the plural, the masculine and the feminine. Each one of us is a human being, as is evident from the fact that God, exalted is He, excepted from the singular, in its wording, a plurality in His saying: ﴿By time, indeed mankind is in loss, except those who have believed...﴾ (103:1–3). So He excepted from the singular a group.

The meaning of ﴿We created﴾ (23:12): We brought into existence from non-existence. We have already said that God also attributed the quality of creating to humans, with the difference between God's creating from nothing and humans' creating from something existing. God's creation has movement and life in it, so it grows and multiplies, whereas what humans make remains fixed in its state and does not change. Therefore the Truth, glorified is He, described His own essence, saying: ﴿So blessed is God, the best of creators﴾ (23:14).

As for the Qur'an's report, quoting Jesus (peace be upon him): ﴿I create for you from clay the likeness of a bird...﴾ (3:49), this is among his particular attributes (peace be upon him), and the bringing into existence in it was by a command from God which He caused to occur at the hand of His prophet.

So the meaning of ﴿And We certainly created man...﴾ (23:12) is: that is, the first man, Adam (peace be upon him), ﴿from an extract of clay﴾ (23:12). The word sulalah (extract): the essence of a thing, drawn out of it as a sword is drawn from its sheath, the scabbard in which it is placed. The sword is the deadly, effective tool, whereas the sheath is merely a protector and carrier of this important thing.

Therefore sulalah is the best part of a thing. God created the first man from the finest elements and kinds of clay, which is the foam (zubad) of clay. If you take a handful of clay and press it between your fingers, the foam slips out of it, and it is the best part of the clay, while remnants of sand and rough things remain in your fist.

When our master Hassan ibn Thabit wished to satirize the Quraysh for their enmity toward the Messenger of God (ﷺ), he said: "Permit me, O Messenger of God, to satirize them from the pulpit." The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Will you satirize them while I am among them?" Hassan said: "I will extract you from them as a hair is extracted from dough."(1)

The word sulalah is also applied to a good thing; they say: "So-and-so is of the lineage of such-and-such," and "So-and-so is a scion of glory," meaning in a context of praise. Even with horses they preserve known, noble lineages and register birth certificates for them that establish the nobility of their descent, and from here came the fame of the noble Arab horses.

Modern science has confirmed the truth of this verse: through experimental laboratory analysis, they have established that the elements composing the human being are the same elements as those of clay, and they are sixteen elements, beginning with oxygen and ending with manganese. The intended reference here is fertile clay soil suitable for cultivation, because the earth in general contains many elements; they have said: one hundred and thirteen elements.

1. Narrated by al-Bukhari in his Sahih (3531), and likewise Muslim in his Sahih (2489), from their shaykh Uthman ibn Abi Shaybah with his chain to Aisha (may God be pleased with her).

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 23, verse 13:

﴿Then We made him a drop (nutfah) in a firm place of rest.﴾ (13)

Meaning: after We made him a well-proportioned human being into whom We breathed a spirit, We made him reproduce from himself. Just as We created the first human from the essence of clay, so We create him in offspring from the essence of water and the purest thing in it, which is the nutfah (drop of semen). This is because a human being eats, drinks and breathes, and the blood draws off the essence of nourishment, while the remainder leaves the body as waste. Then the blood is purified and filters into the lungs and the kidneys, and from the essence of the blood come a person's vitality and the nutfah from which a human is created. Thus, even in the nutfah, he is of a selected lineage.

The nutfah, which is the basis of a human's creation, lives in a suitable medium, namely the seminal fluid. Therefore He, glorified is He, said: ﴿Was he not a drop of ejaculated semen?﴾ (75:37), and then We placed this nutfah ﴿in a firm place of rest﴾ (23:13). Qarar (place of rest): meaning a settled dwelling in which the nutfah comes to rest. The firm place of rest is the womb, which God created in this form, and He protected it with the bones of the pelvis, and made it prepared to receive this nutfah and to preserve it.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 23, verse 14:

﴿Then We made the sperm-drop into a clinging clot, then We made the clot into a lump, then We made the lump into bones, then We clothed the bones with flesh; then We produced it as another creation. So blessed is Allah, the best of creators.﴾

The scholars say: after forty days this sperm-drop transforms into a clot ('alaqah), and it was named so because it clings to the wall of the womb (rahm). The scholars call it the zygote, and it is a fertilized ovum, which begins to take its nourishment from the mother.

Among the marvels of Allah's power in the creation of man is that when a woman does not conceive, the menstrual blood descends upon her; but when she conceives, she never sees menstruation. Why? Because this blood descends when it has no purpose, and the mother does not benefit from it. However, once conception has occurred, it is transformed, by Allah's power, into nourishment for this new fetus.

Then He, glorified is He, says: ﴿then We made the clot into a lump..﴾ [al-Mu'minun 14]: it is a small piece of flesh of the size that can be chewed (mudghah, from the verb madagha, "to chew"). We have previously said that the lump is then divided into formed (mukhallaqah) and unformed (ghayr mukhallaqah), as He, the Exalted, said in the other verse: ﴿then from a lump, formed and unformed, that We may make clear to you..﴾ [al-Hajj 5]. That is a detailed explanation, whereas the verse before us speaks of the stages of creation in general, so that we do not suppose that the Qur'an contains repetition, as some claim.

The formed lump is that from which the limbs and organs of the human being are formed, while the unformed lump remains, as we have said, as a reserve for the preservation of whatever is destroyed in the body, as happens, for example, in wounds and similar injuries that afflict a person; the unformed portion then performs its reserve function.

Then the Exalted says: ﴿then We made the lump into bones, then We clothed the bones with flesh; then We produced it as another creation..﴾ [al-Mu'minun 14]: because throughout all these stages, the sperm-drop, then the clot, then the lump, then the bones and flesh, the fetus still remains dependent on its mother, attached to her, nourished by her. When Allah wills that it be born, it separates from its mother to begin its life on its own. That is why the moment of the fetus's separation from its mother during childbirth is a difficult matter, for it is about to receive an independent life that requires its bodily systems to work for the first time, and the first of these systems is the respiratory system.

It is part of Allah's mercy toward the fetus that it descends head-first so that it can breathe, and then the rest of its body emerges afterward. If the reverse happens and it descends feet-first, it may die, because it has separated from its dependence on its mother and has no capacity to breathe to preserve its new independent life. Therefore, in such a case, the physician resorts to performing a caesarean operation to rescue the fetus from this situation, before it suffocates.

Since the matter of human creation contains many lessons, signs, and proofs of Allah's power throughout these stages through which a human being passes, it was appropriate for the verse to conclude with His saying: ﴿So blessed is Allah, the best of creators.﴾ [al-Mu'minun 14]: because when you stand and contemplate Allah's power in the creation of man, you cannot but say: Glory be to Allah, blessed is Allah the Creator.

It is therefore related that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), when he recited this verse, 'Umar anticipated him and said, "So blessed is Allah, the best of creators," and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to the scribe: "Write it down, for it has been revealed." This is because it was a natural reaction to Allah's power, the wondrous making of His creation, and His marvelous creation; and this is a kind of harmony between the Arab natural disposition and the Arabic tongue, and the style of the Qur'an, which came in the language of its people.

It is also said that our master Mu'adh ibn Jabal uttered it as well, and likewise another man, 'Abdullah ibn Sa'd ibn Abi Sarh, with a difference in the outcome of this utterance. When 'Umar and Mu'adh, may Allah be pleased with them both, uttered it, it was an expression of approval and wonder that ends with Allah, acknowledging to Him, glorified is He, His power and the wondrous making.

As for Ibn Abi Sarh, he also said it out of wonder, but when his words coincided with the words of the Qur'an, he became conceited and claimed that revelation came to him just as it came to Muhammad. Why not, since he was saying what the Qur'an says? Yet he remained outwardly respectful, merely claiming that revelation came to him. But his arrogance increased, and his vanity led him to say: "I will reveal something like what Allah revealed," as though the existence of Allah were not necessary in this matter; so he apostatized, Allah forbid, because of it. And concerning him was revealed the saying of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿And who is more unjust than one who invents a lie against Allah, or says, "It has been revealed to me," while nothing has been revealed to him, or who says, "I will reveal the like of what Allah revealed"..﴾ [al-An'am 93].

Ibn Abi Sarh remained until the conquest of Makkah, when 'Uthman, may Allah be pleased with him, interceded on his behalf with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). When the Messenger saw 'Uthman's eagerness for him, he fell silent and said nothing about him. Thereupon 'Uthman took him and left. The Prophet (ﷺ) then said to his companions: "Was there not among you someone who would finish him off?" They said: "O Messenger of Allah, if only you had signaled to us with your head?" That is, you had gestured to us with this. Observe here the discourse of prophethood: he (ﷺ) said: "It is not befitting for a Prophet to have treachery of the eyes" (khA'inat al-a'yun), meaning: this is a conduct not suitable for prophets. Had you done it on your own initiative, there would have been no harm.

Then after that, the blessing of 'Uthman reaches Ibn Abi Sarh, so he believes and his Islam becomes good. Then he is appointed governor of Egypt, leads the conquests in Africa, and overcomes the uproar they raised in the lands of Nubia, as though Allah, the Exalted, was reserving him for this important matter.

1 - Athar of 'Umar: narrated by Ibn Abi Shaybah, 'Abd ibn Humayd and Ibn al-Mundhir from Salih Abi al-Khalil that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "By He in whose hand is my soul, it was concluded with what you spoke, O 'Umar" [cited by al-Suyuti in al-Durr al-Manthur 6/92].
2 - Athar of Mu'adh ibn Jabal: narrated by Ibn Rahawayh, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, al-Tabarani in al-Awsat, and Ibn Mardawayh from Zayd ibn Thabit, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) dictated to me this verse, ﴿And We created man from an extract of clay (12)﴾ [al-Mu'minun] up to His saying ﴿another creation (14)﴾ [al-Mu'minun]. Then Mu'adh ibn Jabal said: "So blessed is Allah, the best of creators." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) laughed, and Mu'adh said to him: "What made you laugh, O Messenger of Allah?" He said: "It has been concluded with ﴿So blessed is Allah, the best of creators (14)﴾ [al-Mu'minun]."
3 - He is 'Abdullah ibn Sa'd ibn Abi Sarh al-Qurashi al-'Amiri, of the Banu 'Amir ibn Lu'ayy, conqueror of Africa (Ifriqiyah). He embraced Islam before the conquest of Makkah, was among the scribes of revelation, commanded the right wing of 'Amr ibn al-'As when he conquered Egypt, and governed it after him for 12 years. All of Africa submitted to him, and he defeated the Romans in the Battle of Dhat al-Sawari in the year 34 AH. He died in the year 37 AH. [al-A'lam by al-Zirikli 4/89].
4 - Narrated by Abu Dawud in his Sunan (2683) and al-Nasa'i in his Sunan (7/106) from the hadith of Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas, in which the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Was there not among you a rightly guided man who would rise against this one when he saw me withhold my hand from his allegiance, and kill him?" They said: "O Messenger of Allah, we do not know what is in your mind; why did you not signal to us with your eye?" He said: "It is not befitting for a Prophet to have treachery of the eyes."

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 23, verse 15:

After these wonders that we have seen in the stages of human creation and his emergence into life, and the acknowledgment before God, exalted is He, that He is the best of creators, He (glory be to Him) reminds us that this life will not last. So He, blessed and exalted, says:

﴿Then after that, you will surely die.﴾

You may ask: How does the Truth, blessed and exalted is He, tell us about the stages of creation and then directly tell us about the stages of death and resurrection?

We say: God, exalted is He, joined them together so that when you receive life, there is in your mind and memory that which cuts this life short, so that you do not become arrogant and do not forget this end, and so that it is before your eyes, and you arrange the movement of your life on this basis.

Among this also is the saying of God, exalted is He: ﴿Blessed is He in whose hand is the dominion, and He is over all things competent. (1) Who created death and life that He may test you [as to] which of you is best in deed. (2)﴾ [Al-Mulk]. It is as if He, glory be to Him, announces our own deaths to us before He creates life in us, and He placed death before life so that you receive life and, before it, receive death, which cuts it short, so that you are not deceived by life and work for what comes after death.

The Truth, glory be to Him and exalted, addressed His Prophet (ﷺ) with His saying: ﴿Indeed, you will die, and indeed, they will die. (30)﴾ [Az-Zumar]. Some think that "mayyit" with the shadda (mayyit) means one who has already died, and this is not correct. Rather, "mayyit" with the shadda on the yaa is one whose affair is headed toward death, even if he is still alive. In this sense, all of us are "mayyitun." As for one who has actually died, he is "mayt" with a sukun on the yaa, and from it is the saying of the poet:(1)
"He is not one who has died and found rest, a dead man;
Rather, the dead man is the dead of the living."(2)

And the meaning of ﴿after that (15)﴾ [Al-Mu'minun]: that is, after the stages of creation that preceded, from the creation of the first man from clay, until He, glory be to Him, said: ﴿So blessed is God, the best of creators (14)﴾ [Al-Mu'minun].

Whoever reflects on this verse, which speaks of death, which no one denies and no one doubts, yet the Truth, blessed and exalted is He, emphasized it with two of the particles of emphasis: ﴿Then indeed you, after that, will surely die (15)﴾ [Al-Mu'minun]. He emphasized it with "inna" and with the lam. It is well known that we only resort to emphasis when we face a denier, so emphasis comes in proportion to the denial one faces, whereas one whose mind is blank needs no emphasis.

For example, you say to a blank-minded person who does not doubt your words: "Muhammad strives" (yajtahidu Muhammad). If he doubts, you emphasize for him with the nominal sentence, which indicates the establishment and stability of the attribute: "Muhammad is diligent" (Muhammadun mujtahid). And you increase the emphasis of your speech in proportion to the denial, so you say: "Indeed Muhammad is diligent" (inna Muhammadan mujtahid), or "Indeed Muhammad is surely diligent" (inna Muhammadan lamujtahid), or "By God, indeed Muhammad is surely diligent." These are degrees of emphasis according to the condition of the one you address.

So, the speech about death, which no one doubts, was emphasized, and He said: ﴿Then indeed you, after that, will surely die (15)﴾ [Al-Mu'minun].

1 - He is: Adi ibn al-Ra'la' al-Ghassani, a pre-Islamic poet, known for being attributed to his mother, while his father's name was lost. [Al-A'lam by al-Zirikli 4/220].
2 - Ibn Manzur mentioned it in Lisan al-Arab, entry: mawt.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 23, verse 16:

Yet even so, when He spoke of resurrection, which is the locus of doubt and denial, He (glory be to Him) said:

﴿Then indeed you, on the Day of Resurrection, will be resurrected (16)﴾

He did not say "la-tub'athun" (surely you will be resurrected) as He said in ﴿Indeed, you are going to die (15)﴾ [al-Mu'minun]. So how is that which contains affirmation and acceptance emphasized, while that which contains denial is not emphasized?

They said: Yes, because the speaker is Allah, the Exalted, who sees your heedlessness of death despite its clarity. When you were heedless of it, you were like those who deny it and reject it, so He emphasized it for you. Hence it is said: "I have never seen a certainty more like doubt than people's certainty about death." Everyone knows death and undergoes it, yet they keep it away from themselves and do not imagine it applying to them.

As for resurrection and the Last Day, their proofs are too clear for anyone to deny them, so they came without emphasis: ﴿Then indeed you, on the Day of Resurrection, will be resurrected (16)﴾ [al-Mu'minun]. The proofs of resurrection are too evident for the intellect to stop at them or deny them. Therefore I will state it absolutely, without excessive emphasis. As for one who harbors doubt about it or denies it, we emphasize the speech for him. Consider the insight of the Truth, glory be to Him, into the intellects, souls, and faculties of His creatures.

Then the Truthful, glorified is He, says:

﴿And We have certainly created above you seven paths, and We are never unaware of creation.﴾ (23:17)

We notice that the number seven has several occurrences in this surah, and secrets that we must contemplate. At the opening of the surah He mentioned seven categories: ﴿Certainly will the believers have succeeded (1). Those who are in their prayer humbly submissive (2)...﴾ [al-Mu'minun].

In the stages of human creation we find that he passed through seven phases: a extract of clay, then a drop (nutfah), then a clinging clot (alaqah), then a lump of flesh (mudghah), then bones, then flesh clothing the bones, then We developed him into another creation.

And here He says: ﴿And We have certainly created above you seven paths...(17)﴾ [al-Mu'minun].

And in another place He said: ﴿Allah is He who created seven heavens and of the earth, the like thereof...(12)﴾ [at-Talaq].

So these are seven for the ultimate purpose, seven for that which is served by it, namely man, and seven for the heavens and the earth created for man.

And tara'iq (paths): plural of tariqah, meaning "trodden," i.e., things that are hammered out. The thing that is trodden has a size that expands under hammering, just as a piece of iron is hammered, for example. So consider the sky and its vastness, and say: "Glory be to Him who hammered it out."

And you notice that the Truthful, glorified is He, did not mention the earth here. Why? They said: because we stand upon the earth firm, fearing nothing; rather, the fear is from the sky lest it collapse upon us. Therefore He says after it: ﴿and We are never unaware of creation (17)﴾ [al-Mu'minun]: so We will never be unaware of the sky above you, and We will hold it with Our hands, as He said: ﴿Indeed, Allah holds the heavens and the earth, lest they cease; and if they should cease, no one could hold them after Him...(41)﴾ [Fatir].

Then the Truthful, blessed and exalted is He, gives us the sensible evidence for this verse, and how Allah, exalted is He, raised the sky above us without pillars. An example of this is the bird that Allah holds in the sky: ﴿Have they not considered the birds above them, spreading their wings and folding them in? None holds them up except the Most Merciful...(19)﴾ [al-Mulk].

We know that the bird flies in the sky by the movement of its wings, which push the air and resist gravity, so it does not fall, like the swimmer who pushes the water with his arms to swim. When the bird folds its wings and yet remains suspended in the sky without falling, who holds it in this state? This is an image you witness that no one doubts. So if I tell you that I hold the sky so that it does not fall upon the earth, then believe and have faith, and infer the unseen from the seen.

It is as if the Truthful, glorified is He, in His saying: ﴿and We are never unaware of creation (17)﴾ [al-Mu'minun], says: be at ease regarding the sky above you, for We have made for it the necessary safeguards that secure your livelihood beneath its canopy. Be at ease, for it is in Our hands and under Our care.

But what is meant by His saying ﴿of creation (17)﴾ [al-Mu'minun]: is it man or the creation of the sky? The meaning is: We were never unaware of the creation of the sky; We built it upon arrangements and systems that protect you and guarantee your safety.

And ghaflah (unawareness) is leaving something because it has slipped from the mind, and this is a matter that can never apply to Allah, mighty and majestic is He, for slumber and sleep never overtake Him.

Then the Truthful, glorified is He, says:

﴿And We sent down water from the sky in a measured amount, and We caused it to settle in the earth; and indeed, We are able to remove it.﴾ (18)

He, exalted is He, says concerning water: ﴿And We sent down water from the sky in a measured amount﴾ [al-Mu'minun]. So is the water's place of rest the sky? No. The water's place of rest is the earth, as stated in the words of Allah, exalted is He: ﴿Say, "Do you indeed disbelieve in He who created the earth in two days and attribute to Him equals? That is the Lord of the worlds. And He placed within it firm mountains from above it and blessed it and determined therein its sustenance in four days - equal for those who ask."﴾ [Fussilat].

When the Creator, mighty and majestic is He, brought man into this existence, He placed in the earth the means of sustaining his life: air, food and water. And man, as we have said, can endure hunger, and his endurance for water is less, but he has no endurance for air. Therefore the power of Allah willed that it not be owned by anyone, because it is the first foundation of life. The atmospheric envelope and the air surrounding the earth belong to it and are a part of it, included under His words: ﴿And determined therein its sustenance﴾ [Fussilat]. The evidence is that when they leave the earth's sphere, the air is absent.

And among the wisdom and power of the Creator, mighty and majestic is He, is that He made the water on the earth salty, because salt is fundamental to the preservation of things that are subject to corruption. Fresh water is liable to change and stagnation, and with salt we preserve what we fear will change: we put it on food to keep it, and we use it in tanning hides, etc.

Therefore the poet said:
"O men of religion, O salt of the land,
If salt itself becomes corrupt, who will restore the salt?"

So: the origin of water is in the earth, but it descends from the sky after the process of evaporation that purifies it, so it comes down fresh, fit for drinking and irrigation. We have said that the Creator, glorified is He, made the extent of water on the earth greater than the extent of dry land, so that the area of evaporation widens and the rain forms that suffices the needs of the people of the earth.

And from Allah's mercy toward us is that water descends from the sky ﴿in a measured amount﴾ [al-Mu'minun]: meaning, by calculation and according to need. For if it descended all at once, it would become a destructive flood, as happened to the people of Noah and the people of Ma'rib. In another place He, glorified is He, says: ﴿And there is not a thing but that with Us are its depositories, and We do not send it down except in a known measure﴾ [al-Hijr].

Then He, glorified is He, says: ﴿So We caused it to settle in the earth...﴾ (18) [al-Mu'minun]: because we take our need from the rainwater, and the remainder seeps into the depths of the earth, as He, glorified is He, said: ﴿And He makes it flow as springs in the earth﴾ [al-Zumar]. Among the wondrous power of Allah regarding groundwater is that it travels in different channels, so that fresh water does not mix with salt water, along with the property of water that it seeks passages. Those working in well-drilling find wonders in this: they may find fresh water beside salty water, and even in the midst of the sea, because it is not channeled, but rather flows in capillaries that separate from one another.

Groundwater is a natural reserve of water that we bring out when needed, and it supports us when the fresh water on the surface dries up: ﴿So We caused it to settle in the earth...﴾ (18) [al-Mu'minun]: so that it may be a reserve for the time of need; when the rain dries up, you can extract it.

Then the Truthful, glorified is He, reminds us of His power to remove this blessing: ﴿And indeed, We are able to remove it﴾ (18) [al-Mu'minun]: meaning, conduct yourselves with this blessing in a way that does not expose it to vanishing. And He said in another place: ﴿Say, "Have you considered: if your water should become sunken, who would bring you clear water?"﴾ [al-Mulk].

When you count the blessings of Allah with which He has favored us, beginning with the blessing of water: ﴿And We sent down water from the sky in a measured amount﴾ (18) [al-Mu'minun], you will find them also seven. It appears that this number has secrets in this surah: seven attributes of the believers are mentioned, seven stages of the creation of man, seven heavens and earth, and here He mentions seven of His blessings upon us. Therefore the scholars have paused at this very number.

I recall that while we were in the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia, and I was a professor at the College of Shari'ah, along with some of the professors and the head of our mission Sheikh Zaki Ghaith - may Allah have mercy on him and forgive him - and the head of the Ma'arif mission Ustadh Salah Bey al-Baqir, and there always sat with us the Shaykh of the scholars of the Kingdom at that time, al-Sayyid Ishaq Azzouz, and he would gather us every night at the hotel where we were staying, and we would study some matters of knowledge.

Shaykh Ibrahim Atiyya raised the question of this number in the Noble Qur'an. He was reading in the Tafsir of al-Qurtubi and found in it: 'Umar ibn al-Khattab said to Ibn 'Abbas: "O Ibn 'Abbas, do you know when Laylat al-Qadr is?" Ibn 'Abbas said: "The strongest assumption is that it is the night of the twenty-seventh." When we heard this statement, we said: "This is seven, and this is twenty-seven." When we disagreed, Shaykh Muhammad Abu 'Ali - may Allah prolong his life - suggested that we go and pray in the Haram instead of praying in the hotel, in accordance with the Sunnah of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), for he would turn to prayer whenever a matter distressed him. We said: "Perhaps Allah will open this question to us."

After we had prayed, we sat discussing this matter, when a man we did not know, with the appearance of the majdhubin (those in spiritual rapture), indifferent to himself, sat down beside us and listened to what we were saying. Then he joined our conversation and said: "Did not the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: 'Seek it in the last ten of Ramadan'? (1)" So: set aside the twenty days, and calculate within the last ten. Then we looked, but did not find him. It is as if the unit of time in which Laylat al-Qadr is found is these ten, and as if in this sense it is the night of the seventh, and this too is one of the secrets of this number: ﴿And above every possessor of knowledge is one who knows﴾ (76) [Yusuf].

May Allah prolong the lives of those of them who remain, and forgive those who have passed.

1 - Narrated by al-Bukhari in his Sahih (2021) from the hadith of Ibn 'Abbas, and narrated by Muslim in his Sahih (1166), Book of Fasting, from Abu Hurayra, may Allah be pleased with him, with the wording: "I was shown Laylat al-Qadr, then some of my family woke me and I forgot it, so seek it in the last (ghawabir) ten."

Then the Mighty and Majestic says:

﴿Then We produced for you thereby gardens of date palms and grapevines; in them you have abundant fruits, and from them you eat.﴾

Al-Jannah (the garden): a place full of tall trees and crops that shelter the one who walks in it, or that shelter him from the outside, so that he has no need, for the requirements of his life, of anything else. It is so complete that it suffices him, and he has no need to leave it. He chose these two kinds, ﴿date palms and grapevines﴾, because of their standing among the Arabs. And he said ﴿abundant fruits﴾ because he did not restrict all the kinds (of fruit).

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 23, verse 20:

﴿And a tree that grows out of Mount Sinai, producing oil and a relish for those who eat.﴾ (20)

Al-Tur: a mountain attributed to Sinai, and Sinai is a good place, because Allah blessed it. Al-Tur is the mountain where Allah spoke to Musa, so it is a blessed place, just as Allah blessed the land of Bayt al-Maqdis, when He said: ﴿Glory be to the One who took His servant by night from al-Masjid al-Haram to al-Masjid al-Aqsa, whose surroundings We have blessed﴾ (1) [al-Isra'].

The meaning of ﴿grows with oil﴾ (20) [al-Mu'minun]: al-Duhn (oil, i.e. fat/grease) is al-dasm (fatty substance), and what is meant here is the olive tree, from which they extract the well-known olive oil. ﴿And a relish for those who eat﴾ (20) [al-Mu'minun]: that is, they make it a condiment into which they dip bread and eat it, and it is among the most appetizing and delicious foods for those who grow olives in Sinai and in the lands of al-Sham. We tasted this famous dish in Lebanon, when we went there during the olive harvest season.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 23, verse 21:

﴿And indeed, in the livestock there is a lesson for you. We give you to drink from what is in their bellies, and for you in them are many benefits, and from them you eat.﴾

Al-An'am (livestock): it refers to camels and cattle. Water buffalo is added to cattle, and it was not mentioned because it did not exist in the Arab environment. The sheep and goats (al-ghanam) include both sheep (al-day'an) and goats (al-ma'iz). In Surat al-An'am, the Exalted says: ﴿Eight pairs: of sheep two, and of goats two...﴾ [al-An'am: 143].

It is also said: an'am and ni'am (with a fatha on the nun and the 'ayn).

Al-'ibrah (lesson): something by which you take heed and reason to the power of God and the wondrous nature of His creation in the creation of livestock.

But what is the lesson in the creation of these livestock? The Truth, glory be to Him, spoke of the creation of man, that He created him from the choice essence, extract and lineage of clay and of the sperm-drop, and so in all the stages of his creation. And in the livestock you see something of this selection and choosing: the livestock eat from here and from there and gather all kinds of foods, and from this mixture comes out the fargh (digesta), which is foul, its smell unbearable, and the blood of the animal is formed; and between the fargh and the blood, the Creator, Mighty and Majestic, purifies for you pure milk. This too is a lineage and a purification.

The Exalted said: ﴿And indeed, in the livestock there is a lesson for you. We give you to drink from what is in their bellies, from between digesta and blood, pure milk, palatable to the drinkers﴾ [al-Nahl: 66].

We note that the verse before us says ﴿We give you to drink from what is in their bellies﴾ [al-Mu'minun], while the verse of al-Nahl says ﴿We give you to drink from what is in their bellies﴾ [al-Nahl]. That is because we take milk from the female livestock, not from all livestock. So the meaning of ﴿from what is in their bellies﴾ [al-Mu'minun] is: the females among them; and ﴿from what is in their bellies﴾ [al-Nahl] means: the bellies of some of them; and therefore the pronoun returned masculine.

As for His saying ﴿nusqikum﴾ [al-Mu'minun: 21], it is from saqa, and in another place ﴿fa-asqaynakumuhu﴾ [al-Hijr: 22] from the verb asqa. Some say the two are synonyms, but they are not so, because each has its own meaning: saqa means he gave him drink, while asqa means he prepared for him what he drinks until the time he wishes to drink.

Therefore, when the Truth, glory be to Him, spoke of the drink of Paradise, He said: ﴿And they will be adorned with bracelets of silver, and their Lord will give them to drink a pure drink﴾ [al-Insan: 21].

And when He spoke of rainwater He said, glory be to Him: ﴿And We sent the winds fertilizing, and sent down water from the sky, and We gave you to drink of it, and you are not its storers﴾ [al-Hijr: 22]; meaning: He placed it in a reservoir until the time of need for it.

As we said of "murdi'" (with a kasra) and "murda'" (with a fatha): murdi' (with kasra) is the one who is actually nursing, as in His saying ﴿On the day you see it, every nursing mother will forget what she nursed﴾ [al-Hajj: 2]. As for murda' (with fatha), it is one fit for nursing.

Then the Exalted says: ﴿And for you in them are many benefits, and from them you eat﴾ [al-Mu'minun: 21]. We note that the verse of al-Nahl focused on the matter of purifying milk from between digesta and blood, while here it focused on other benefits of livestock. Each verse takes one aspect of the subject and treats it from a particular angle. We clarify this for those who speak of repetition in the Noble Qur'an: verses on one subject are not repetition, but rather a foundation with different snapshots, each snapshot performing in its place a station of admonition and lesson, such that if all these apparent repetitions are gathered, they give you the complete picture of the thing.

The benefits of livestock are many: from them we take wool and fur, and they used to make from it clothing, carpets and tents, before modern clothes and fabrics were known. From woolen garments the name "Sufiyya" was given to those who wear coarse garments; and they now make from wool soft garments like silk, worn by the affluent.

Among the benefits of livestock also are hides, bones and other things. The Exalted says: ﴿And God has made for you from your houses a dwelling, and has made for you from the hides of livestock tents that you find light on the day of your travel and the day of your settling, and from their wool, their fur and their hair, furnishings and provision for a time﴾ [al-Nahl: 80].

﴿And from them you eat﴾ [al-Mu'minun: 21]: meaning, meat. The meat is mentioned at the end of these benefits, because it is the last thing that can be benefited from in the animal. We have previously mentioned that the animal which God has permitted us, when it is exposed to what takes its soul, it raises its neck for you and reveals to you the place of its slaughter, as if it were saying to you: hasten and benefit from me before I die.

In another snapshot of the benefits of livestock, the Exalted says: ﴿And it carries your loads to a land you could not have reached except with great hardship﴾ [al-Nahl: 7]. So every verse that spoke of livestock gives us a benefit, so that you remain connected to the whole Qur'an.

1 - Al-fargh: the digested food in the rumen, changed and foul-smelling. [al-Qamus al-Qawim 2/74].
2 - Al-Farra' said: the Arabs say for everything that comes from the bellies of livestock, or from the sky, or a flowing river, to a people: asqaytu (I gave them to drink). But if he gives you water to quench your thirst, they say saqahu, and do not say asqahu, as the Exalted said: ﴿And their Lord gave them to drink a pure drink﴾ [al-Insan: 21]. And they may say for what is in the bellies of livestock and for rainwater: saqa and asqa. [Lisan al-Arab, root: s-q-y].
3 - Al-zaʿn: moving from one place to another, i.e., travelling. [al-Qamus al-Qawim 1/415].

**Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1–53, fragments of 54–66) on surah 23, verse 22:**

﴿And upon them, and upon the ship, you are carried.﴾ (23:22)

﴿And upon them﴾ (23:22) [al-Mu'minun]: That is, upon the beasts you are carried. We ride the beasts, and we load our goods upon them. But since three-quarters of the earth is water, the Real—glory be to Him and exalted is He—did not leave us on the sea; rather, He also carried us upon it: ﴿and upon the ship you are carried﴾ (23:22) [al-Mu'minun]. Just as He prepared mounts for you on the narrow dry land, so too He prepared for you what you ride on this vast expanse of water.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 23, verse 23:

Since the discussion here concerns the ship (al-fulk), it is fitting that it be followed by mention of one who had a connection with the ship, namely Noah (peace be upon him):

﴿And We certainly sent Noah to his people, and he said: "O my people, worship Allah; you have no deity other than Him. Will you not then fear Him?"﴾ (23)

After the Noble Qur'an has told us of the creation of man and the creation of animals, and has told us of some of His blessings which He bestowed upon us, it moved us on to the craft of shipbuilding. For a questioner may ask: how do these ships come into being, that is, are they created like man and animals through reproduction, or do they grow like crops? So the Creator, glorified be He, made clear that they were discovered through revelation, in His saying, exalted be He: ﴿So We revealed to him, "Build the ship under Our eyes and Our revelation"﴾ [al-Mu'minun] (27).

The meaning of ﴿under Our eyes﴾ [al-Mu'minun] (27) is that it is a precise craft, in which the Truth, glorified be He, did not leave His prophet to do as he pleased; rather He accompanied him, watched over him, and directed him to how it should be built and the materials used in it, as He, glorified be He, said: ﴿And We carried him upon a [vessel] of planks and nails﴾ [al-Qamar] (13). The "nails" (dusur) are the ropes, with which they used to tie the wooden planks and join them to one another, or the nails with which the planks are fastened to one another.

But, however firmly the wooden planks are joined to one another, there must remain between them pores through which water seeps. So how do we avoid that in the building of ships, especially in their primitive stages? They say: the shipbuilder must dry the wood thoroughly before working it; then when the wood meets water, it absorbs it, its volume increases, and it closes these pores completely, so that water does not seep through them.

Among the wonders and miracles of the Qur'an in the matter of ships is His saying:

﴿And His are the ships, running in the sea like mountains﴾ [al-Rahman] (24). That is: like lofty mountains. These ships did not exist at the time the Qur'an was revealed, but God informed of them, which indicates that He, the One who bestowed this blessing upon us, knew what development in shipbuilding man could arrive at, and that they would be lofty and towering like mountains.

Since our discussion concerns ships, it is natural and fitting that we mention Noah (peace be upon him), for he was the first to be guided by revelation to the building of ships. So He, glorified be He, said: ﴿And We certainly sent Noah to his people…﴾ (23) [al-Mu'minun]. When the Truth, glorified be He, spoke of the blessings and benefits in the cattle, which all return—and the world with them—to passing away, He wished to give us a portion of the enduring life and the everlasting bliss that does not pass away, so He mentioned the method of Allah with which Noah was sent, and he was one of the Ulu al-'Azm (the steadfast messengers).

Sending (al-irsal) is that one party commissions another to a recipient. The one who commissions is the Truth, glorified be He; the one commissioned with the message is Noah (peace be upon him); and those to whom he was sent are his people. Allah does not send to a people except when they concern Him, and how could they not, since they are His servants and His creation, and He has made them successors (khala'if) on the earth?

Whoever creates a creature, or makes a craft, must set down a law for its maintenance, so that it may perform its task in life and fulfil its role in the most perfect manner—as we illustrate this, and to Allah belongs the highest likeness, by a manufacturer of a refrigerator or a television who places with it a catalogue containing the operating instructions, the method of maintenance, and how to repair faults.
