Therefore He who created man and made him His successor on the earth is more deserving of this law and more deserving of maintaining His creation. For this reason, He, glorified be He, says in the sacred hadith: "O son of Adam, I created all things for your sake, and I created you for My sake, so do not busy yourself with what is for you in neglect of that for which you were made." That is: since everything is for your sake, working for you and performing its task, you too must perform your task for which you were created.

Thus your Lord has set for you the law of your maintenance: do this and do not do that. You must adhere to the command and carry it out, for it is the secret of beauty in the universe and the secret of happiness and harmony in the movement of life. You must also avoid the prohibition and not approach it, for it leads to ugliness and will expose one of the nakednesses of society. As for matters on which He has been silent, you are free to do or not do them, for these do not bring about ugliness in society; these matters are called the permissible (mubahat), and Allah has left them to your freedom and choice.

When the Truth, blessed and exalted be He, summoned man into this universe, He created for him the requisites of his life: the requisites for sustaining life such as food, drink and air, and for preserving the species through procreation. The law of maintenance has encompassed all these requisites, organising them and specifying what is lawful and what is unlawful. He said: eat this and do not eat that, drink this and do not drink that. If we observe inventors in material matters, we find the maker specifying the requirements of his creation: for example, this device works on 110 volts and this on 220 volts; this machine runs on petrol and this on diesel. If you change these requirements, the machine breaks down and fails to perform its task.

Likewise—and to Allah belongs the highest likeness—you must adhere to the law and method of your Creator, mighty and majestic be He, and not deviate from it, or your condition will be corrupted and you will be unable to perform your task in life. If we wish the succession for which God created us to be upright for us—and it is a succession of reform, not corruption—then we must hold to the law of maintenance which our Creator has set for us, mighty and majestic be He.

Therefore, if you see an obvious nakedness (corruption) in society in any aspect of life, know that it is a natural consequence of departing from the method of Allah and suspending one of His rulings. For example, when you see the poor, the hungry and the needy, know that in the matter there is a suspension of one of the rulings of Allah: either they are idle and do not strive to walk in the earth's pathways, or they are unable, and those who are able have deprived them and monopolised the wealth to themselves.

Some say: if Allah, glorified be He, has forbidden us certain things, why did He create them? They give as examples the pig and wine. The error of these people is that they think everything created is meant to be eaten, and this is not correct, for Allah created these things for a task they perform in life, and it is not necessary that they be eaten. The pig, Allah created it to clean the environment of filth, which is why you do not see it eating anything other than that.

As for wine, it was not created as wine; rather it is the sweet grape which is eaten fresh. Man took it, entered it into this nature, and corrupted it by fermenting it, and so the lawful became unlawful.

Let us return to the saying of Allah, exalted be He: ﴿And We certainly sent Noah to his people…﴾ (23) [al-Mu'minun]. The "qawm" (people) are the men, especially of the society, and not men and women, as is shown by His saying: ﴿O you who have believed, let not a people ridicule another people, perhaps they may be better than them, nor let women ridicule other women, perhaps they may be better than them…﴾ (11) [al-Hujurat]. Thus "women" stands in contrast to "qawm," i.e., men.

From this is the saying of the poet (1): "And I do not know, and I will think I know: is it the people of Hisn (2) or women?"

But did Noah (peace be upon him) send to the men without the women? Noah was sent to everyone, but the word "qawm" is mentioned because they are the ones who will carry the matter of the call with them and travel with it, and convey it to those under their authority among the women; and the men are charged with carrying out the affairs of the building and reform of the universe.

The idafa (genitival construction) in ﴿his people (qawmihi)﴾ (23) [al-Mu'minun] carries the sense of lam (belonging to), meaning: a people belonging to him, because the idafa may come in the sense of min (from), like ardab qamh, meaning "an ardab of wheat"; in the sense of fi (in), like makr al-layl, meaning "the scheming of the night"; and in the sense of lam, like qalam Zayd, meaning "Zayd's pen."

So the meaning here is: a people belonging to him, because he was one of them, trusted by them, and his earlier conduct was known to them; so when he speaks to them they do not accuse him. Thus it is from the mercy of Allah toward creation that He sends to them one of themselves, as He said: ﴿There has certainly come to you a messenger from among yourselves…﴾ (128) [al-Tawbah]. In this there is familiarity and comfort for the people, unlike if the messenger were an angel, for example, when the people would be alienated from him and not at ease with him.

For this reason, the Prophet (ﷺ) was called among his people, even before his mission, "al-Sadiq al-Amin" (the Truthful, the Trustworthy), because his past and conduct were known to them, and the components of his life encouraged them to believe what he brought. And how could they believe him in matters of this world but not believe him in conveying from Allah?

So: ﴿to his people (ila qawmihi)﴾ (23) [al-Mu'minun] means: We did not bring you a messenger of another kind, nor of another tribe, but from among you; you know his past and history, so you are at ease with what he brings and do not take a stance of hostility toward him.

Or the meaning may be: "to a people from him," because they would not be a people capable of managing the affairs of reforming life unless they heard his method; so they are "from him," for they will take from him the method of Allah.

Then He, glorified be He, says: ﴿So he said, "O my people, worship Allah; you have no deity other than Him."﴾ (23) [al-Mu'minun] "O my people" is an expression of endearment and tenderness toward them. "Worship Allah; you have no deity other than Him": worship (ibadah) is the obedience of a worshipper to the command of the one worshipped, and worship entails being charged with commands and prohibitions. So divinity (uluhiyyah) is obligation and worship, while lordship (rububiyyah) is bestowal and nurture. For this reason He, glorified be He, said: ﴿He is your Lord, and to Him you will be returned﴾ [Hud] (34): that is, your Lord collectively—the Lord of the believer and the Lord of the disbeliever, the Lord of the obedient and the Lord of the disobedient.

As we have said: the sun, the moon, the earth, the rain, etc., all serve everyone, with no difference between believer and disbeliever, because that is the bestowal of lordship. And if you ask the denying disbeliever: "Who created you? Who provided for you?", he will have no choice but to say: "Allah." So let these people be shamed by their own conduct, and let them know that He alone, exalted be He, deserves obedience and worship; for the requirements of lordship and belief in it require that we believe in divinity.

Just as a small child grows up between his father and mother and reaches maturity, finding no one other than them to serve him, meet his needs, and supply his requirements, and even to remove harm from him and watch over his comfort—all of this with a happy spirit and a contented, tranquil soul—they may go hungry so that you may be fed, go unclothed so that you may be clothed, and deprive themselves so as to secure for you a dignified life. Then when the child grows up, reaches adulthood and manhood, you find him disobeying them, rebelling against their authority, and friends of evil take him from their embrace and adorn for him rebellion against his father and mother.

To such an undutiful son we say: be ashamed of your own conduct and feel shame. This is not how a kindness is repaid. And where were these friends the day you were small and needed someone to support you, remove harm from you, and watch over your comfort? You ought not to have listened except to one who had done good to you.

This is an example of the Oneness of divinity and the Oneness of lordship—and to Allah belongs the highest likeness. How can you take the bestowal of lordship from your Lord and then rebel against Him in divinity, disobeying His command and denying His blessings? It was incumbent upon you to be faithful to the blessing.

You must know that your Lord, mighty and majestic be He, is trustworthy toward you in the imposition of commands and prohibitions, because you are His servant and His creation; and when you fulfil what is incumbent upon you toward divinity, Allah gains nothing from it; rather its benefit returns to you. And so, if you trace matters of obedience, worship and obligations, you will find that in the end they too return to the bestowal of lordship, for they return to you with benefit.

So we take commands and prohibitions as obligations and burdens required by faith in divinity; we say: yes, they are obligations from Allah, but for your own good. If you were fair, you would find divinity to be of lordship. When, for instance, the drinking of wine is forbidden to you, and this protects you from the corruption of the mind—does He, glorified be He, gain anything from that?

For this reason He, exalted be He, says about these people: ﴿And if you asked them who created the heavens and the earth, they would surely say, "Allah."﴾ (25) [Luqman].

And He says: ﴿And if you asked them who created them, they would surely say, "Allah."﴾ (87) [al-Zukhruf].

Since He, glorified be He, is your Creator and your Provider and the Creator of the heavens and the earth, why do you disobey Him? Has your disobedience diminished anything of His dominion? Has the obedience of the obedient added anything to His dominion? Has the obedience of the obedient added to the dominion of Allah any earth or heaven, or sun or moon?

Before He created you, the Truth, glorified be He, created for you, through the attributes of perfection that are His, all the requisites of your life, and summoned you into a universe prepared for your reception and your livelihood. Therefore your Lord, mighty and majestic be He, is neither benefited by obedience nor harmed by disobedience.

For this reason He says in the sacred hadith: "O My servants, if the first of you and the last of you, your humans and your jinn, were as...

1 - He is Zuhayr ibn Abi Sulma, the poet-sage of the pre-Islamic era. His father, his maternal uncle, his sister Sulma, and his two sons Ka'b and Bujayr, and his sister al-Khansa', were all poets. He was born in the land of Muzayna in the vicinity of Madina; among his most famous poems is his mu'allaqa. He died in the year 13 BH. [al-A'lam of al-Zirikli 3/52].
2 - He means: Hisn ibn Hudhayfa al-Fazari. Said by Ibn Manzur in [Lisan al-Arab, entry: hisn].

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi (surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66)) on surah 23, verse 24:

Then the Truthful (al-Haqq) subhanahu says:

﴿Then said the chiefs (al-mala') of those who disbelieved among his people: "This is no more than a human being like yourselves, who wants to make himself superior over you. And if Allah had willed, He would have sent down angels. We never heard of this among our forefathers of old."﴾ (24)

Al-mala': from al-mal', meaning that which fills a thing. Al-mala' are those who fill the eyes with their nobility, their station, their greatness and their dignity. From this is the saying: "So-and-so is a filler of the eye" (malu' al-ayn), or "a filler of the hearing and sight." They say of a man who has reached a high degree of beauty: "So-and-so is fixed upon the eyes (qid al-uyun)," meaning that when you see him you do not turn your gaze to anything else, because of his intense beauty, as if he had fixed your gaze upon himself. On the other hand, they say: "So-and-so is overlooked by the eye, and you do not see him, as if he did not exist."

So al-mala' are those who fill the seats of assemblies with dignity, grandeur, prominence and leadership. But why are these particular people the ones who became fanatically opposed to him and confronted him?

They say: Because the methodology (manhaj) of Allah came only to reform what had become corrupt in the universe and what evil had spread within it. Allah, blessed and exalted, sends down a methodology upon the tongue of a first messenger, and asks his people to convey the methodology of their messenger after him. But heedlessness comes upon this methodology, so people deviate from it, and their deviation from the methodology of their Lord takes several forms:

Among them is one who deviates from the methodology of his Lord and commits sin, but then he returns to himself, reviews it, blames it, and soon repents and feels remorse. His restrainer is from within himself and his admonisher is from inside him. These are the ones who mixed good deeds with other, evil ones.

Among them is one who deviates from the methodology of his Lord in a deviation that has no return and no restraint. We call this in our language "faqid" (one who has lost it), meaning that no restrainer from the law or from conscience remains for him. Then there remains the restraint of society: when it sees such deviants from the methodology of truth, it must confront them, shun them, and not show them affection or respect. Otherwise, if the deviant and the perpetrator of abominations remain in the same state of being respected and esteemed by people, and remain in their station in society, he will persist in his error and be extravagant against himself and against his society. Thus evil spreads within society, corruption becomes general, and chaos becomes widespread.

Do you not see that the wise Law, when it made the blood-money for manslaughter fall upon the 'aqilah, meaning the family of the killer, and not upon the killer alone? Why? So that they may restrain their son if he deviates or if signs of aggression appear in him, because they will all bear this responsibility together.

We say: al-mala' were singled out in particular because they are the ones who profit from evil and corruption in society, and it is in their interest that this situation continue, so that their worldly authority and station remain. Therefore they are the first to meet the messages with denial and rejection. Did not the Truthful, subhanahu, say about them in another verse: ﴿We see you only as a human being like us, and we see none following you except those who are the lowest of us...﴾ (27) [Hud].

Those whom they call the lowest are the oppressed, the poor, the crushed, and those concerned with the affairs of creation, religion and values. As soon as their ears hear of a message, they long for it and throw themselves into its embrace, because it came to rescue them. Therefore they are the first to believe. And if the methodology came to deliver justice to these people, it also came to strip from the holders of power, tyranny and arrogance their authority and their instruction, so they must confront it and oppose it.

As for the meaning of: ﴿those who disbelieved among his people...﴾ (24) [al-Mu'minun]: "disbelieved" means they denied the existence of Allah. ﴿This is no more than a human being like yourselves﴾ (24) [al-Mu'minun]: the first thing that turned them away from the Messenger was that he was a human being. So, then, what were you expecting? This meaning is explained in His saying: ﴿And nothing prevented the people from believing when guidance came to them except that they said: "Has Allah sent a human being as a messenger?"﴾ (94) [al-Isra'].

It is necessary that the messenger be of the same kind as those to whom he is sent, so that he may be a model (uswah), that they may imitate him and be guided by him. Otherwise, if a messenger came as an angel, how would the exemplary model be realized in him? And how would you obey him when you know he is an angel who does not eat, drink or reproduce, has no desire, and lacks the means of disobedience?

Let us suppose that Allah sent down an angel to you: how would you see him and receive from him? It is necessary, then, that he come to you in the form of a man, so that you may be able to see him and receive from him. Thus we return in the discussion of this matter to his being a man. Therefore He, subhanahu, said: ﴿And if We had made him an angel, We would have made him a man, and We would have covered for them what they cover.﴾ (9) [al-An'am], and the doubt remains.

So: it is foolishness to say that the messenger should be an angel.

As for their saying: ﴿a human being like yourselves﴾ (24) [al-Mu'minun]: yes, he is a human being, but not like you. You are lying in this likeness, because he is a human being whom Allah chose by revelation. Therefore the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Something is taken from me and I say: 'I am only a human being like you,' and something is given to me from Allah and I say: 'I am not like any of you.'"

And the Most High says to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ): ﴿Say: I am only a human being like you; it is revealed to me that your God is one God.﴾ (6) [Fussilat]. Hence the superiority lies in his being a human being to whom revelation is sent, and his humanity is only for intimacy and familiarity.

Then the Truthful, subhanahu, continues the saying of these disbelievers from the people of Nuh: ﴿who wants to make himself superior over you﴾ (24) [al-Mu'minun]. "Yatafaddal" means he ascribes to himself virtue, nobility and leadership, so that he may be followed while they are followers. ﴿And if Allah had willed﴾ (24) [al-Mu'minun]: that is, if He had willed to send a messenger, ﴿He would have sent down angels﴾ (24) [al-Mu'minun]: that is, messengers. Allah the Most High has refuted this saying of theirs, and said, blessed and exalted is He: ﴿Say: If there were in the earth angels walking securely, We would have sent down upon them from the heaven an angel as a messenger.﴾ (95) [al-Isra'].

Then they say: ﴿We never heard of this among our forefathers of old﴾ (24) [al-Mu'minun]: what is meant by "this" is that someone should come and say: worship Allah, you have no god other than Him, because our forefathers of old worshipped idols, and no one came to say this word to us as Nuh did.

This is evidence that they are imitators of their fathers, with no thought or independence of judgment by which they look at things with the gaze of truth and justice. In another place the Most High said of them: ﴿Indeed we found our fathers upon a community (ummah)(1), and indeed we are following in their footsteps.﴾ (23) [al-Zukhruf].

If we reflect on the condition of societies, including our own society in which we live, it becomes clear to us that these people were lying in their claim of imitating their fathers. How? Consider the condition of the different generations: you find that each generation has its own opinion, aspirations and desires, which may differ between the son and his father. Young people now have independent opinions: a boy chooses, for example, the college he likes and the clothes he loves, even if this contradicts his father's opinion. It may even reach the point of accusing fathers of rigidity and backwardness if the matter requires it, and this exists in every generation.

So: why did you not say in such matters: "Indeed we found our fathers upon a community"? Why did you have individuality and independent opinion in worldly affairs but not in matters of religion? You adopt individuality in whatever satisfies your desires, appetites and deviations, and you adopt imitation in whatever lessens your obligation, because obligation would restrict these desires and appetites and put an end to these deviations. Therefore these people rebel against the methodology of Allah.

Therefore we are astonished at what we see and hear of the condition of our children today, and how the reins have slipped from fathers and mothers. The young man goes his own way in deviant matters; if his father directs him, he turns away from him and accuses him of belonging to an old generation whose time has gone without return. The matter has passed from the sons to the daughters, who have also become rebellious against these values and no longer care for them.

As for their saying: ﴿We never heard of this among our forefathers of old﴾ (24) [al-Mu'minun], and their saying: ﴿Indeed we found our fathers upon a community﴾ (23) [al-Zukhruf]: they are also lying in this statement, because if they were truthful they would have imitated them in everything, in what is for them and against them, in matters of the world and in matters of religion, values and morals.

Therefore the Truthful, blessed and exalted, addresses this issue in several places in His noble Book, and by different methods, among them His saying, subhanahu: ﴿And when it is said to them: "Follow what Allah has sent down," they say: "No, we follow what we found our fathers upon..."﴾ (170) [al-Baqarah].

Because this relieves them from the hardship of obligations. Worship is the obedience of a worshipper to a worshipped one in his commands and prohibitions. How easy it is to worship idols, for they are gods, as they claim, but they have no methodology and no obligations with them. By what did the idol command you? From what did it forbid you? What reward did it prepare for whoever obeyed it? What punishment did it prepare for whoever disobeyed it? So: a worshipped one without methodology and without obligations. This is evidence of their lying in worshipping idols and their other gods.

Did they not say: ﴿We do not worship them except that they bring us near to Allah in position﴾ (3) [al-Zumar]? This is foolishness, ignorance and folly, because logically the statement does not hold: how do you say we worship them when they have no methodology and no obligations, while worship is the obedience of a worshipper to a worshipped one?

So it is nothing but emptiness and doctrinal bankruptcy. Therefore the Truthful, blessed and exalted, answers them, saying: ﴿Or even if their fathers did not understand anything and were not guided?﴾ (170) [al-Baqarah].

In another place He, subhanahu wa ta'ala, says about them: ﴿They said: "Sufficient for us is what we found our fathers upon..."﴾ (104) [al-Ma'idah]. This is more emphatic than the previous one, because they escalate their disbelief and insist upon it. Their saying: ﴿Rather we follow what we found our fathers upon﴾ (170) [al-Baqarah] leaves room that they might reconsider themselves and be guided to the truth and oppose the fathers. But here: ﴿Sufficient for us﴾ (104) [al-Ma'idah] means: it suffices us, and we will not change it or turn away from it. So each verse is concluded with what suits it: in the first He said, refuting them: ﴿Or even if their fathers did not understand anything﴾ (170) [al-Baqarah], and in the other He said, refuting them: ﴿Or even if their fathers did not know anything...﴾ (104) [al-Ma'idah].

Intellect ('aql) is mentioned in the first because a person deliberates within himself through it, and knowledge ('ilm) is mentioned in the other because a person deliberates through his knowledge, and knowledge is also an intellect. So knowledge is broader than intellect. Therefore He mentioned it with their saying ﴿Sufficient for us﴾ (104) [al-Ma'idah], which indicates exaggeration and persistence in disbelief.

We also observe about them in their saying: ﴿We never heard of this﴾ (24) [al-Mu'minun] that heedlessness had become entrenched in them, because Nuh, peace be upon him, is the fifth grandfather after Adam, peace be upon him. Between them there is a long period. How is it that they had not heard during all this time of any messenger or prophet who says: worship Allah, you have no god other than Him?

1 - Ibn 'Abbas said: "i.e., a religion (din)." In his answer to the questions of Nafi' ibn al-Azraq, he said: "upon a creed other than the creed to which you call us." [Both cited by al-Suyuti in al-Durr al-Manthur 7/372; he attributed the first to Ibn Jarir al-Tabari and the second to al-Tastuti.]

Tafsir al-Sha'rawi (surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 23, verse 25:

﴿It is only a man who has madness in him, so wait for him for a while.﴾ (23:25)

﴿Inna huwa..﴾ (23:25): meaning: he is not [anything but]. And ﴿jinnah﴾ means jinn (madness), which is the veiling of the intellect that governs a person's movement in life, so that he proceeds according to its regulations ("do this" and "do not do that"). As for the madman, he acts on whatever occurs to him without presenting his actions to the intellect or to reflection. Therefore, it is from God's justice toward His creation that we do not hold the madman to account for his conduct when he assaults one of us with insults or blows, for example; we can only smile at him and pray that God spares us from what He has afflicted him with.

If this is the condition of the madman in the movement of his life, then would one whose character proceeds according to the laws of life, and is governed by systems and moral values, be a madman? It is strange that this accusation of madness continues on the tongues of those who deny the messengers in every time and place. It was levelled at the Messenger of God (ﷺ), and God refuted them and negated this attribute from His Messenger in His saying: ﴿Nun. By the pen and what they inscribe. You are not, by the grace of your Lord, a madman. And indeed, for you is a reward never cut off. And indeed, you are of a great moral character.﴾ (68:1-4)

How then could one of [such] character be a madman? And even if the Prophet (ﷺ) were mad, why would they have entrusted him with their deposits and precious possessions, been reassured by him, and named him "the Truthful, the Trustworthy"? They did not do that except because they knew his character, and that he is governed by values of truth and goodness that do not waver.

Since the matter is no more than [an accusation that he is] a man with madness in him, ﴿so wait for him for a while﴾ (23:25): that is, wait and leave him to himself. Perhaps he will return to his right mind and abandon this matter of his own accord when he sees us turning away from him and paying him no heed. Or leave him: if he is upon the truth and God supports him and makes his affair manifest, then we will follow him; and if it is the other way, then here we are, turned away from him from the very beginning.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 23, verse 26:

﴿قال رب انصرني بما كذبون ( ٢٦ )﴾ :

After his people denied him, he called upon God to grant him victory, ﴿by what they denied﴾ [al-Mu'minun 23:26]. That is: grant me victory because of their denial, and make their denial have no meaning, so that I triumph over them despite their denial. Or: O Lord, compensate me for their denial with victory; that is, replace their denial with victory for me, just as you say: "I bought such-and-such for such-and-such," so you take this in exchange for that.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 23, verse 27:

Then the Truth, glorified and exalted is He, says:

﴿So We revealed to him, "Build the ark under Our eyes and by Our revelation. Then when Our command comes and the oven gushes forth,(1) load into it of every kind two mates, and your family, except those against whom the word has already gone forth. And do not address Me concerning those who have wronged; indeed, they are to be drowned."﴾ (23:27):

Allah, the Exalted, answered the supplication of His Prophet Nuh, peace be upon him, for victory over his people, so He commanded him to build the ark (al-fulk). Al-Fulk is the ship, and it is used for both the singular and the plural. Allah, the Exalted, says: ﴿Then We saved him and those with him in the laden ship﴾ (26:119) [al-Shu'ara'], and He says: ﴿And you see the ships therein plowing through [the water], that you may seek of His bounty and perhaps you will be grateful﴾ (35:12) [Fatir]. So it indicates the singular once and the plural another time.

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿under Our eyes and by Our revelation﴾ (23:27) [al-Mu'minun] is evidence that Nuh, peace be upon him, was not a carpenter as some claim; for if he had been a carpenter, his intellect would have guided him to the craft of it. Rather, he built it by revelation from Allah, under His direction and care, as He, glorified is He, said: ﴿And that you may be raised under My eye﴾ (20:39) [Ta-Ha]. The meaning is: Build the ark, and I will enable you to build it, guide you to what it must be, and correct you if you err in placing something in other than its proper place. So: You are commanded, assisted, and followed. And revelation (al-wahy) is Allah's speech to His Messenger in concealment.

Then He, the Exalted, says: ﴿Then when Our command comes and the oven gushes forth﴾ (23:27) [al-Mu'minun]. Here the context does not address the period during which Nuh built the ark, which is mentioned in His saying: ﴿And he was constructing the ark, and whenever a company of his people passed by him, they ridiculed him. He said, "If you ridicule us, indeed we ridicule you just as you ridicule"﴾ (11:38) [Hud]. That is because they did not know anything about the reason for building it.

In another place, He, glorified and exalted, teaches us how it was built, saying: ﴿And We carried him upon one of planks and nails(13)﴾ (54:13) [al-Qamar]. We have said: al-Dusur are the ropes with which the wooden planks are bound to one another, on condition that they are dry, and they are joined together with wisdom, so that when water descends and they soak in it, their size increases and they seal the gaps between the planks, just as we see them, for example, making oil barrels from wooden strips.

One of them built a ship of papyrus in this manner, sailed with it to America, and used ropes instead of nails.

Then He, glorified is He, says: ﴿Then when Our command comes...﴾ (23:27) [al-Mu'minun], meaning: by the saving of those who believe in you and the destruction of the deniers. ﴿And the oven gushes forth﴾ (23:27) [al-Mu'minun]. Al-Tannur is the oven in which they bake bread. It is said that it was inherited by Nuh from the days of Adam, and it gushes with water, meaning: water comes out of it, though it was originally a place for fire, so water comes out of it as if it were boiling. But will all the water come out of the oven? The water will come out from all parts of the earth and will descend from the sky; the gushing of the oven is a signal that this process has begun and is its beginning.

When this happens, ﴿load into it of every kind two mates﴾ (23:27) [al-Mu'minun], meaning: carry and admit into it two mates, male and female, of every kind of creature, as in His saying: ﴿What has brought you into Saqar?﴾ (74:42) [al-Muddaththir], meaning: what has admitted you. And He, glorified is He, says: ﴿Put your hand into your pocket﴾ (28:32) [al-Qasas], meaning: insert it. And He, glorified is He, says: ﴿Thus We let it enter into the hearts of the criminals﴾ (15:12) [al-Hijr].

From the root (s-l-k) we take our linguistic usages. We say: "salaka al-masurah" or "al-ayn", meaning: he inserted into it something that removes its blockage.

The tanwin in ﴿of every kind two mates﴾ (23:27) [al-Mu'minun] means: of every thing whose type we want to preserve and continue, because the flood will drown everything, and the Truth, blessed and exalted is He, wants to preserve for His believing servants the foundations of their life and what serves them of animals, livestock, and all other kinds of creatures, of whatever gives birth or lays eggs.

The meaning of ﴿two mates﴾ (23:27) [al-Mu'minun] is not, as some think, that zawj means two; rather, zawj means an individual together with its like. From it is His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Eight mates: two of the sheep and two of the goats. Say, "Has He forbidden the two males or the two females, or what the wombs of the two females contain? Inform me with knowledge, if you are truthful." And two of the camels and two of the cattle...﴾ (6:143-144) [al-An'am].

So He named each individual of these eight a zawj, because with it is its like.

This applies to all creatures. As for humans, He did not say "two mates" but said: ﴿and your family﴾ (23:27) [al-Mu'minun], whatever their kind and number. But is the "family" here a family of kinship or a family of faith?

The family here is intended to mean the family of faith and following, as evidenced by the fact that Allah, the Exalted, explained this point in another verse, saying on the tongue of Nuh, peace be upon him: ﴿He said, "My Lord, indeed my son is of my family..."﴾ (11:45) [Hud].

His Lord said to him: ﴿Indeed, he is not of your family; indeed, he is one whose work was other than righteous﴾ (11:46) [Hud].

So the sonship of the prophets is sonship of deed and following; if it comes from his loins, welcome and well; and if it comes from others, welcome and well. Therefore the Prophet (ﷺ) said about Salman al-Farisi: "Salman is one of us, the Family of the House" (3). He surpassed being a Muslim until he became one of the Family of the House.

Likewise, include in it your family of kinship, as evidenced by His exception of some of them: ﴿except those against whom the word has already gone forth﴾ (23:27) [al-Mu'minun]. He had two wives: one disbelieved in him and betrayed him, she and her son Kan'an. This is mentioned in Allah's saying in Surat al-Tahrim: ﴿Allah presents an example for those who disbelieve: the wife of Nuh and the wife of Lut. They were under two of Our righteous servants but betrayed them...﴾ (66:10) [al-Tahrim].

And Kan'an is the one who said: "I will take refuge in a mountain that will protect me from the water." This incident is not mentioned here, because the events of this story came in scattered form in several places, such that if they were gathered they would give the general picture of the story. If you say: why did it not come all at once, as in the story of Yusuf, peace be upon him?

We say: the story of Yusuf came complete in one place, to give us through it the Truth, glorified and exalted is He, as a model of the complete, well-woven story, which shows His power, exalted is He, to bring the story at once for whoever wishes that. If you want it complete, We are able to do so, and here is the story of Yusuf. The purpose of the stories in the Qur'an, however, is to strengthen the heart of the Prophet (ﷺ), as He said: ﴿Thus, that We may strengthen thereby your heart; and We have spoken it in gradual recitation﴾ (25:32) [al-Furqan], because he (ﷺ) would encounter situations of denial, enmity, and obstinacy from his people, and would face severe crises and need something to console and strengthen him before these events.

Therefore the pieces of the Qur'anic stories came scattered in several places to console the Messenger of Allah and to lighten his burden whenever he faced one of these situations; and by gathering these scattered pieces, the complete, well-ordered story takes shape for you.

Nuh brought with him his other wife, the believing one, and his sons: Sam, Ham, and Yafith, and their wives. These are six, and Nuh and his wife make eight, and with them are seventy-two of the believers, and the roots of faith remaining with Nuh, peace be upon him.

Since the judgment of drowning for those of his family who disbelieved was a matter not open to reconsideration, He, the Exalted, said after it: ﴿And do not address Me concerning those who have wronged; indeed, they are to be drowned﴾ (11:37) [Hud]. But who are "those who have wronged"? They wronged themselves when they disbelieved in Allah. And the Truth, glorified is He, says: ﴿Indeed, association [with Allah] is a great injustice﴾ (31:13) [Luqman].

It is true that when you disbelieve, you take the right of Allah, that He is One, the Eternal, existing, and a God with no worshipped one besides Him, and you give it to other than Him. But this wrong did not harm Allah in anything; it harmed you, and you wronged yourself by it. The utmost folly and foolishness is for a person to wrong himself.

1 - Al-tannur: the place where water gushes forth, and the oven in which one bakes. His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And the oven gushed forth (23:27)﴾ [al-Mu'minun] means: the earth burst forth with abundant water, or burst forth with water resembling the boiling of fire in the oven. [al-Qamus al-Qawim 1/102].
2 - Al-Hasan al-Basri said: Nuh did not carry in the ship except what gives birth or lays eggs. As for bedbugs, flies, and worms, he carried none of them, for they came out of the mud. Cited by al-Qurtubi in his tafsir [6/4653].
3 - Narrated by al-Hakim in his Mustadrak (3/598) from the hadith of Amr ibn Awf al-Muzani. al-Dhahabi and al-Ajluni in Kashf al-Khafa (1/558) said: its chain is weak.
4 - Ibn Kathir said in his tafsir (2/446): "His saying, ﴿And Nuh called his son... (11:42)﴾ [Hud]: this is the fourth son, and his name was Yam."

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 23, verse 28:

Then the Truthful (al-Haqq) (subhanahu) says:

﴿So when you and those with you have settled upon the ship, say: "All praise is for Allah, who has delivered us from the wrongdoing people."﴾ (28)

﴿Settled (istawayta) (28)﴾ [al-Mu'minun]: meaning: you have risen high and mounted, you and those with you, upon the ship, and your heart has become at rest concerning the salvation of the believers with you. ﴿Then say: "All praise is for Allah" (28)﴾ [al-Mu'minun]: The believer must receive Allah's blessings upon him with praise, and must not let the blessing make him forget the majesty of the Bestower. So the moment the matter becomes settled for you upon the ship and you are at ease, hasten to praise Allah.

In another place He (subhanahu) says: ﴿And when harm touches man, he calls upon Us, lying on his side, or sitting or standing. But when We remove his harm from him, he continues on as if he had never called upon Us for a harm that touched him. Thus is made attractive to the transgressors what they were doing.﴾ (12) [Yunus].

It is as if the Truthful (al-Haqq), may He be blessed and exalted, gives us immunity and makes for us an example in His own Self, subhanahu, so that when we are confronted with ingratitude from one to whom we have shown kindness, we do not become angry, because people deny favours even towards Allah, Mighty and Majestic.

Therefore, when Musa (peace be upon him) said: "O Lord, I ask You that it not be said about me what is not in me," meaning: that people not accuse me of wrongdoing unjustly, his Lord, Mighty and Majestic, replied: "O Musa, how [could they], when I did not do that for myself."

So this is a matter that no one should expect otherwise. Had every doer of good withheld his goodness from people because they deny it, the affairs would have been corrupted, the interests among creatures would have halted, and the people of goodness would have withheld their goodness. Therefore our Lord, Mighty and Majestic, placed for us the example in Himself, subhanahu.

And if a person is base, he does not stop at denying favour, but goes further, hating the one who has done him good and harbouring resentment against him. That is because man is created with love of self, self-exaltation and arrogance. So when he sees the one who has done him good, he hates him, because that one humbles the pride of his self and restricts his haughtiness.

From here they said: "Beware the evil of the one to whom you have done good." Why? Because he feels disgraced the moment he sees you, while he wants to be exalted, and your presence breaks that exaltation within him.

So: prepare yourself for the fact that goodness may be denied even if its doer is the Lord of Might, subhanahu, so let it not grieve you that your own favour is denied.

On this the poet said:
"Those in need walk behind you, humbled;
if they reach what they sought, they turn against you and rush away.
The best of them is one who, when mentioned in something, stops and does not deny, though he may exaggerate.
So do not abandon kindness, however they deny it,
for the reward of Allah is greater and more abundant."

The meaning is: when you and those with you have settled and the matter is secure for you upon the ship, beware lest you become deluded or turn aside and forget to praise Allah for this blessing. That is why we were commanded, whenever we mount any vessel, to say: "In the name of Allah be its course and its anchoring," because you did not make it run by your skill and strength, but by the name of Allah who inspired, by the name of Allah who helped, by the name of Allah who granted success to me and watched over me with His eye. As long as you remember the Bestower at the time of the blessing and acknowledge the owner of the favour for his favour, He preserves it for you.

As for denying it to its owner and attributing it to yourself, like the one who said: ﴿"I have only been given it on knowledge I possess."﴾ (78) [al-Qasas], then He says: since the matter is so, guard it yourself.

Even in mounting an animal, the Prophet (ﷺ) taught us to say: "Glory be to Him who has subjected this to us, and we were not capable of it, and to our Lord we are surely returning." (2)

And His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿who has delivered us from the wrongdoing people (28)﴾ [al-Mu'minun]: the mention of deliverance is because averting harm takes precedence over securing benefit.

1 - From the saying of the Shaykh, may Allah have mercy on him.
2 - Muslim recorded in his Sahih (1342), Book of Hajj, from the hadith of Ibn 'Umar, may Allah be pleased with them both, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) when he mounted his camel setting out on a journey, would say "Allahu akbar" three times, then say: "Glory be to Him who has subjected this to us, and we were not capable of it, and to our Lord we are surely returning." Ahmad also recorded it in his Musnad (2/144, 150).

Then his Lord will teach him another supplication, which he makes when the ship comes to rest on al-Judi, and when he disembarks to begin his new life on the earth:

﴿And say: "My Lord, cause me to disembark at a blessed place, and You are the best of those who bring to land."﴾ (23:29)

In another place He, glory be to Him, said: ﴿It was said: "O Noah, descend with peace from Us and blessings upon you and upon nations from those with you..."﴾ (11:48) [Hud], because you will disembark from it, and it is not the place of your living.

Likewise the Prophet (ﷺ) supplicated, saying, as the Qur'an relates: ﴿And say: "My Lord, cause me to enter a sincere entrance and cause me to exit a sincere exit..."﴾ (17:80) [al-Isra'].

It is necessary that you mention the Bestower of the blessing in the blessing bestowed upon you. Therefore, those who are struck by the evil eye of envious people in the blessings of Allah upon them—be fully certain that when they saw the blessing of Allah upon them, they did not mention the One who bestowed it. Had a person, upon seeing a blessing of Allah upon him in his wealth or his children, said: "Mā shā' Allāh, lā quwwata illā billāh" (What Allah wills; there is no power except through Allah), and placed the blessing under the protection of its Bestower, he would have guaranteed the continuation of his blessing and its safety from the eyes of the envious, because he would have placed it under the law of divine preservation.

As for the meaning of ﴿a blessed place...﴾ (23:29) [al-Mu'minun]: the blessed thing is that which gives beyond what its size would suggest. For example, a person may live a dignified life on a modest salary and raise his children in the best upbringing, so people ask: "From where does he have that?" We say: it is the blessing (barakah) that descends upon the little so that it becomes much. It is true that the income is small, but its smallness of expenditure makes it abundant.

We have illustrated this with a person who earns his livelihood from what is lawful, whom Allah makes his affairs easy and settles his needs at the least cost. If his child falls ill, for example, Allah cures him with an aspirin tablet and a cup of tea, and he is not alarmed by the illness, because his heart is at rest, his soul content, and he trusts in Allah's help. But the one who earns from what is unlawful and takes bribes, etc.—if his child falls ill, he rushes him to the doctors and expects the most dangerous diseases for his child; and if he takes a bribe of ten, he spends a hundred on it.

We have said before that this blessing is the provision of subtraction, which does not increase your income but reduces your expenses.

As for the phrase ﴿and You are the best of those who bring to land﴾ (23:29) [al-Mu'minun]: Is He the only one who causes to land? The meaning of "Allah is the best of those who cause to land" is: He permitted that the servant also be called one who causes to land when he settles a person in a comfortable place, such as lodging him, for example, in a comfortable apartment, or receiving him as a guest, etc. And if you are a "one who causes to land" in this sense, then Allah, mighty and majestic, is the best of those who cause to land, because when He settles you, He settles you according to His measure, glory be to Him, and according to the measure of His generosity and bounty.

Thus: the Truth, blessed and exalted is He, did not withhold from His creatures that He describe them with what He described Himself with. He did not withhold from you that He describe you with creating, so He said: ﴿So blessed is Allah, the best of creators﴾ (23:14) [al-Mu'minun]. He affirmed for you the attribute of creating, because you bring into existence what was non-existent, although you bring it into being from something that exists by Allah's creation—for example, you make a glass cup from sand and fire—but what you bring into being remains inert in its state, does not grow or reproduce, and has no life in it. Yet your Lord named you a creator. Likewise He said: ﴿the best of inheritors﴾ (21:89) [al-Anbiya'], and He said: ﴿the best of schemers﴾ (3:54) [Al 'Imran].

Just as Allah, mighty and majestic, did not withhold these attributes from you, so do not withhold from Him, glory be to Him, that He is the best of those who cause to land, the best of inheritors, the best of schemers, and the best of creators.

Then the Truth, glory be to Him, says:

﴿Indeed in that are signs, and indeed We are ever testing.﴾ (30)

﴿And in that..﴾ (30) [al-Mu'minun]: meaning: in what has preceded. ﴿Signs..﴾ (30) [al-Mu'minun]: lessons, admonitions and wonders, which, if a person reflects upon them with a neutral intellect, will lead him to good. ﴿And indeed We are ever testing﴾ (30) [al-Mu'minun]: So do not think that trial is restricted to the wrongdoers and disbelievers whom God seized and destroyed, for trial may befall those who do not deserve it. When God tests the people of goodness and righteousness, it is only so that their reward may increase, their rank may be raised, and their faith may be purified.

Among these are the trials that befell the first Muslims. They were not out of dislike for them or as vengeance against them; rather, they were a refining of their essence and a manifestation of their firm faith, which cannot be shaken, because they would bear the call of God until the Hour arrives, so there must be their testing and refining.

As He, glory be to Him, said: ﴿Do people think that they will be left to say, "We believe," and they will not be tried?﴾ (2) [al-'Ankabut]. No indeed; there must be a trial that distinguishes the truthful from those who worship God on an edge (ḥarf). Those must inevitably fall away from the procession of the call, and there remain only the believers, firm in their faith, whom events do not shake.

Therefore, the meaning of ﴿And indeed We are ever testing﴾ (30) [al-Mu'minun] is: the people of faith who do not deserve punishment, because We wish to raise their degrees and purify their faith so that they may be fit for the call of God. For this reason the Truth, blessed and exalted is He, says in the sacred hadith:

"By My might and My majesty, I do not take My servant out of this world when I have intended good for him until I have repaid him for what he did of evil deeds: illness in his body, loss in his wealth, and loss of his children. But if a sin remains upon him, the agonies of death are made heavy upon him until he comes to Me as on the day his mother bore him... And by My might and My majesty, I do not take My servant out of this world when I have intended evil for him until I have repaid him for what he did of good deeds: health in his body, and blessing in his wealth and children. But if a good deed remains for him, I lighten the agonies of death for him until he comes to Me with no good deed at all."

Therefore, trial, just as it may be vengeance against the disbelievers and wrongdoers, is also a means of educating the believer toward benefit, a purification of faith, and a desire for reward.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 23, verse 31:

Then the Truthful, glorified is He, says:

﴿Then We produced after them another generation (qarn).﴾ (31)

That is: after the people of Noah, peace be upon him. We have said that the qarn is the period of time that gathers people who are close to one another in the affairs of life. The scholars have concluded that a qarn is a hundred years, or a king's reign however long it lasts, or a prophetic mission however long it lasts; all of these are called a qarn (1).

1 - Al-Azhari (al-Azhari) said: The qarn is the people of any period in which there was a prophet or in which there was a class of people of knowledge, whether the years were few or many. The evidence for this is the saying of the Prophet (ﷺ): "The best of you is my qarn (generation), meaning my companions; then those who follow them, meaning the Successors (tabi'un); then those who follow them, meaning those who took from the Successors." Al-Qurtubi said in his commentary on the verse (6/4654): "They are the people of 'Ad, and the Messenger is Hud, for no nation was produced after the people of Noah except 'Ad..."

Then the Truthful, Glorified be He, says:

﴿Then We sent among them a Messenger from themselves, [saying]: "Worship Allah; you have no god other than Him. Will you not then fear Him?"﴾ (23:32)

After the people of Noah came the people of 'Ad, to whom Allah sent our master Hud (peace be upon him), as stated in His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿And to 'Ad [We sent] their brother Hud...﴾ (7:65). He called them with the very same call as Noah: ﴿Worship Allah; you have no god other than Him...﴾ (23:32), and he also said to them: ﴿Will you not then fear Him?﴾ (23:32).

So, this is a single method common to all the divine messages, as He, Glorified be He, said: ﴿He has ordained for you of religion that which He enjoined upon Noah, and that which We have revealed to you, and that which We enjoined upon Abraham, Moses and Jesus: "Establish the religion and do not be divided therein..."﴾ (42:13).

The religion of Allah is one, brought by all the messengers and prophets. If you say: then what is the meaning of His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿For each of you We have appointed a law (shir'ah) and a clear way (minhaj)...﴾ (5:48)?

We say: Yes. The creed and the fundamentals are the constant elements that do not change: "Worship Allah; you have no god other than Him." As for the method (minhaj) and the specific law (shari'ah) concerning the branches (furu'), these are subject to change between the messengers, because they concern the movement of life, and the Truthful, Blessed and Exalted, gives each environment, through the tongue of its messenger, what suits it and what treats its diseases and ailments.

The shir'ah is the law that governs the movement of your life, whereas the din (religion) is the fixed and unified matter established by Allah, Mighty and Majestic, which no one has the right to alter by a single letter.

Therefore, the bane of nations has been that they made themselves into separate groups and divided parties, and these are the ones of whom Allah said: ﴿Indeed, those who divided their religion and became sects, you are not [associated] with them in anything...﴾ (6:159).

Reflect on: ﴿divided their religion...﴾ (6:159). He did not say "divided their law or their method", because the religion is one with Allah, whereas methods and laws are the sphere of difference according to the diseases present in each nation. These groups worshipped idols, those cheated in measure and weight, and those denied the blessings of Allah, and so on.

We had previously explained that the difference in diseases among these nations resulted from the isolation that kept them apart, so that this one did not know about that one while they were in the same era. But in the message of Islam, this general final message, it came at an appointed time of the meeting of nations and the connection of civilizations, so that what happens in the farthest north is known to those in the farthest south. Therefore the diseases became unified, and one final Messenger came with a legislation suitable for all times and all places, until the Hour is established.

The bane of the Muslims is blind fanaticism, which places matters of ijtihad (independent reasoning), which Allah left to His servants to choose freely, at the level of the fundamentals and creeds where there is no ijtihad. Thus they hasten to judge people and accuse them of disbelief merely for differing in matters of ijtihad.

We say: It is among Allah's mercy to us that He made the fundamentals one, with no disagreement over them. As for the branches and the matters of ijtihad that arise through the understanding of the mujtahid, Allah left them to the people of understanding, and each of us should respect the opinion of the other in them, based on the saying of Allah, Exalted is He: ﴿And if they had referred it to the Messenger and to those of authority among them, those who draw conclusions from it would have known it...﴾ (4:83).

Otherwise, if Allah, Glorified be He, had willed, He would not have made ijtihad for us in anything, and all the matters of religion would have come compelled, with no opinion or ijtihad for anyone. But the Truthful, Exalted is He, in His wisdom willed to gather us by compulsion on the matters which, if we did not agree upon, would be corrupted, while matters that are sound in any form He left to the ijtihad of His creatures.

So it is incumbent upon us to respect the opinions of others, not to presume against them, but to honor what Allah has chosen for us of freedom of thought and ijtihad.

Our model in this matter is the sunnah of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and the predecessors of this Ummah at the Battle of the Confederates (al-Ahzab). When the wind blew upon the camp of the disbelievers, uprooted their tents, scattered their ranks, and they fled the field, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) returned to Madinah. But soon his Lord commanded him to head to Banu Qurayzah to discipline them, and He informed him, Exalted is He, that the angels were still in readiness and had not laid down their weapons. So the Messenger of Allah gathered the Companions and said to them: {Whoever believes in Allah and the Last Day, let him not pray 'Asr except in Banu Qurayzah} (1).

Indeed, the Companions set out towards Banu Qurayzah between 'Asr and Maghrib. Some of them feared that Maghrib would overtake them before they prayed 'Asr, so they prayed on the way; and others adhered to the command of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) not to pray except in Banu Qurayzah, even if Maghrib overtook them. This difference arose among the Companions of the Messenger of Allah in his presence, but it was a difference in branches. When they referred it to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), he approved both groups, and he did not reproach any of them for what they had striven to derive.

So, in matters of ijtihad we should respect the opinions of others. Therefore, the scholars (may Allah be pleased with them) and people of balanced thought say: "My opinion is correct but may contain error, and the opinion of others is wrong but may contain correctness." Would that the Muslims rid themselves of this bane that has divided them and weakened their strength among the nations. Would that they always remember the saying of Allah, Exalted is He: ﴿Indeed, those who divided their religion and became sects, you are not [associated] with them in anything...﴾ (6:159).

When the Truthful, Blessed and Exalted, spoke about the matter of wudu', He, Glorified be He, said:

﴿O you who have believed, when you rise to prayer, wash your faces and your hands up to the elbows, and wipe over your heads and your feet up to the ankles...﴾ (5:6)

We notice that when He mentioned the face He said ﴿wash your faces...﴾ (5:6) without specifying limits for the face. Why? Because there is no disagreement among people about the face. But for the hands He said ﴿and your hands up to the elbows...﴾ (5:6), so He specified the hand up to the elbow, because it is a point of disagreement: some people say "the hands up to the shoulder," others say "up to the elbow," and others say "the palm of the hand."

Therefore our Lord, Mighty and Majestic, specified it to take us out of the circle of disagreement regarding washing this limb. Had He left it without this specification, the matter would have been permissible, with each person washing his hand as he sees fit. Likewise regarding the head, He, Glorified be He, said: ﴿and wipe over your heads...﴾ (5:6), and He left it to the possible meanings of the letter "bi'" (ب) which some see as indicating attachment, or extension, or partialness.

So, when you see one who differs with you in such matters, do not accuse him, because the text itself permitted this difference, and granted him, as it granted you, the right of ijtihad.

(1) A hadith agreed upon (muttafaq 'alayh). Related by al-Bukhari in his Sahih (4119), and likewise Muslim in his Sahih, Kitab al-Jihad wa al-Siyar (hadith 69), from the hadith of Ibn 'Umar, may Allah be pleased with them both, that the Prophet (ﷺ) proclaimed among them on the day the Confederates withdrew from them: "None of you should pray Zuhr except in Banu Qurayzah," and in another wording "'Asr."

Then the Truth, glory be to Him, said:

﴿And the chiefs of his people who disbelieved and denied the meeting of the Hereafter, and whom We had given luxury in the life of this world, said: "This is none but a human being like you. He eats of what you eat and drinks of what you drink."﴾ (23:33)

We have spoken about the meaning of al-Mala' (the chiefs, the notables) in ﴿al-mala'﴾ (23:33) [al-Mu'minun]: they are the essence of the notables, the people of authority and influence among the people, those who are troubled by the faith-based method, which undermines their standing, stands against their tyranny, their domination, and their subjugation of creation.

﴿And the chiefs of his people who disbelieved…﴾ (23:33) [al-Mu'minun]: exactly as happened with their predecessors, the people of Noah. ﴿…and denied the meeting of the Hereafter, and whom We had given luxury in the life of this world…﴾ (23:33) [al-Mu'minun]: the root is t-r-f, like farira (to be joyful). We say: taraffa al-rajul yataraffu (the man lived in luxury) when he enjoyed comfort. When you add the hamza (atraf), we say: atrafathu al-ni'mah, atrafahu Allah, meaning: prosperity became the cause of his tyranny, and God widened His bounty upon him so that he would expand in tyranny.

In this sense the Almighty said: ﴿So when they forgot what they had been reminded of…﴾ (6:44) [al-An'am], meaning: of the method of truth, ﴿We opened for them the gates of every thing until, when they rejoiced in what they had been given, We seized them suddenly, and at once they were in despair(1)﴾ (6:44) [al-An'am].

That is so that the seizing may be stronger, more severe, and more painful and more grievous. We previously mentioned an illustration that made the attendees laugh greatly, and to God is the highest likeness: we said that when God wants to bring down a stubborn opponent, He does not bring him down from a mat on the floor; rather He brings him down from a high chair and an elevated status, so that the fall (al-hadr) is stronger and more severe.

As for an ordinary person who owns nothing to grieve over, be it wealth, rank, or position, the matter is light. But when He raises him, elevates his standing, and makes him luxuriate in bliss, and then seizes him in this state, there is no doubt that it is the seizing of one mighty and powerful, and this is more intense and more painful.

So then: "atrafnahum" means: We widened for them and supplied them with various blessings so that they would increase in their disbelief and tyranny, in accordance with His saying: ﴿So leave them in their confusion(2) for a while. Do they think that what We extend to them of wealth and children [means that] We hasten to them in good things? Nay, they do not perceive.﴾ (23:54–56) [al-Mu'minun].

God, glorified and exalted, extends to these people the means of error and deviation so that they increase in them and go deeper into their sins, so that we may go deeper in their punishment and vengeance against them.

Then the Qur'an relates their saying which passed on the tongues of all of them in every message: ﴿This is none but a human being like you…﴾ (23:33) [al-Mu'minun]. It is as if this statement has become a necessary attribute of those who deny the messengers and obstinately oppose God's method. Then they insist on the humanity of the Messenger, saying: ﴿He eats of what you eat and drinks of what you drink﴾ (23:33) [al-Mu'minun]. Did not the disbelievers of Mecca say to the Messenger of God (ﷺ): ﴿What is with this Messenger that he eats food and walks in the markets?…﴾ (25:7) [al-Furqan].

Glory be to God! It is as if they speak with one tongue despite the differences of nations and the distance of times. But, as they say: disbelief is one creed.

1 - Ublisa: he was grieved, despaired, became bewildered, and fell silent in sorrow and distress, or fell silent because his argument was cut off. [al-Qamus al-Qawim 1/82].
2 - That is: in their misguidance and error. Said by Ibn Kathir in his tafsir (3/247). Al-Qurtubi said in his tafsir (6/4664): "al-ghamrah in language is what covers and overwhelms you, and its origin is concealment. Al-ghamr is abundant water, because it covers the earth. What is meant here is bewilderment, heedlessness, and error."

Qur'an 23:34: "And if you obey a human like yourselves, then indeed you would be losers."

Losers if you obey a human like yourselves. But he is a human who is not like you. He is a human to whom revelation is sent, so I do not follow him for his humanity; I only follow what is revealed to him.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 23, verse 35:

﴿Does he promise you that when you have died and become dust and bones, you will be brought forth?﴾ (35)

They deny resurrection after death, which their Prophet promises them. But what is the difficulty in the matter of resurrection? Is not re-creation easier than initial creation? If the Creator, exalted and majestic is He, has created you from nothing, then restoring you from crumbled remains is easier for Him. And although the word "easier" (ahwan) is not fitting with regard to God, Exalted is He, since He does not carry out His affairs through treatment or practice, but only through the word "Be" (kun), still, speech on this matter comes in terms that minds are accustomed to, and in a way that brings the issue closer to understanding.

﴿Hayhaat, hayhaat, for that which you are promised.﴾ (36)

﴿Hayhaat... (36)﴾ [Al-Mu'minun]: an ism fi'l (noun functioning as a verb, "verbal noun" in form), meaning "far off" or "remote," i.e., far off is this matter, namely that we should be returned after death, and after we have become bones and dust.

In the language, a word (kalimah) is either a noun (ism), a verb (fi'l), or a particle (harf). The noun is what indicates a meaning that is independently understood and not tied to a time; when you say "sama'" (sky), we understand that it is everything above you that shades you. The verb is a word that also indicates a meaning that is independently understood, but it is tied to a time; when we say "akala" (he ate), we understand the intended meaning, and it relates to the past tense. As for the particle (harf), it is a word that indicates a meaning that is not independent in itself. The particle "ala" (on) indicates the meaning of elevation, but elevation of what?

So the meaning, then, is not self-standing; it needs something to clarify it. Likewise, "fi" (in) indicates location, but does not by itself specify that location. Likewise "min" (from), which indicates the starting point, and "ila" (to), which indicates the end point. Each of the noun, verb, and particle has special markers by which it is recognized.

Apart from these three there is a fourth category that departs from this rule, which is why they call it al-Khalifah (the deviant one). It is the ism fi'l, such as "hayhaat" (far off), meaning "ba'uda" (be remote). It is a noun that indicates the meaning of a verb without accepting the markers of a verb. Similar to it is "shatana" (meaning "to be far apart/separated"), and "uff" (meaning "I am annoyed"), etc.

Then the Truthful, Glorified and Exalted says of them that they said:

﴿It is nothing but our life of this world: we die and we live, and we will not be resurrected.﴾ (23:37)

These people found the matter of resurrection far-fetched, because they do not believe in any life other than their worldly life; the matter, in their view, is confined to it. ﴿It is nothing but our life of this world...﴾ (23:37). Here "in" (إن) is a particle of negation meaning "it is not," as in His saying, exalted be He: ﴿They are not their mothers. Their mothers are only those who gave birth to them...﴾ (58:2). That is, "their mothers are none but those who bore them."

As for His saying, ﴿we die and we live...﴾ (23:37): some may think that by this statement they affirm resurrection, since they said "we die and we live," so how could they deny it? But what is meant is: we die, and those who come after us of our offspring live on, as is shown by their following words: ﴿and we will not be resurrected﴾ (23:37).

He is only a man who has invented a lie against God, and we will not believe him.

That is, the man who tells you about the matter of resurrection. It is strange of them to say this, for they know God and acknowledge Him: ﴿has invented a lie against God﴾. How could He be God without conveying to you a message through His Messenger? Otherwise, how would you come to know the method of God? They said: "By reason." But reason is not valid in this matter.

We have already given an example of this, and to God belongs the highest likeness: Suppose we are sitting in a closed room and the doorbell rings. There is no doubt that we will all agree that someone is at the door. This is called "ta'aqqul" (rational perception), but we will differ in our imagining: Is it a man? Or a woman? Or a child? Is it a bringer of good news or a warner? ... and so on.

So we agree when we stop at rational perception, but how do we know who is at the door? We have him tell us about himself when we say: "Who is the visitor?" He says: "I am so-and-so, and I have come for such-and-such." So who reports on rational perception? Its owner.

Likewise, your reason believes that the universe has a Creator who is Existent, and the signs of the universe point to Him. If you looked at this electric bulb that lights one room and reflected on it, you would find behind it factories, machines, tools, workers, engineers and inventors. Yet it has a limited capacity, a estimated lifespan, and it may break for some reason and go out.

Will you not likewise look at the sun and contemplate the signs and wonders in it, and how it lights half the earth at one time without ceasing to function, and without needing maintenance or a spare part? Yet no one has claimed it for himself. Does this not indicate that behind this great creation there is a greater Creator?

If we record the history of the discoverer of electricity and the inventor of the electric lamp, and mention what he made and how he reached what he reached, should we not be more worthy of investigating the Creator of this wondrous universe?

If you try to look at the disc of the sun during the day, your sight becomes dazzled and you cannot. When its heat intensifies, no one can bear it, although between you and the sun there are eight light-minutes, each second of which is three hundred thousand kilometres. What energy is this that emanates from the sun?

Among its wonders also is that you feel its heat on flat ground, but when you rise above a mountain, for example, or a high area, the temperature decreases even though you are getting closer to the sun. This is contrary to what happens if you light a fire, for you find that its heat decreases the further you move away from it. As for the sun, the closer you get to it, the lower the temperature becomes. Who is able to bring about this phenomenon?

If someone comes and tells me that he is the creator of this sun, I say to him: "Then it is yours, until a rival comes who claims it for himself." And no rival has come claiming it up to now.

As for their saying ﴿has invented﴾: it is an exaggeration on their part regarding their Messenger, because iftira' (invention) is the deliberate telling of a lie, and a lie, as we have said, is speech that contradicts reality. Speech may contradict reality yet be according to the knowledge of its speaker, in which case it is, in itself, truthful.

Subhan Allah, it is as if the history of the messages repeats itself with the deniers, and as if it is a fixed script (a "cliché") upon the tongues of the messengers: "Worship Allah; you have no god other than Him." Then they accuse him, deny him, and say: "You are only a human being like us." And the end always comes the same: "My Lord, help me against what they deny"; that is, "Replace their denial for me with victory."

This is the saying of Hud, peace be upon him, when his people denied him, and the saying of Nuh, and the saying of every prophet whose people denied him. For when a messenger is denied by those he was sent to, he takes refuge only in the One who sent him, because the One who sent him promised him support and succour: ﴿And indeed Our soldiers, they will be the victorious﴾ [al-Saffat: 173].

And He said: ﴿Allah will surely help those who help Him﴾ [al-Hajj: 40].

And He, glorified is He, said: ﴿And certainly has Our word preceded for Our servants, the messengers. Indeed, they would be the ones given victory﴾ [al-Saffat: 171-172].

So the meaning is: "Help me, for You have sent me, and my people have denied me after I have exhausted all my means in calling them, and I have no more strength against them, and nothing remains for me but Your aid." A person who has exhausted all the means that Allah has granted him, without reaching his goal, has become one in need (mudtarr), entering into His saying: ﴿Or who answers the distressed one when he calls upon Him...﴾ [al-Naml: 62].

Therefore: do not turn to Allah except after you have first fulfilled what is incumbent upon you, and expended all your effort in the pursuit of your goal. But do not sit idle from the means and say, "O Lord," while the land is before you, the axe is in your hand, and you have health and capability. Rather, work and exhaust your means first, so that you stand in the position of the distressed one whose supplication Allah answers.

Thus we often hear someone say: "I called upon Allah and He did not respond to me." We tell him: "You did not supplicate with the supplication of the distressed. You supplicate with the supplication of one who holds the means in his hand but neglected them; therefore you are not answered."

We see this even among people, and to Allah belongs the highest example: suppose you are a man of wealth and trade, and a shipment has arrived for you from customs, for instance, and you sit watching the workers carry it into the warehouses. It is not your task to carry or store it; that is the workers' duty. But suppose you find a worker whose load has become heavy on him, and the crate is about to fall him to the ground. What would your position be? Undoubtedly you would hasten to him, take him by the hand and help him, because he has done all that he could, and exhausted all his means and strength, so you would not withhold your aid from him.

Likewise, your Lord, Mighty and Majestic, wants you to fulfil what is upon you and not leave it for something for which He has made means available to you, for the means are the outstretched hand of Allah toward His creation. So do not reject Allah's hand by means, seeking the Essence without means.

Hence the saying of the messengers who were denied came: ﴿My Lord, help me against what they deny﴾ [al-Mu'minun: 39]: not while sitting idle, negligent and remiss, but rather, "against what they deny": that is, "I have done everything within my power, and I have no more strength against them."

Then the answer comes with speed:

﴿He said: "In a little while they will surely become regretful." (40)﴾

﴿ʿAmmā qalīl (in a little while) (40)﴾ [al-Mu'minun]: That is, after a little while. Here ʿan (عن) carries the sense of "after," as in His saying, exalted is He: ﴿You will surely ride from state to state (19)﴾ [al-Inshiqaq], meaning: after state.

As for mā (ما) in ﴿mā (40)﴾ [al-Mu'minun]: here it indicates a temporal adverbial sense, because what is meant is "after a little time."

﴿They will surely become regretful (40)﴾ [al-Mu'minun]: when there befalls them that which they used to deny, and the punishment descends upon them, they will regret, because they will not be able to make up for what they missed; there will be nothing left for them then but regret. This matter shows that the human nature (fitrah), when desires do not cloud it, ends in itself at the truth, and even if anger drives it toward falsehood, it returns to its balance and to the right path once the fury of anger subsides.

The Truth, blessed and exalted is He, gives us proofs and indications concerning this matter in the story of the two sons of Adam, peace be upon him, where He says: ﴿And recite to them the news of the two sons of Adam in truth, when they each offered a sacrifice, and it was accepted from one of them but not accepted from the other. He said: "I will surely kill you." He said: "Allah only accepts from the righteous (27)"﴾ [al-Ma'idah].

Until He, glorified be He, said: ﴿So his soul induced him to kill his brother, and he killed him... (30)﴾ [al-Ma'idah]. The killing came as an effect of anger. It would be expected that after he had killed him he would have relieved his soul and should have rejoiced, because he had achieved what he wanted. But ﴿he became among the regretful (31)﴾ [al-Ma'idah].

That is: after the fury of anger had subsided within him, he regretted what he had done. Why? Because this is the nature of the human soul, which is not thrown off balance nor driven out of its equilibrium except by caprice; if caprice departs, it returns to rectitude and to the truth. It is as though God, exalted is He, created in man standards that passions must not corrupt and anger must not drive beyond the limit of moderation. Therefore they say: the bane of opinion is caprice.

Qabil awoke, but only after he saw the evil consequence to which his haste had brought him. But the intelligent person awakens before the reaction.

Yet why did He choose for them the time of morning specifically? ﴿They will surely become regretful (40)﴾ [al-Mu'minun]: One who follows what befell the nations that denied of punishment and retribution finds that it generally came in the morning, as He, exalted is He, said: ﴿Then do they seek to hasten Our punishment? (176) But when it descends upon their courtyard, evil is the morning of those who were warned (177)﴾ [al-Saffat].

And He, glorified be He, said: ﴿And there had already come upon them in the morning a settled punishment (38)﴾ [al-Qamar].

And He, glorified be He, said: ﴿So they called one another in the morning (21)﴾ [al-Qalam].

That is because morning follows a period of sleep and bodily inactivity. They rise from their sleep and the punishment surprises them, seizing them unawares and unprepared to confront it, unlike if the punishment came to them during the day while they were ready.

Their regret is that they denied a matter that should not have been denied, and it dragged upon them calamities. Regret over a good that has passed is characteristic of human nature, which is often overcome by desire, which is lured by folly to reject the truth, and which is restrained by arrogance from submitting to the Messenger in particular, since he is a human like them, and who, in their assumption, wishes to dominate over them. But when they face the consequence of this denial and the result of this folly, they regret, and ﴿there is no time for regret (lāt sāʿat mandam)﴾.

Thus: the soul's desire makes a person take a stance which, if he is requited for it with severity, he regrets not having carried out and not having obeyed. He regrets his arrogance in a situation where he should have relinquished his pride. Therefore they say: "Courage is to be cowardly for an hour."

This is good when you are before an enemy you cannot confront. We may recall the late President Sadat's stance when he said: "I cannot fight America." Some understood this statement as weakness and cowardice, but it is not so; it is rather courage from the man, a refined kind of courage, because among courage is also to be brave against yourself, and this is a higher courage than courage against your enemy. And imagine if Sadat had entered such a war and been defeated: how would he have regretted a reckless bravery that does not reckon consequences. We have seen the outcome of daring to enter a war of unequal strength.

Then the Truth, glory be to Him, says:

﴿So the Blast seized them in truth, and We made them debris (ghuthaa’). So away with the wrongdoing people.﴾ (23:41):

Since the Truth, blessed and exalted is He, has threatened them and set for them an appointed time, this threat must certainly befall them at that very time. Otherwise, if it passed without anything befalling them that would make them regret it, the principle itself would collapse from its foundation, since God Most High has said it and recorded it upon Himself, glory be to Him, in a Qur'an that He Himself preserves.

﴿In a little while they will surely become regretful.﴾ (23:40): So the punishment must descend upon them in the morning.

Therefore: ﴿So the Blast seized them in truth..﴾ (23:41): not with injustice and aggression.
