In another place He, glory be to Him, said of them: ﴿And as for ʿĀd, they were destroyed by a furious, screaming wind.﴾ (69:6). The two meanings converge, for the screaming wind has a roaring sound like the blast and the shriek.

﴿And We made them debris..﴾ (23:41): Ghuthaa’ (ghuthaʾ) is what the torrent carries of straw, leaves and remnants of plants, forming a layer floating on the surface of the water, which the wind carries away to one side. Ghuthaa’ is also the foam (zabad) of which the Truth, glory be to Him and exalted, said: ﴿As for the foam, it vanishes as scum; but as for what benefits people, it remains upon the earth..﴾ (13:17).

In the noble hadith, the Prophet (ﷺ) said to his companions: "The nations will soon summon one another against you as diners summon one another to their bowl." That is, some of them call others to fight you, as though you were spoils they wish to divide. They said: "Is it because of our small number, O Messenger of God?" He said: "Rather, you will be many on that day, but you will be debris like the debris of a torrent." (1) That is: something insignificant, of no value, that passes away swiftly.

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿So away with the wrongdoing people.﴾ (23:41): that is, away from Our mercy and Our bounty, which We promised them and held out to them had they believed. "Away" here does not mean distance from the punishment, for distance (bu'd) is a measure of time or place; we say, "This is far," meaning its time or its place. What is meant here is distance from the bounty that awaited them had they believed.

Injustice (zulm), as we have said, is taking the right of another. Association (shirk) is the greatest injustice, because it is injustice in the matter of the summit. Some superficial people think that associating partners with God is a great wrong because you have wronged God, Glory be to Him, by denying His existence while He exists, and by associating with Him another while He is One with no partner. Yes, you have wronged, but you have not wronged God, for no one can wrong Him. Even if injustice, as we say, is taking the right of another, God's right is preserved and established for Him, glory be to Him, before anyone exists to acknowledge that right. God's right stands firm, however high falsehood rises and however the people of misguidance boast.

Therefore the Mighty and Majestic says: ﴿And He made the word of those who disbelieved the lowest..﴾ (9:40). And in contrast: ﴿And the word of God is the highest..﴾ (9:40). He did not say, by analogy with the first, "and the word of God the highest," because that would mean the word of God was not highest at any time. So it came with "the word of God" as a nominal sentence, indicating permanence: ﴿And the word of God is the highest..﴾ (9:40): that is, always, and however high the word of the disbelievers rises. Why?

They said: because the elevation of the word of the disbelievers is in itself an elevation for the word of God. When disbelief rises and its evil spreads, it startles people, awakens their heedlessness, and alerts them to the baseness and vileness of disbelief and the injustice and corruption it brings upon them, so they reject it and return to the right path and to the truth that is firmly God's, the Mighty and Majestic.

So: the word of God is the highest, however the round goes to the word of those who disbelieved. As they say: "Opposites reveal each other's beauty." God, the Mighty and Majestic, does not abandon the truth, but leaves it to test people's zeal for it; if they are not jealous for it, He Himself becomes jealous for it.

Since they did not wrong God, and cannot do so, they wronged only themselves. And if reason understands your wronging of another and taking his right, it does not understand your wronging of yourself, for that is the most grievous and far-reaching kind of injustice.

1 - Recorded by Ahmad in his Musnad (5/278), and Abu Dawud in his Sunan (4297), from the hadith of Thawban, freedman of the Messenger of God (ﷺ).

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 23, verse 42:

﴿Then We produced after them other generations.﴾ (42)

Some verses earlier the Truthful, Blessed and Exalted said: ﴿Then We produced after them another generation.﴾ (31) [al-Mu'minun]. Here the word "qarn" (generation) came in the singular, because the account was confined to the people of 'Ad, the people of Hud. As for here, He, Exalted is He, said: ﴿Then We produced after them generations..﴾ (42) [al-Mu'minun], because the discussion is about to address nations and messages that are different and many. Thus "qurun" (generations) came in the plural form: generations following one another, or contemporaneous, as Abraham and Lot were contemporaries, and as Moses and Shu'ayb were contemporaries, upon them all be peace and the blessings of Allah, and upon our Prophet be prayers and peace.

Then Allah, glorified and exalted, says:

﴿No community can precede its appointed term, nor can they delay it.﴾ (43)

Reflect on this verse carefully and give it your full attention. Every community has an appointed term at which it comes to an end without fail, just like the appointed term of individuals, which can neither advance nor be postponed. Generation after generation and nation after nation pass through various stages, like the stages of human life, until they arrive at decline and are succeeded by others.

For every community there is a messenger who carries the call of Allah and His method and strives to spread it, until Allah grants him victory, his call spreads, and people hold fast to it. Then heedlessness and lethargy regarding the method of Allah overtake them, so they turn away from it, disagree, and split apart. This becomes a sign of their passing, and others then succeed them.

Likewise with civilizations that crumble to make way for other, stronger civilizations. We hear of ancient civilizations in Egypt, in China, and in Yemen; we hear of the Roman civilization, the Phoenician civilization, and so on. Civilizations follow one another and take their share of advancement and luxury, but they bequeath to their people softness and slackness, and they exchange for their sturdiness and strength pliancy and weakness. So they become heedless of the causes of their advancement and progress, and their civilization collapses, and in its place arises one stronger and firmer than it.

This is an example and a model of a civilization that reached the peak of its greatness: ﴿Have you not considered how your Lord dealt with 'Ad, [the people of] Iram, of the pillars, the like of which was not created in the land? And Thamud, who carved out the rocks in the valley? And Pharaoh, the one of the stakes?﴾ [Al-Fajr].

And to this day, as we see the remains of the Pharaonic civilization and how it draws the attention of people of modern civilizations and wins their admiration, they come to it from every corner of the world, although the civilization of 'Ad was greater than it, because Allah the Exalted said concerning it: ﴿the like of which was not created in the land﴾ [Al-Fajr].

Yet we see no trace of them that indicates the greatness of their civilization. This civilization had no immunity to protect itself or preserve anything for itself, so it collapsed, perished, and not even a trace of it remained.

Likewise, the followers of the messengers pass through this same cycle: after the strength of faith, heedlessness overtakes them, weakness and a bad condition seep into them, until Allah, glorified, sends a new messenger.

﴿No community can precede its appointed term, nor can they delay it.﴾ [Al-Mu'minun] (43)

The meaning of the first clause is clear: no community can precede the term that Allah has set for it, and it cannot end or collapse before that term arrives.

But what is meant by His saying: ﴿nor can they delay it﴾ [Al-Mu'minun] (43)? How can that happen? Our understanding is this: "they cannot precede their term" means that their term is for them to collapse after twenty years, so they cannot collapse before fifteen. But how can it be that after reaching twenty they are delayed to ten? How does that happen?

We say: "nor can they delay" means: in terms of ruling, they do not precede the term, and they are judged as not being delayed, because delay after reaching the term is impossible, just as if we said: a person who has reached the age of twenty cannot die at the age of ten. So the meaning is: the basic principle is that it cannot be delayed.

Then the Truth, glory be to Him, says:

﴿Then We sent Our messengers in succession. Every time a messenger came to a nation, they denied him, so We made them follow one another, and We made them into tales. So away with the people who do not believe.﴾ (23:44)

﴿Tatran (in succession)...﴾ (23:44): It means successive, following one another. For this reason some took it to be a verb, though it is not a verb, as is shown by the fact that it is read in another recitation as "tatran" with tanwin (nunation), and a verb does not take tanwin. Therefore it is a noun, and the alif in it is for the feminine, like in "hublá" (pregnant).

Moreover, the first letter ta' in the language may stand in place of a waw, as in the noble hadith of the advice of the Prophet (ﷺ): "Guard Allah and He will guard you; guard Allah and you will find Him before you" (or "in front of you"), meaning: facing you.

So if the first ta' in "tatran" is replaced by a waw, you say "watran", meaning following one after another, one by one, and the watr (odd, single) is the single unit.

Then He, glory be to Him, says: ﴿Every time a messenger came to a nation, they denied him...﴾ (23:44): This is a characteristic and a necessary attribute of those sent to. No messenger was sent to a people except that they denied him. Then he turns to his Lord: ﴿He said: "My Lord, help me, for they have denied me."﴾ (23:39).

Had the messengers not been denied, there would have been no need for sending them to them. A messenger only came after falsehood had spread and tyranny had become widespread. It is natural that there would be denial from those who profit from evil, who benefit from falsehood, and who defend it with all their strength. Their denial of the messengers was evidence of the correctness of the messengers' coming; otherwise there would have been no need for new messages.

As for His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Then We made them follow one another...﴾ (23:44): It means one passes away and another messenger comes after him, or We destroy the deniers and then others come after them, and they deny, so We destroy them too.

﴿And We made them into tales...﴾ (23:44): "Aḥādīth" is either the plural of ḥadīth, as we say "the ḥadīths of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ)", or the plural of uḥdūthah (a topic of talk), which is the saying that everyone gossips about and that every tongue chews over. From this is the saying of a person when people's talk about him has become much: "They have made me a uḥdūtha," meaning by way of rebuke and reproach to them.

So His saying: ﴿And We made them into tales...﴾ (23:44) is as if no trace of them remained except that we speak about them and mention them as a history that is recounted. In another place He, exalted is He, says: ﴿So We made them into tales and scattered them completely.﴾ (34:19)

Then He, exalted is He, says of them, as He said of their predecessors: ﴿So away with the people who do not believe.﴾ (23:44): It means: away from the mercy of Allah, and away from the bounty of Allah that awaited them; had they believed, they would have attained it.

[Footnote 1: This is the reading of Ibn Kathir and Abu 'Amr with tanwin, taking it as a verbal noun (maṣdar) with tanwin added to a fatha on the rā'. (Tafsir al-Qurtubi 6/4659)]

[Footnote 2: Recorded by Ahmad in his Musnad (1/293, 303, 307), and al-Tirmidhi in his Sunan (2516), who said: "a hasan sahih hadith", from the hadith of Abdullah ibn Abbas.]

Then the Truth, glory be to Him, says:

﴿Then We sent Moses and his brother Aaron with Our signs and a clear authority﴾ (45):

The story of Moses, peace be upon him, is repeated many times, and with him his brother Aaron, as He said: ﴿Strengthen my back through him, and make him a partner in my affair﴾ [Ta-Ha]. Some people think that Moses came with one message, but he came with two messages: a special message to Pharaoh, the summary of which is: ﴿So send with us the Children of Israel and do not torment them...﴾ [Ta-Ha].

He also brought miracles that proved the truth of his message from God. Moses' debate with Pharaoh on the matter of faith was not part of this message; rather, it came incidentally in the discussion that took place between them.

The other message is his message to the Children of Israel, represented in the Torah.

As for His saying ﴿with Our signs...﴾ [al-Mu'minun] (45): we have said that the word ayat (signs) is the plural of ayah, which is a wondrous thing that catches the eye, surpassing its peers and equals, and which is honoured and taken pride in. The signs are either cosmic, indicating God's power in creation, such as the sun and the moon, etc., as He, glory be to Him, said: ﴿And among His signs are the night and the day...﴾ [Fussilat] (37).

The task of these cosmic signs is to draw the creature's attention to the marvellous craftsmanship of the Creator and the necessity of believing in Him. From them we know that behind this marvellous universe there is a Creator and a power that sustains and governs it. Who supplies the sun with this tremendous power? If the electric current is cut off, this lamp goes out. Who created the sun from nothing and supplied it with energy from nothing?

So: behind this universe is a power. What is it? What does it demand of us? This is the task of the Messenger: to convey to us and answer these questions for us.

The word ayah is also applied to the miracle that proves the Messenger's truthfulness in conveying from God.

The word ayah is also applied to the verses of the Qur'an, which carry the rulings and contain God's method for His creation.

Then He, exalted is He, says: ﴿and a clear authority﴾ [al-Mu'minun] (45). So ﴿a clear authority﴾ is conjoined to ﴿with Our signs...﴾ [al-Mu'minun] (45). This is the conjunction of an attribute to the thing it describes, for greater specificity, because the signs are the authority. Thus "authority" means proof. The proof of the Supreme Being is the signs of the universe, the proof of the Messenger's truthfulness is the miracles, and the proof of the rulings is the verses that carry them.

Moses' miracle, peace be upon him, the staff (al-'asa), was called a clear authority, meaning encompassing, because it was a repeated miracle with several states that we witnessed: this dry staff at one time turns into a serpent that swallows the serpents, at another time he strikes the sea with it and it splits, at another he strikes the rock with it and water gushes forth from it, and beyond that He said of it: ﴿and I have in it other uses﴾ [Ta-Ha] (18).

Among the meanings of sultan (authority) is compulsion to do something, or persuasion by proof to do that thing. Therefore the only argument of Iblis on the Day of Resurrection will be that he says to his followers: ﴿I had no authority over you except that I invited you and you responded to me...﴾ [Ibrahim] (22). That is: you were at my beck and call; I have no authority over you, neither authority of compulsion nor authority of proof.

Therefore He said at the end: ﴿I cannot help you, nor can you help me...﴾ [Ibrahim] (22). A person cries out (yasrukh) when a matter that he has no means to handle frightens him, so he cries out summoning a helper who will assist him. Whoever hastens to him and helps him is said to "asrakha-hu" (relieve his cry): that is, he removes the cause of his crying out.

﴿To Pharaoh and his chiefs, but they behaved arrogantly, and they were a haughty people (46)﴾:

﴿Pharaoh (46)﴾ [al-Mu'minun]: a title for everyone who ruled Egypt, like Kisra (Khosrow) among the Persians and Caesar among the Romans. We have spoken about the meaning of al-Mala' (the chiefs/notables), which derives from imtila' (being full), and it refers to the people who fill the eyes with awe and rank, who are the nobles of the people and the foremost in gatherings. From the same root is their saying: "So-and-so is qayd al-nawazir," meaning: whoever looks at him does not turn away from him to anything else.

As for His, exalted is He, saying: ﴿So they behaved arrogantly, and they were a haughty people (46)﴾ [al-Mu'minun]: istikbar (arrogance) is other than ta'ali (haughtiness). The arrogant person knows the ruling and acknowledges it, but refuses to obey it and disdains to do what he was commanded. As for the haughty person, he is one who thinks that he never entered into the command from the beginning.

From here came His saying, exalted is He, to Iblis when he refused to prostrate to Adam: ﴿Have you become arrogant, or were you among the haughty ones? (75)﴾ [Sad].

And "al-'Alun" (the haughty ones) are the angels who are overwhelmed in God, and who know nothing of Adam and his offspring.

Al-Sha'rawi's commentary on surah 23, verse 47:

﴿Fa-qalu anu'minu libasharayni mithlana wa-qawmuhuma lana 'abidun﴾ (47):

They also objected here to the humanity of Musa and Harun, as had happened with the earlier nations. They want the Messenger to be an angel, as occurs in another passage: ﴿And nothing prevented the people from believing when guidance came to them except that they said, "Has Allah sent a human as a messenger?"﴾ [al-Isra' 94].

It is foolish for them to ask for an angel as a messenger, for if an angel had come to them as a messenger, how would he serve as an example for humans? How would they see him and receive from him? Therefore, he must come to them in human form. For this reason the Exalted says: ﴿And if We had made him an angel, We would have made him a man and We would have covered for them what they cover [themselves with]﴾ [al-An'am 9].

The doubt would remain: what would make you believe that he is an angel?

As for His saying, ﴿and their people are for us worshippers﴾ (47) [al-Mu'minun]: it means: how can we believe in Musa and Harun when their people, the Children of Israel, are our servants, who carry out our orders? Rather, we humiliate them, slaughter their sons, spare their women, and subject them to terrible torment.

He called that worship (ʿibada) because whoever submits to a person and obeys his command is, as it were, his slave.

﴿So they denied the two of them, and they became among those destroyed﴾ (23:48).

That is: by drowning. This is a well-known and familiar story, and God made it a warning example and a lesson.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 23, verse 49:

﴿And We certainly gave Moses the Scripture, that they might be guided.﴾

﴿The Scripture...﴾ [Al-Mu'minun]: That is, the Torah, and in it is the method of guidance. ﴿That they might be guided.﴾ [Al-Mu'minun]: That is, they take the path that leads to the noble and beneficial goal by the shortest route.

Then Allah, glorified and exalted, says:

﴿And We made the son of Mary and his mother a sign, and We gave them refuge on a high ground, a place of settlement and flowing water.﴾

After giving us this brief glimpse of the story of Musa and Harun, He moved on to the Messiah, the son of Mary. In speaking of Jesus, peace be upon him, the Qur'an sometimes says "the son of Mary" and sometimes says "Jesus, the son of Mary." Naming Jesus after his mother is what made our lady and the mistress of the women of the worlds, Mary, when she was given the good news of a boy, express astonishment and say: "How can I have a son when no man has touched me?" It did not occur to her that she could marry and bear a child. Why? Because God called him the son of Mary, and since He named him after his mother, then he would have no father.

Nothing is harder for a young woman than to find herself pregnant when no man has touched her, because a young woman's honour is the most precious and dear thing she possesses. For this reason, the Truth, blessed and exalted, prepared the ground for this matter and readied Mary to receive it, and gave her the immunity necessary to face this wondrous affair, just as we now do with vaccination against diseases, providing the immunity that prevents illness.

When Zakariya, peace be upon him, entered upon Mary and found with her provision that he had not brought, and he was her guardian and responsible for her, he asked her: ﴿Where has this come to you from?﴾ She said: ﴿It is from Allah.﴾ [Al 'Imran 3:37] This answer from Mary came from a complete understanding of the matter of provision, and was not the speech of mere pious simplicity, as evidenced by her saying afterwards: ﴿Indeed, Allah provides for whom He wills without account.﴾ [Al 'Imran 3:37]

In this situation there is a lesson for every father, every guardian and every head of a household: that he should ask the people of his house about everything he sees in his home that he did not bring, so that he does not leave his children the opportunity to reach out their hands to what is not theirs.

Zakariya, peace be upon him, benefited from this statement and became aware of this truth. Yes, Zakariya knew that Allah provides for whom He wills without account, but that knowledge was a piece of information on the margin of his consciousness. When he heard it from Mary, it moved into the centre of his awareness, and at that point he prayed to Allah to grant him a child, though he had reached great old age and his wife was barren.

Likewise, Mary benefited from it when she sensed the pregnancy without any human having touched her, and she was reassured, because Allah provides for whom He wills without account.

As for His saying, exalted be He: ﴿And We made the son of Mary and his mother...﴾ [al-Mu'minun 23:50]: He reported about the two, using the singular for the dual: ﴿a sign...﴾ [al-Mu'minun 23:50], because they share in it. Mary is a sign because she bore a child without a husband, and Jesus is a sign because he was born without a father. So the sign is not found in one of them without the other, and they are equal in it.

For this reason the Qur'anic text observes this equality: it mentions Jesus first in the verse ﴿And We made the son of Mary and his mother a sign﴾ [al-Mu'minun 23:50], and it mentions Mary first in another verse: ﴿And We made her and her son a sign for the worlds﴾ [al-Anbiya' 21:91]. This is justice in the text, because they are equal in being a sign, and neither is distinguished from the other.

The sign is the wondrous matter that establishes for us the unrestricted power of the Creator in creation. Lest some think that the matter of creation is a "mechanical" matter of a father and a mother, the wonder in the creation of Jesus was that it departed from this rule, so that Allah would make it a proof of His power, exalted be He. If He wills to create, He creates from nothing, or from a father alone, or from a mother alone. Even when both elements are complete, a father and a mother exist, but there is no begetting. So the matter is by the will of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, and an expression of a divine power without limits.

He, glorified be He, says: ﴿To Allah belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth. He creates what He wills. He grants to whom He wills females and grants to whom He wills males, or He pairs them, males and females, and He makes whom He wills barren.﴾ [al-Shura 42:49-50]

Now we notice that some try to prevent childbirth by all means, but if a child is decreed for someone, it comes in spite of everyone, and despite the perfection of the methods of contraception in which they have excelled.

Then He, glorified be He, says: ﴿And We gave them refuge on a high ground, a place of settlement and flowing water.﴾ [al-Mu'minun 23:50] It is natural that after Mary had conceived in this manner she would be persecuted and pursued by her people, and that she would feel shame before people and avoid being seen by anyone. Do you not see His saying, exalted be He, about the daughter of Shu'ayb: ﴿Then one of the two women came to him walking bashfully﴾ [al-Qasas 28:25]? "Bashfully," because she went to summon a young man who was a stranger to her. What then of Mary, when the people see her pregnant with no husband? It is a matter as hard as anything can be for a woman.

For this reason, when Imam Muhammad 'Abduh was asked, while he was in Paris: "In what manner did 'A'isha face her people after the incident of the slander?" God inspired him with the answer and guided him to what is correct. He said: "In the same manner in which Mary faced her people when she came carrying her child." That is because they wanted to make her a disgrace and a stain on the forehead of Islam.

And since Mary was of this character, Allah took charge of her and defended her. There was Yusuf the carpenter, who was Mary's betrothed. When he saw the matter of her pregnancy, and he was the most jealous of men regarding her, instead of doubting her and accusing her, his heart turned towards her with tenderness, as He said, exalted be He: ﴿And know that Allah intervenes between a person and his heart﴾ [al-Anfal 8:24].

So he began to serve her and be kind to her, because Allah caused the matter to settle in his heart with acceptance. And everything he said when disputing with Mary and enquiring about what had happened, in a courteous manner, was: "O Mary, have you seen a tree without a seed?" Mary laughed, having understood what he meant, and said: "Yes, the tree that first produced a seed." [2] This is the speech of people of faith and of understanding of Allah.

So Allah gave them refuge, both she and her son: ﴿And We gave them refuge on a high ground, a place of settlement and flowing water.﴾ [al-Mu'minun 23:50] Whenever you hear the word "refuge," you understand that a person was compelled to a place to which he resorts and in which he takes shelter. Likewise Mary was compelled and needed a place to shelter her, since she was persecuted by her people. In such a place of refuge there must be the essentials of life available, especially for someone like Mary who was preparing to receive her child. The essentials of life are air, water and food.

Consider how the Truth, glorified and exalted be He, prepared a place of refuge for Mary: ﴿a high ground﴾ [al-Mu'minun 23:50], meaning a place raised above the ground, lower than the mountain. It has a moderate climate, being between the heat of the level ground and the cold at the top of the mountain.

﴿a place of settlement﴾ [al-Mu'minun 23:50], meaning that the causes of stability were available to her, such as water and food. The water came to her from the top of the mountains and flowed past her as "flowing water," meaning that you can see it with your own eye. The food came to her from the fruit of the palm tree that had come down beside her.

It is well known that a high ground is the most suitable place, since water passes over it from above and no groundwater remains there to harm its crops, because the water drains away from the lower land beneath it.

For this reason the Truth, blessed and exalted be He, struck for us the parable of fertile land that yields abundant produce, saying: ﴿And the example of those who spend their wealth seeking the approval of Allah and for the strengthening of their souls is like a garden on a high ground﴾ [al-Baqarah 2:265].

So Allah, exalted be He, chose for Mary a place of settlement in which the essentials of life are available at the highest level, such that she would have no need to move from it to anywhere else.

1 - Al-Rabwa: what is raised above the ground. Ibn Kathir said in his commentary (3/246): "The commentators differed about the location of this high ground: which land is it?
- In Egypt. This was said by 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn Aslam, who said there are no high grounds except in Egypt. Ibn Kathir said: this is very far-fetched.
- Damascus. This was said by Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib. Ibn 'Abbas said: the rivers of Damascus.
- Ramla in Palestine. This was said by Abu Hurayra.
- Bayt al-Maqdis (Jerusalem). This was said by al-Dahhak and Qatada.
Ibn Kathir said: "This, and Allah knows best, is the most apparent, because it is the one mentioned in the other verse, and the Qur'an explains itself, and this is the most fitting thing to explain it by, then the sound hadiths, then the reports."
2 - Ibn Kathir cited it in his commentary (3/116), and in it Mary, peace be upon her, answered him: "As for your saying, 'Can a tree grow without a seed and a crop without a grain?' Indeed Allah created trees and crops, when He first created them, without seed or grain. And can a child be born without a father? Indeed Allah, exalted be He, created Adam without a father or a mother." He confirmed her, and accepted her situation.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 23, verse 51:

After speaking of settled existence and the necessities of life, namely food, drink and air, the Truthful and Exalted One (Allah, glory be to Him) speaks of a general matter, and it is fitting that He, glory be to Him, should speak of food:

﴿O messengers, eat of the good things and do righteous deeds. Indeed, I am Knowing of what you do.﴾ (23:51)

But how does the Lord, blessed and exalted, address all the messengers at one time? We say: because the Noble Qur'an is the eternal speech of Allah. It did not come specifically for Muhammad (ﷺ); although it was revealed to him, it is therefore an address to every messenger who came.

After Allah commanded them to eat of the good, He commanded them to do righteous deeds: ﴿and do righteous deeds...﴾ (23:51), then He says: ﴿Indeed, I am Knowing of what you do﴾ (23:51). It is as if Allah, glory be to Him, is saying: Listen to My speech regarding what I command you, for I am Knowing and Aware of everything that benefits you, because I am the Creator who knows how your constitution is made upright for good action, and your constitution is not made upright for good action except if you take your food from what is lawful and good.

As we have said: the maker of a machine supplies it with the fuel suited to its operation, otherwise it stops performing its task.

So, in order that you may perform righteousness in the movement of your life, you must begin with good food that builds your particles from what is lawful, so that harmony arises among these particles, and they work together, cooperating and not opposing one another. If your particles are in harmony and in accord, they help you toward righteousness.

But if the unlawful enters your food and your particles are polluted by it, they repel one another and oppose one another, just as if you put into a machine a fuel other than that which was made for it. So understand this matter, for I am the Creator; so believe in Me just as you believe in the power of the maker when he makes a manufactured product for you and sets down for you the rules for its maintenance.

Thus: Allah, glory be to Him, first commanded His messengers to eat of the good things, because righteous action requires a sound apparatus that is in harmony from within. Therefore, in the biography of the Prophet (ﷺ) it is related that Umm Abdullah, the sister of Shaddad ibn Aws, sent to the Prophet on a day when he was fasting and it was hot some milk for him to break his fast with, and he (ﷺ) knew that she was poor and owned nothing, so he sent to her: "From where do you have this milk?" She sent back: "From a sheep I have." He sent to her: "And from where do you have the sheep?" She said: "I bought it with money I had arranged." Then the Messenger of Allah drank of the milk.(1)

And although we do not scrutinize our food with all this scrutiny, this is the Messenger of Allah, who implements the method of Allah as it came to him, and in the most perfect manner. In the noble hadith: "O people, indeed Allah is Good and accepts only what is good, and indeed Allah commanded the believers with what He commanded the messengers, so He said: ﴿O messengers, eat of the good things and do righteous deeds. Indeed, I am Knowing of what you do﴾ (23:51). And He said: ﴿O you who have believed, eat of the good things with which We have provided you...﴾ (2:172)." Then he mentioned a man who prolongs the journey, disheveled and dusty, who raises his hands to the sky, saying: "O Lord, O Lord," while his food is unlawful, his drink is unlawful, his clothing is unlawful, and he is nourished with the unlawful, so how could he be answered?"(2)

Indeed, how could he be answered, when he calls upon Allah with a transmitting device that is corrupt, clouded, defiled, and mixed with the unlawful?

And in the hadith of our master Sa'd, may Allah be pleased with him, when he said to the Messenger of Allah: "O Messenger of Allah, supplicate Allah for me that I may be one whose supplication is answered." The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "O Sa'd, purify your food and you will be one whose supplication is answered."(3)

Then Allah, glory be to Him, concludes this verse with His saying: ﴿Indeed, I am Knowing of what you do﴾ (23:51). That is: I know what benefits you and what brings you good.

1 - From Umm Abdullah, the sister of Shaddad ibn Aws, that she sent to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) a bowl of milk at his breaking of the fast, while he was fasting, and that was in the length of the day and the intensity of the heat. His messenger returned to her: "From where do you have this milk?" She said: "From a sheep of mine." He said: The messenger returned to her: "From where did this sheep come to you?" She said: "I bought it with my own money." So he took it from her. When it was the next day she came to him and said: "O Messenger of Allah, I sent you milk, having been distressed for you because of the length of the day and the intensity of the heat, but you returned the messenger with it." He said to her: "With that were the messengers commanded: not to eat except what is good, and not to act except righteously." Narrated by al-Haythami in Majma' al-Zawa'id (10/291), who said: "Al-Tabarani narrated it, and in its chain is Abu Bakr ibn Abi Maryam, who is weak."

2 - Recorded by Muslim in his Sahih (1015), Ahmad in his Musnad (2/328), and al-Tirmidhi in his Sunan (2989), from the hadith of Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him.

3 - From Ibn Abbas, who said: This verse was recited in the presence of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ): ﴿O mankind, eat of what is on earth [that is] lawful and good...﴾ (2:168). Then Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas stood and said: "O Messenger of Allah, supplicate Allah that He make me one whose supplication is answered." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "O Sa'd, purify your food and you will be one whose supplication is answered. By the One in whose hand is the soul of Muhammad, indeed a servant casts a morsel of unlawful food into his stomach, and his deeds are not accepted for forty days; and whatever servant's flesh grew from the unlawful, the Fire is more deserving of him." Narrated by al-Haythami in Majma' al-Zawa'id (10/291), who said: "Al-Tabarani narrated it in al-Saghir, and in it are people whom I do not know."

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 23, verse 52:

Then the Truthful One, glory be to Him, says:

﴿And indeed, this community of yours is one community, and I am your Lord, so fear Me.﴾

After the Truthful One, may He be exalted, spoke of the battle between faith and disbelief, He wished here to speak of another battle, no less dangerous than the first: the battle of division and disagreement within the ranks of the believers. He warns us against the disputes that split our unity, that weaken the strength of the Ummah and make it feeble before its enemies. We hear them now saying about us, given what we have come to of sects and parties: let them first agree among themselves, and then preach Islam.

The ummah (community) is a group united by a single time or a single religion. It is also applied to a single individual in whom the qualities of goodness gather, which gather only in a whole community. For this reason God, exalted be He, named His Prophet Ibrahim an ummah in His saying, exalted be He: ﴿Indeed, Ibrahim was a community, devoutly obedient to Allah, a hanif, and he was not of the polytheists.﴾ [An-Nahl: 120]

As for His saying, glory be to Him: ﴿For each of you We have made a law and a clear way.﴾ [Al-Ma'idah: 48], how then do we say: it is one community?

They said: because religion consists of principles and beliefs, and these are one, not differing with the differing of religions; and of morals and branches (furu'), and these differ from one religion to another according to the environment, because they come with what suits the movement of life in every age.

He, exalted be He, says: ﴿He has ordained for you of religion what He enjoined upon Noah and what We have revealed to you, and what We enjoined upon Ibrahim and Musa and Isa: that you establish the religion and do not be divided therein...﴾ [Ash-Shura: 13]

So then: the community is one, meaning in its beliefs, even if it differs in the sharia and the method, and in the partial rulings that address the matters of life. Among that is His saying, exalted be He: ﴿and to make lawful for you some of what was forbidden to you...﴾ [Ali 'Imran: 50]

In the earlier nations, if impurity fell on a garment, they would cut off the place on which it fell. When Islam came, it lightened this hardship for people and prescribed that they wash it so that it becomes pure.

Since your community is one community, ﴿and I am your Lord, so fear Me﴾ [Al-Mu'minun: 52], meaning: fear God regarding this one community, and preserve its unity, and beware of what divides it of disputes over branches; if some disagree about them, they accuse the others of disbelief, because they want to seize for themselves a worldly authority from the all-encompassing religion.

And the Lord, blessed and exalted be He, says: ﴿Indeed, those who divide their religion and become sects, you have nothing to do with them in anything...﴾ [Al-An'am: 159]

So the matters that Allah has made firm in clear, decisive wording are principles on which there is no disagreement and in which there is no ijtihad (independent reasoning). As for the matters that He, glory be to Him, left to ijtihad, we must respect the ijtihad of others in them; otherwise, had the Truthful One wished, He would have made the whole matter firm, leaving no room for opinion or ijtihad.

The meaning of ﴿and I am your Lord...﴾ [Al-Mu'minun: 52] is: that among the gifts of My lordship is that I made for you firm matters and fixed beliefs, because disagreement over them corrupts society, and I left you other matters, which you may do or leave, each according to his ijtihad, because disagreement over them does not result in corruption of society. We have previously given examples of these matters.

As for His saying: ﴿so fear Me﴾ [Al-Mu'minun: 52], it means: by obeying the command. So whatever I have made firm, make firm, and whatever I have left to you as ijtihad, accept in it the ijtihad of others.

Yet have we truly heeded the word of God and obeyed it? He, glory be to Him, says:

﴿So they cut their affair among themselves into sects, each faction rejoicing in what it has.﴾

﴿Zuburan (sects)...﴾ [al-Mu'minun] means: separate pieces. From the same root is ﴿Bring me blocks of iron...﴾ [al-Kahf, 96].

﴿Each faction rejoicing in what it has﴾ [al-Mu'minun]: meaning, each group is zealous for its own opinion and rejoices in it, as if it alone is upon the truth and others upon falsehood. They want to have temporal authority among the people, and they present to them that they have brought what no one before them brought, and that they have noticed what the others neglected.

﴿In what they have...﴾ [al-Mu'minun]: that is, in the opinion they desire, not in the ruling that the Truth, glory be to Him and exalted, approves.

Among this is their saying that prayer in a mosque that has a grave or a shrine in it is invalid, and that this is shirk in worship, etc. Yet if the matter were as they say, let them demolish the grave in Medina.

It is incumbent upon those who stir up such disputes to understand matters in their correct manner, so that we do not become among those of whom God said:

﴿So they cut their affair among themselves into sects, each faction rejoicing in what it has.﴾ [al-Mu'minun].

Nothing has corrupted the reception of the religions that preceded Islam except disputes of this kind. Otherwise, every religion that preceded Islam, especially the religion of Moses and Jesus, gave glad tidings of Muhammad (ﷺ). They were People of the Book, possessors of revelation and connected to heaven, and they used to argue with the disbelievers, the idol-worshippers, saying: "The time of a prophet has drawn near who will appear among you; we will follow him and kill you with him, the killing of ʿAd and Iram."¹

Yet ﴿when there came to them what they recognised, they disbelieved in it...﴾ [al-Baqarah, 89]. Why? Because they wanted to keep their temporal authority.

How could they not deny the Messenger of God (ﷺ), when one of them² was preparing to install himself as king over Medina on the day the Messenger of God entered it, and so he spoiled what he intended?

¹ — From elders of the Ansar, who said: "We had dominated them by force for a long time in the Jahiliyyah, while we were people of shirk and they were People of the Book. They used to say: 'A prophet is about to be sent now; we will follow him, and his time has drawn near, and we will kill you with him, the killing of ʿAd and Iram.' So when God sent His Messenger from Quraysh and we followed him, they disbelieved in him." Mentioned by Ibn Kathir in his Tafsir (1/124), quoting Ibn Ishaq.

² — He is ʿAbd Allah ibn Ubayy ibn Salul, chief of the hypocrites in Medina, Abu al-Hubab from Khuza'ah; Salul was his grandmother on his father's side. He was the lord of the Khazraj in their final days of Jahiliyyah, and whenever a calamity befell the Muslims he rejoiced at them, and whenever he heard of an evil he spread it. He died in the year 9 AH. [al-A'lam of al-Zirikli, 4/65].

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1–53, fragments of 54–66) on surah 23, verse 54:

﴿So leave them in their confusion for a while.﴾ (54)

﴿So leave them..﴾ (54) [al-Mu'minun]: meaning, let them be. The Arabs did not use the past tense of these two verbs, so the present forms yadaʿu and yadhar appear in their place. This verb also occurs in His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And leave Me with those who deny, the people of luxury..﴾ (11) [al-Muzzammil].

And in His saying, exalted is He: ﴿So leave Me with whoever denies this statement..﴾ (44) [al-Qalam].

The meaning is: leave them to Me, for I Myself will take charge of their punishment and do with them as I will; or: leave them to do whatever they wish, so that they deserve the punishment and the torment descends upon them.

Al-ghamra (the flood, or overwhelming mass): the body of water that covers a man's height and prevents him from breathing, so that he has no hope of life remaining except to the extent of the air in his lungs. For this reason a person strives to train himself so that his lungs can expand to take in the greatest possible amount of air.

From this the word munafasa (rivalry, competition) is derived. Its origin is that two people dive under water so that each tests the other: which of them remains underwater for the longer period without breathing.

He, exalted is He, says: ﴿And for that let the competitors compete..﴾ (26) [al-Mutaffifin]. You can carry out this competition with yourself: take a deep breath and then count: one, two, and you will see the amount of air in your lungs.

So the meaning is: leave them in their folly and heedlessness, for their time will not be long, because they are like one whom the water has overwhelmed, whose breath is soon cut off and who departs from life. For this reason He, exalted is He, said after it: ﴿for a while (ḥattā ḥīn)﴾ (54) [al-Mu'minun]. Al-ḥīn is a period of time that may be long, as in His saying: ﴿It gives its produce every season by the permission of its Lord..﴾ (25) [Ibrahim].

It may also be short, as in His saying: ﴿So glorify Allah when you enter the evening and when you enter the morning..﴾ (17) [al-Rum]. It is as if Allah, exalted is He, expressed it by al-ghamra to indicate that their ḥīn will not be long.

Then the context moves on to address a matter that occupies many believers:

﴿Do they think that what We extend to them of wealth and children (55) is [as if] We were hastening for them in good things? Rather, they do not perceive (56)﴾:

This is a matter that has preoccupied many believers when they see disbelievers in God living in ease and luxury, with wealth and influence in their hands, while believers are poor. Perhaps some have doubted, and their faith has been shaken by these contradictions.

To these people we say: this was not the condition of the believers in the past. They ruled the world with their sciences and cultures, and their civilization flourished for a thousand years. When they abandoned their religion and their values, what they are in now befell them.

Others have outstripped us because they took up the means of this world, and it is incumbent upon us Muslims to take up these means as well, for they are a bounty of Lordship (rubūbiyyah) from which neither believer nor disbeliever is barred. Whoever does well with them obtains their fruit and takes their good.

He, glory be to Him, said: ﴿Whoever desires the tilth of the Hereafter, We increase him in his tilth; and whoever desires the tilth of this world, We give him of it, but he has no share in the Hereafter (20)﴾ [al-Shura].

The means are God's outstretched hand toward His creatures. Whoever pushes away the hand of God will inevitably be wretched in the journey of life.

The comfort of these people may be mere luxury that drags them into tyranny, as the Most High said: ﴿So when they forgot what they had been reminded of, We opened for them the gates of everything, until when they rejoiced in what they had been given, We seized them suddenly, and they were then in despair (44)﴾ [al-An'am].

Therefore, the Truth, blessed and exalted is He, addresses this issue here:

﴿Do they think that what We extend to them of wealth and children (55) is [as if] We were hastening for them in good things... (56)﴾ [al-Mu'minun]. Do they suppose this is good for them? No; rather it is respite and gradual entrapment so that they may increase in tyranny.

In another place He, glory be to Him, says: ﴿So let not their wealth and their children impress you; God only intends to punish them with them in this world... (85)﴾ [al-Tawbah].

And His saying, the Most High: ﴿Rather, they do not perceive... (56)﴾ [al-Mu'minun]: (bal) indicates a turning away from what precedes it and an affirmation of what follows it. It turns away from the matter of these people's luxury, because it is a temporary and passing blessing, and in reality it is a calamity for them, but they do not perceive it. They do not perceive that this blessing does not mean God's love for them or His pleasure with them, and they do not perceive the plot and the trap being laid for them.

We have previously explained that when God, the Most High, wishes to take vengeance on His enemy, He first extends to him, widens provision for him, and raises his station, until when He seizes him, the seizing is painful and severe.

And His saying, the Most High: ﴿We hasten for them in good things... (56)﴾ [al-Mu'minun]: the verb "al-musara'ah" (hastening) occurs in the Book of God with several meanings. Sometimes the verb takes "ilā" (to), as in: ﴿And hasten to forgiveness from your Lord... (133)﴾ [Al 'Imran], and sometimes it takes "fī" (in), as in: ﴿They hasten in good things... (61)﴾ [al-Mu'minun]. So what is the difference between the two meanings?

"Sāra'a ilā kadha" (he hastened toward such-and-such) is said when one is outside of it and wants to step toward it with quick steps. But if one is already within good and wants to ascend in it, one says "sāra'a fī al-khayrāt" (he hastened in good things). The first is addressed to one who has not entered the sphere of good, and the second to one who is enveloped in good and seeks to rise.

Then the context moves on to address a matter that occupies many believers:

﴿Do they think that what We extend to them of wealth and children (55) is [a means of] hastening good for them? Nay, they do not perceive (56).﴾

This is a matter that has occupied many believers when they see disbelievers in God living in comfort and luxury, with wealth and influence in their hands, while the believers are poor. Some may doubt and have their faith shaken by these contradictions.

We say to these people: This was not the condition of the believers in the past. They ruled the world with their sciences and cultures, and their civilization flourished for a thousand years. When they abandoned their religion and their values, what they are now experiencing befell them.

Others have surpassed us because they took up the means of this world, and it is incumbent upon us Muslims to take up these means too, for they are a gift of Lordship (rubūbiyyah) from which neither believer nor disbeliever is barred. Whoever does well with them obtains their fruit and takes their benefit.

He, glorified is He, says: ﴿Whoever desires the tillage of the Hereafter, We increase for him in his tillage; and whoever desires the tillage of this world, We give him from it, but he has no share in the Hereafter (20).﴾ [al-Shura]

And the means (asbāb) are the outstretched hand of God toward His creation. Whoever pushes away the hand of God will inevitably be wretched on the journey of life.

Perhaps the luxury of these people is merely opulence that drags them into tyranny, as the Most High said: ﴿So when they forgot what they had been reminded of, We opened for them the gates of everything, until when they rejoiced in what they had been given, We seized them suddenly, and they were then in despair (44).﴾ [al-An'am]

Therefore, here the Truth, blessed and exalted is He, addresses this issue:

﴿Do they think that what We extend to them of wealth and children (55) is [a means of] hastening good for them?.. (56)﴾ [al-Mu'minun]: Do they suppose that this is good for them? No; rather it is a respite and a gradual drawing-on, so that they may increase in tyranny.

In another place He, glorified is He, says: ﴿And let not their wealth and their children impress you; God only intends to punish them thereby in this world... (85)﴾ [al-Tawbah].

And His saying, the Most High: ﴿Nay, they do not perceive.. (56)﴾ [al-Mu'minun]: "Bal" (بل) indicates a turning away from what precedes it and affirmation of what follows it — a turning away from the matter of these people's luxury, because it is a temporary and passing blessing, which in reality is a calamity upon them, but they do not perceive. They do not perceive that this blessing does not mean God's love for them or His pleasure with them, and they do not perceive the scheme and the trap being prepared for them.

We have previously explained that when God, the Most High, wishes to take vengeance on His enemy, He first extends to him, widens his provision and elevates his station, until when He seizes him, the seizing is painful and severe.

And His saying, the Most High: ﴿We hasten for them in good things.. (56)﴾ [al-Mu'minun]: The root sāra'a (مسارعة, hastening) occurs in the Book of God with several meanings. Sometimes the verb takes ilā (إلى), as in: ﴿And hasten to forgiveness from your Lord.. (133)﴾ [Al 'Imran], and sometimes it takes fī (في), as in: ﴿They hasten in good things.. (61)﴾ [al-Mu'minun]. What is the difference between the two meanings?

Sāra'a ilā kadhā (سارع إلى كذا): when you are outside of it and want to step toward it with quick steps. But if you are already within good and want to ascend in it, you say sāra'a fī al-khayrāt (سارع في الخيرات). The first is addressed to one who has not entered the realm of good, and the second to one who is already enveloped in good and seeks to rise.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 23, verse 57:

﴿Indeed, those who are fearful of the awe of their Lord,﴾ :

Al-khashya (fear rooted in awe): it is the most intense fear. A person may fear something yet still keep hope of deliverance, expecting from the means at hand something that will rescue him and ease his fear. But when you fear God, it is a fear with no outlet for hope in it, and no gentle breeze of kindness blows through it to make you feel comforted.

The meaning of ﴿fearful﴾ [al-Mu'minun]: al-ishfaq (apprehensive dread) is also a kind of fear, and it is a fear that is praised, not blamed, because it is a fear that carries its bearer and urges him to avoid the causes of divine displeasure through righteous deeds. It is apprehension of a sin that deserves punishment, like the student who studies diligently out of fear of failing. So too is the state of the believer, who feels this fruitful, praiseworthy fear that leads him to take up the means of deliverance, and this is a sign of faith.

As for apprehension after the opportunity has been lost, which the Qur'an recounts of the criminals: ﴿And the Book will be placed, and you will see the criminals fearful of what is in it, and they will say, "Woe to us..."﴾ [al-Kahf, 49]: this is apprehension that brings no benefit, because it comes after the opportunity has been lost and the time for action has ended. The Resurrection has come, the books have been spread open, and there is no hope of deliverance at that point.

Then the Truth, glorified is He, says:

﴿And those who believe in the signs of their Lord (58), and those who do not associate anything with their Lord (59)﴾:

We notice in these verses that the Truth, glorified is He, speaks to us of apprehension and fear, then of belief in the signs of Allah, and finally of the matter of shirk (associating partners with Allah). You may ask: why did He not begin with a warning against shirk?

We say: because the shirk intended here is the hidden shirk (ash-shirk al-khafi) into which even the believer may fall, concerning which Allah said: ﴿And most of them do not believe in Allah except while they associate others with Him (106)﴾ [Yusuf]. So do not think that shirk is only that you make a partner for Allah, or that you prostrate to an idol. Among shirk is a hidden, subtle shirk that creeps into the heart and mingles with the deed, however believing its doer may be.

Therefore, the Prophet (ﷺ) teaches us good manners in this matter, and he says in his supplication: "O Allah, I seek Your forgiveness for every deed I intended for Your sake but in which there mingled with me that which was not for You" (1).

A person begins a deed and sincerely intends it for Allah, yet some show-off (riya') and the adornment of Satan creep into it. For this reason the Prophet (ﷺ) described hidden shirk as more hidden than the crawling of a black ant on a black stone in a dark night (2).

Moreover, major shirk (ash-shirk al-akbar) cannot be conceived from one whose attributes are the attributes mentioned above.

1 - Ibn Rajab al-Hanbali mentioned it in "Jami' al-Ulum wa al-Hikam" (p. 27), from the supplication of Mutarrif ibn Abd Allah, that he used to say: "O Allah, I seek Your forgiveness for that which I repented of to You and then returned to; and I seek Your forgiveness for what I pledged to You upon myself and then did not fulfil to You; and I seek Your forgiveness for what I claimed I intended for Your sake, but there mingled in my heart of it what You know."

2 - Ahmad related it in his Musnad (4/403) from the hadith of Abu Musa al-Ash'ari, may Allah be pleased with him, from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "O people, beware of this shirk, for it is more hidden than the crawling of the ant." Someone among those whom Allah willed said: "How can we guard against it, when it is more hidden than the crawling of the ant, O Messenger of Allah?" He said: "Say: O Allah, we seek refuge in You from associating anything with You knowingly, and we seek Your forgiveness for what we do not know."

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi (surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66)) on surah 23, verse 59:

﴿And those who believe in the signs of their Lord,﴾ (58) ﴿and those who do not associate anything with their Lord.﴾ (59):

We notice in these verses that God, glory be to Him, spoke to us of ishfaq (apprehensive fear) and khashya (awe), then of belief in the signs of God, and finally of the matter of shirk (association of partners with God). You may ask: why did He not begin with a warning against shirk?

We say: because the shirk intended here is the hidden shirk (al-shirk al-khafi) into which even the believer may fall, of which God said: ﴿And most of them do not believe in God without associating others with Him.﴾ (Yusuf, 106). So do not think that shirk is only that you make a partner for God, or that you prostrate to an idol. Among shirk is a hidden, subtle shirk that creeps into the heart and mingles with the deed, however faithful its doer may be.

Therefore, the Prophet (ﷺ) teaches us good manners regarding this matter, and he says in his supplication: "O God, I seek Your forgiveness for every deed I intended for Your sake which was mixed with something that was not for You" (1).

A person begins a deed and sincerely intends it for God, yet some ostentation (riya') and the adornment of Satan creep into it. For this reason the Prophet (ﷺ) described hidden shirk as more hidden than the crawling of a black ant on a black stone in a dark night (2).

Moreover, major shirk (al-shirk al-akbar) cannot be conceived from one who possesses the attributes mentioned earlier.

1 - Ibn Rajab al-Hanbali mentioned it in "Jami' al-'Ulum wa al-Hikam" (p. 27), from the supplication of Mutarrif ibn 'Abd Allah, that he used to say: "O God, I seek Your forgiveness for what I repented to You of and then returned to, and I seek Your forgiveness for what I pledged to You upon myself and then did not fulfil for You, and I seek Your forgiveness for what I claimed I intended for Your sake, yet there mingled with my heart from it what You know."

2 - Ahmad narrated it in his Musnad (4/403) from the hadith of Abu Musa al-Ash'ari, may Allah be pleased with him, from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "O people, beware of this shirk, for it is more hidden than the crawling of ants." Then a man whom God willed said to him: "And how can we guard against it, when it is more hidden than the crawling of ants, O Messenger of Allah?" He said: "Say: O God, we seek refuge in You from associating anything with You knowingly, and we seek Your forgiveness for what we do not know."

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 23, verse 60:

Then the Truth, glory be to Him, says:

﴿And those who give what they give while their hearts are fearful, because they are returning to their Lord.﴾ (23:60)

﴿Yu'tuna (they give)...﴾ (23:60): meaning wealth. Then He says ﴿ma atau (what they give)...﴾ (23:60): without setting any limit to it, neither a tenth nor half a tenth. God, glory be to Him, wants to open wide the scope for generosity and open-handedness of soul. Therefore ﴿ma atau⦆ came in this indefinite form, so that we do not assume it means zakat, and so that we know that God opens the field to benevolence (ihsan) and bounty. This is the station of ihsan (excellence in conduct) of which God, the Exalted, said:

﴿Indeed, the God-fearing will be in gardens and springs, taking what their Lord has given them. Indeed, they were before that doers of good (muhsinin).﴾ (51:15-16)

The muhsin (one who does good) is the one who binds himself to acts of obedience beyond what God has obliged him to, but of the same kind as what God has made obligatory upon him. If the obligation in fasting is the month of Ramadan, the muhsin fasts Ramadan and adds to it. Therefore you find the precision of the Qur'anic expression, where He says after it:

﴿They used to sleep little by night, and at the dawns they would seek forgiveness.﴾ (51:17-18)

These are matters beyond what God has obliged upon them. He has not asked you to stand in prayer all night without sleeping; rather, pray the night prayer ('isha') and sleep until dawn. This matter is clear in His saying after it:

﴿And in their wealth there is a right for the beggar and the deprived.﴾ (51:19)

He did not say "a known right (ma'lum)", because the verse does not speak of the known right, which is zakat, but of charity and voluntary giving beyond what God has obliged.

The indefiniteness in ﴿ma (what)...﴾ (23:60) also appears in God's saying:

﴿Then there covered them of the sea that which covered them.﴾ (20:78)

He did not specify the quantity of water that covered them, and left the matter indefinite so that the meaning would be more forceful, and so that imaginations would run in every direction regarding its terror.

But, since they have given and extended their hands to others in giving, why does He say ﴿and their hearts are fearful...﴾ (23:60)?

We say: because what counts is not merely the deed, but the acceptance of the deed. A deed is not accepted unless it is sincere for the sake of God's face, not mixed with showing off (riya') or seeking reputation. They therefore act and strive for sincerity and the causes of acceptance, and one of them gives charity in such a way that his left hand does not know what his right hand has spent. Yet, despite that, he fears non-acceptance, and this too is one of the signs of faith.

It is as if your Lord, mighty and majestic, is jealous over you lest you perform a deed for which you take no reward. For if you see people in some deed, God leaves you and them, and you take your recompense from them. This is then a wasted effort with no benefit, and this is a matter your Lord does not accept for you.

In the sacred hadith: "Sincerity is one of My secrets, which I have deposited in the heart of whomever of My servants I love; no angel gets to know it so as to record it, nor does any devil get to it so as to corrupt it."(2)

Al-wajal (fear): a compelled emotion and agitation that befalls the limb out of fear or dread. Fear (khawf) is something that frightens you; whereas khashyah (awe) is higher than fear, and it is that you fear the one who would inflict upon you a harm more severe than what you are in.

Some of the exegetes hold that the verse ﴿those who give what they give while their hearts are fearful...﴾ (23:60) was revealed concerning the man who steals, the man who commits adultery, and the man who drinks wine, but whose heart is fearful of meeting God and of His awe, so that there remains in him some remnant of faith and of shame before God, the Exalted. They said: 'Aisha, may God be pleased with her, understood this from the verse.(3)

But this understanding does not agree with His saying ﴿yu'tuna (they give)...﴾ (23:60), meaning: they give to others, so there is then a giver and a recipient. Had he intended theft, adultery and drinking wine, He would have said ya'tuna (they come to).

So the meaning is: they give others what is due to them of right, whether these rights are owed to God, such as zakat, expiations (kaffarat), vows (nudhur) and the prescribed punishments (hudud), or are connected to the servants, such as deposits, trusts, and justice in judging between them, etc. The believer discharges what is incumbent upon him of these rights, while his heart is fearful lest his deed lack sincerity and so not be accepted.

Then He, exalted, says: ﴿that they are returning to their Lord.﴾ (23:60) The believer discharges what is upon him, yet you see him fearful and anxious, because he is certain of returning to God and standing before Him, glory be to Him, and He is his Lord who will recompense him according to the measure of his sincerity. He also fears that his affair will be exposed if some showing off mixes with his deed, because his Lord is jealous and does not accept a partner in the deed, and He, glory be to Him, knows everything and reckons for the atoms of good and the atoms of evil.

There are deeds that outwardly are of the religion, but within them is some showing off, even if the person is unaware of it. Among these are the sayings: "I do this for God, then for you," or "I put my trust in God and in you," etc. These phrases and their like carry within them meanings of association (shirk) which we must keep God free of, so we should not link anyone with God, even unintentionally.

Therefore He, exalted, says: ﴿And most of them do not believe in God without associating others with Him.﴾ (12:106) On the Day of Resurrection, the people of sincerity will be reassured about their reward, while the people of association and showing off will be surprised by the presence of God, the Exalted, which had not been in their minds when they acted: ﴿And those who disbelieve, their deeds are like a mirage in a desert plain, which the thirsty one thinks is water, until, when he reaches it, he finds it to be nothing, and finds God with him, and He pays him his account in full.﴾ (24:39)

So then: since we shall be surprised by the presence of the Truth, and nothing but the Truth, let our deeds be for the Truth, and nothing for other than the Truth.

1 - From Aisha, may God be pleased with her, who said: I asked the Messenger of God (ﷺ) about this verse, ﴿And those who give what they give while their hearts are fearful...﴾ (23:60). Aisha said: "Are they those who drink wine and steal?" He said: "No, O daughter of the Truthful (al-Siddiq), but they are those who fast and give charity while fearing that it will not be accepted from them. Those are the ones who hasten to the good deeds." Narrated by Ahmad in his Musnad (6/159, 205), al-Tirmidhi in his Sunan (3175), and Ibn Majah in his Sunan (4198), and the wording is that of al-Tirmidhi.

2 - Mentioned by al-Ghazali in Ihya' 'Ulum al-Din (4/376). al-Iraqi said in his takhrij: "We narrated it in a part of al-Qazwini's musalsalat, a chain in which each narrator says: 'I asked so-and-so about sincerity,' and it comes through the narration of Ahmad ibn 'Ata' al-Hujaymi from 'Abd al-Wahid ibn Zayd from Hudhayfah from the Prophet (ﷺ) from Jibril from God. Both Ahmad ibn 'Ata' and 'Abd al-Wahid are abandoned (matruk), and they are both ascetics. It was also narrated by Abu al-Qasim al-Qushayri in al-Risala from a hadith of 'Ali ibn Abi Talib with a weak chain."

3 - The hadith of Aisha and her understanding of the verse was mentioned earlier, on page 10065.

﴿Those⦅...⦆ (61)﴾ [Al-Mu'minun]: that is, the people possessing the qualities mentioned earlier. ﴿They hasten toward good deeds...﴾ (61) [Al-Mu'minun]. There is a difference between *asra'a* and *sara'a*. *Asra'a* (to hasten) means that he himself hastens. *Sara'a* (to race, to vie) means that he sees another hastening, so he tries to outdo him. It therefore carries emphasis and an incentive to competition.

We have already clarified the difference between *sara'a ila* (to hasten toward) and *sara'a fi* (to hasten within). The meaning of ﴿They hasten toward good deeds...﴾ (61) [Al-Mu'minun] is that they are already within the sphere of good deeds and enveloped by it, yet they strive to rise and increase in good deeds in order to reach a higher rank.

As for the words of the Exalted, ﴿and they are foremost in them﴾ (61) [Al-Mu'minun]: Is the hastening the *'illah* (effective cause) of their having preceded others to good deeds, or is their precedence to good deeds the *'illah* of the hastening?

In the language, they speak of *sabab* (cause) and *musabbab* (effect), *shart* (condition) and *jaza'* (consequence), and *'illah* (effective cause) and *ma'lul* (effect). When you say, "If you study, you will succeed," then studying is the cause of success. But did studying precede success? No. Rather, success first existed in your mind: you pictured its benefits and how your standing would be among society and people. Thus a motive and a thought arose in you, and then you wished to realize it in fact, so you studied in order to reach that goal.

Therefore, in every condition and consequence: the consequence is a cause of the condition, and the condition is a cause of the consequence. The consequence is a cause of the condition as a motive for it, and the condition is a cause of the consequence in actuality and execution. Success arose first as a motive for studying, and studying came into being in reality so that success might be realized.

Likewise in ﴿They hasten toward good deeds and they are foremost in them﴾ (61) [Al-Mu'minun]: the meaning is that the intention is to precede, so they hasten; they hasten in reality in order to actually precede. Yet the precedence comes before the hastening, because the mind is first prepared for it and its realities are clear.

Therefore, condition and consequence, cause and effect, and *'illah* and *ma'lul* revolve between a motive, which is the consequence, and a reality, which is the condition.

As for the meaning of ﴿and they are foremost in them﴾ (61) [Al-Mu'minun]: that is, they are fit for this work and capable of it. This is like when you ask me for something and I say to you, "This is difficult," and you reply, "And you are capable of it."

Then Allah, glorified and exalted, says:

﴿And We do not burden any soul except within its capacity. And with Us is a record which speaks with truth, and they will not be wronged.﴾ (23:62)

After Allah, glorified is He, spoke of racing and competing (in good deeds), He made clear that these are according to one's capacity and ability, and that He, glorified is He, has only imposed upon you a duty after His knowledge of your power, and that you can bear this obligation. So beware of looking at the ruling and saying, "I can bear it or I cannot bear it." Rather, look at the obligation: as long as your Lord has imposed it on you, know that it is within your capacity. And when your Lord knows from you an inability, He lightens the obligation for you without you having to ask for that. The examples of the lightening of obligations are clear in the prayer, the fast, the pilgrimage, and so on.

Now we hear someone say: "In this age, capacity no longer bears these obligations; the time has changed, deeds and responsibilities have multiplied," and other such statements whose speakers intend to escape from the Law of Allah. We say: as long as the obligation remains, the capacity remains, and Allah, the Exalted, knows best the capacity and abilities of His creation.

So: I look first at the obligation, then I judge the capacity from the obligation, and I do not judge the obligation from the capacity.

Then He, glorified is He, says: ﴿And with Us is a record which speaks with truth, and they will not be wronged.﴾ (23:62). What is meant here is the record of our deeds(1) in which everything that "the hands have sent forward" is recorded. But: what is the wisdom behind recording deeds? And do the servants lie to their Lord, Mighty and Majestic, regarding what has been recorded against them?

They said: the wisdom behind recording deeds is that it be a proof against its owner, and so that he knows that Allah has not wronged him in anything. Therefore his Lord will say to him: ﴿Read your record...﴾ (17:14), meaning: by yourself, so that the proof is established against you and you have no objection.

Then He said after it: ﴿and they will not be wronged﴾ (23:62), because wronging is not conceivable from Allah, the Exalted. Wronging results from need, and you wrong another when you want to benefit from the effect of another's good beyond what you have. So wronging is the result of need, whereas Allah is the Giver, the Self-Sufficient who has no need of anyone. Why would He wrong?

Likewise, the weak may wrong others to take what is in another's hand to satisfy his need or desire; and had he been strong, he would have sufficed himself with his own effort.

(1) Al-Qurtubi in his tafsir (6/4667) mentioned other opinions regarding what is meant by "the record" in the verse, saying: "It was said: it refers to the Preserved Tablet (al-Lawh al-Mahfuz), in which everything has been recorded, so they do not transgress that. It was said: the indication in His words ﴿And with Us is a record...﴾ (23:62) is the Qur'an. Allah knows best, and each is possible, and the first is more apparent." He means that it is the record counting the deeds of the servants, which is what Fadilat al-Shaykh al-Sha'rawi, may Allah have mercy on him, held.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 23, verse 63:

Then the Truth, glory be to Him, says:

﴿Nay, their hearts are in confusion about this, and they have deeds other than that which they are doing.﴾ (23:63)

﴿Bal (nay).. (63)﴾ [al-Mu'minun]: a particle indicating a turning away from the preceding speech and the affirmation of the judgment for what follows it. Al-ghamrah (the overwhelming flood), as we have said, is the mass of water that rises above a person's height until it prevents him from breathing and deprives him of air, and this is the first of the foundations of life.

A person can endure without food for a month, and can endure without water from three days up to ten. But he cannot endure without breath beyond what the chest holds of air. If your lungs are sound, they can expand to take in the largest quantity of air, and you can bear not breathing for a longer period. But if the lungs are diseased, they do not expand to hold a large quantity, and the air soon runs out and the person dies.

From breathing (tanaffus) came competition (munafasah), as in His saying: ﴿And for that let the competitors compete.﴾ (83:26) [al-Mutaffifin]. Then the word was used for every deed in which you compete with others, because air is the essential element of life.

Therefore, when the Creator, the Mighty and Majestic, created this human structure, He made for it a unique system regarding its fuel and its nourishment, unlike the craftsmanship of human beings. If you deprive a car of petrol, for example, it stops. But the craftsmanship of the Creator, the Mighty and Majestic, is that the body takes its need of food and water, then stores the remainder for the time of need. The Truth, glory be to Him, knows your desire and your love for food and drink, and that you take from them beyond your need, so if food is absent from you, your body nourishes itself from this divine store.

Therefore, we see some people, when food is delayed for them, say: "My soul has been turned away from eating," while in reality he has eaten, and nourished himself from the store of food and drink in his body.

From the wisdom of God is that surplus food is stored in one form, namely fat, which transforms automatically into any other element the body needs. When the fat is finished, the body feeds on the flesh and muscles, then on the bones, which are the last store of sustenance in the human body. Therefore, in the story of Zakariyya, peace be upon him, it came: ﴿He said: "My Lord, indeed my bones have weakened and my head has glistened with grey, and I have never been, in my supplication to You, my Lord, unblessed."﴾ (19:4) [Maryam].

As for air, it has no store except what the lung can hold. When the air is exhausted from it by inhalation and exhalation, there is no remedy for it. And from the mercy of God toward His servants is that He has not made air the possession of anyone. Food may be possessed, and perhaps water too, but the air that a person needs with every breath, God has made the property of all, so that no one may prevent it from another, because you cannot devise a way to obtain it as you devise ways to obtain food and drink. And if the Owner of the air were angry with you, you would die before He became pleased with you.

We note here that the overwhelming flood does not encompass their concern; rather it encompasses their hearts: ﴿Nay, their hearts are in confusion..﴾ (23:63) [al-Mu'minun]. This is a greater trial, because the heart is the place where the perceptions that the intellect takes are gathered, which it distinguishes among, chooses from, and weighs. Then these perceptions turn into beliefs that settle in the heart, and by their guidance one walks in the movement of life.

Therefore, if the heart itself is in the flood, the calamity is more severe and the affliction greater, because it is the repository of the beliefs and principles that illuminate the path for you.

The heart is the place of God's regard toward His servants. Therefore He says: ﴿And We have certainly created for Hell many of the jinn and mankind; they have hearts with which they do not understand..﴾ (7:179) [al-A'raf].

And He said: ﴿God has set a seal upon their hearts..﴾ (2:7) [al-Baqarah]: because they loved disbelief and were at ease with it, and because He, glory be to Him, is the Lord who manages the lordship over creation, giving them what they desire even if it is disbelief. Therefore He sealed their hearts so that faith does not enter them and disbelief does not leave them, because they had become enamoured of disbelief and loved it.

Likewise, we say to those people who are afflicted in a precious or dear one, so they grieve over him, exaggerate in holding funeral gatherings and mourning tents, and observe the commemoration of the Thursday and the fortieth day and others; and perhaps the son was undutiful to his parents during their lifetime, but when his father or mother dies, he holds funerals and occupies the people, and he is as the poet said: "Do not mourn me after death, when in my life you did not bring me provision." Or the mother who has lost her only son, for example, so she lives grieved and troubled, as if she had fallen in love with sorrow and loved it. We warn these people and advise every grieving person to close the door of sorrow with the nails of contentment and submission, for sorrow, if it sees its door ajar, enters and remains with you and clings to you.

We have already explained that the Truth, glory be to Him, does not lift an affliction from His servant until he is content with it. And for us the example in this matter is our father Ibrahim, peace be upon him, when his Lord tested him with the slaughter of his son in a vision he saw, which he took as a command. He was content with God's decree and submitted to His command. Then he informed his son, his only one, of this vision so that he would not deprive him of this reward nor take him unawares, so that his heart would not change toward him:

﴿So when they both submitted and he put him down upon his forehead (1), We called to him, "O Ibrahim, you have fulfilled the vision." Indeed, thus do We reward the doers of good. Indeed, this was the clear trial. And We ransomed him with a great sacrifice.﴾ (37:103-107) [al-Saffat].

So after Ibrahim and his son were content with God's decree, God lifted the affliction from them, and the ransom came from God for Isma'il. Moreover, He increased it by giving them the good news of another son, Ishaq, and after Ishaq, Ya'qub: successive generations came as a bounty from God and a reward for contentment with His decree and destiny. How well the poet said in this situation (2): "Submit to your Lord's judgment, for in a wisdom He decrees, until you rest and profit.
