So: light is necessary so that the movement of life and the striving in the earth's expanses may be accomplished, and likewise darkness is necessary to prevent radiation from reaching the body, so that it may rest from the toil of work. Modern science has established the danger of radiations to human health.

Therefore He, exalted, says: ﴿and His is the alternation of the night and the day..﴾ (80) [al-Mu'minun]: He made them alternate and succeed one another so that each may perform its function in the universe. He, exalted, says: ﴿By the night when it covers (1), and the day when it brightens (2)﴾ [al-Layl]. Since each of them has its task, beware of turning night into day or day into night, for by doing so you oppose the nature upon which Allah created you. Look at those who follow this course: they stay up through the night until dawn and sleep through the day until sunset, and how much corruption they have caused in the movement of life. The student sleeps during the lesson, and the worker sleeps and falls short in performing his work.

The Prophet (ﷺ) alerted us to this matter in his saying: "...Extinguish the lamps when you go to sleep" (1), because the body does not take its rest, nor become calm, except in darkness, so that the person becomes strong, rested and energetic. And read the words of Allah, exalted: ﴿And We made the night a covering (10), and We made the day for livelihood (11)﴾ [an-Naba'].

It is part of the precision of the Qur'anic expression that it takes into account those who work at night, whose nature of work requires staying awake, such as policemen, bakery workers and others. So He, exalted, says: ﴿And among His signs is your sleep by night and day..﴾ (23) [ar-Rum]. The night is the basis, and the day is for such people who serve society at night; therefore they should make a artificial night out of the day, closing the windows and sleeping in a quiet place, so that the body may take its share of rest and calm.

So: the night and the day are not opposites; rather they are complementary creations, not contrary to one another, and they are like the male and the female, each completing the other, not as some claim, that they are opposed and contrasting. Therefore, after the Almighty swore by the night when it covers, and by the day when it brightens, He said: ﴿And by Him who created the male and the female (3), indeed your efforts are diverse (4)﴾ [al-Layl]. So the night and the day are like the male and the female, each having a task in the movement of life.

The alternation of night and day is in terms of light and darkness, and length and shortness, and in the difference of places. The night does not embrace the whole universe, nor does the day; so when it is night for you, it is day for another, as He, exalted, says: ﴿He causes the night to enter into the day and causes the day to enter into the night..﴾ (13) [Fatir].

From this results the multiplicity of easts and wests according to the multiplicity of places, such that every east has a corresponding west and every west has a corresponding east, to the extent that they have said: a night and a day arise in each one of a millionth of a second.

From this, as we have said, results the continual remembrance of Allah throughout the whole time, such that the call to prayer does not end, and prayer in the universe does not cease for a single moment: you are praying Maghrib while another is praying 'Isha', and so on. So the Almighty wants to be mentioned throughout the whole universe at all times of prayer at every moment.

Indeed one of the Sufis and people of gnosis, addressing time, says: "O time, and in you is all time." That is: O noon, in you is 'asr, maghrib, 'isha' and fajr, but with others.

From the alternation of night and day there also arises the hot summer and the cold winter. The Almighty imposed on all His servants one single obligation, such as the Hajj for example, and tied all the acts of worship to the Hijri calendar. Summer and winter revolve through the year, and this becomes clear if you compare the Hijri and Gregorian calendars. Thus whoever finds the Hajj unsuitable in summer performs it in winter, because the difference of the lunar reckoning colours the whole year with all kinds of weather.

Therefore they said: the Night of Power revolves through the whole year, because the twenty-seventh of Ramadan falls sometimes on the first of January, sometimes on the second, sometimes on the third, and so on.

From the alternation of night and day is also that they succeed each other, as He, exalted, says: ﴿And it is He who made the night and the day succeed each other for whoever wishes to remember or wishes to be grateful (62)﴾ [al-Furqan].

We see the night succeeding the day and the day succeeding the night. But judge the matter in all its stages of time: since the Almighty made the night and the day succeed one another, this must be from the beginning of their creation. For if the night existed first and then the day, the night would not be a successor, because nothing preceded it. This means that they were created together, and when time revolved, each succeeded the other. This cannot occur except if the earth is spherical, such that night and day are together at one time: whoever faces the sun is in day, and whoever faces the darkness is in night.

Then He, glory be to Him, says: ﴿Will you not then use your reason? (80)﴾ [al-Mu'minun]: because these matters were especially something you ought to understand, and the differences of times were formerly based on reasoning; but now they are based on transmission, since distances have drawn close, and we know the exact time difference between ourselves and all parts of the world.

Likewise, people in the past denied the theory that the earth is spherical, and even after photographs were taken that showed its roundness, some of our thinkers still denied it. We say: why do we take this stance against established theories which our Qur'an has preceded in stating? And why do we give others the impression that our religion neglects these matters, when it has preceded all these discoveries?

If you reflect upon His saying: ﴿And it is He who spread out the earth..﴾ (3) [ar-Ra'd], you will find in it conclusive proof of the truth of this theory, for the spread-out earth is that which has no edge, and this can only be if the earth is spherical, such that you travel over it and find no end until you reach the place from which you began. Had the earth been of any shape other than spherical, such as square or rectangular, it would have had an end. But the instruments that would clarify and show this truth were not available to us in the past.

So: the Almighty, in His saying: ﴿Will you not then use your reason? (80)﴾ [al-Mu'minun], alerts us to the necessity of exercising our minds in cosmic matters, for these will spare us much on the path to Allah, Exalted is He. Why does a person use his mind and show ingenuity, for instance, in committing crimes, arranging and planning them? But Allah, exalted, lies in wait for him and casts him into a slip, leaving behind him an outlet for proving his crime and a gap through which he is reached. Therefore the men of law say: there is no perfect crime, and this is the task of the judge or investigator who interrogates the criminal to reach this gap.

It is as if the Almighty, glory be to Him, says: You used your mind for what was not appropriate and enslaved it to your soul's desires, so I must cast you into a slip in which your affair is exposed. If I conceal it for you once, beware of persisting, or thinking that you have escaped by your mind and your arrangement; otherwise I will seize you even with a crime you did not commit, for you cannot arrange with your mind against Allah, and His justice, glory be to Him, is above every arrangement.

It is like a person who is publicly disgraced for something of which he is innocent, and harm and injury befall him because of this false condemnation; then the justice of heaven comes, and Allah conceals from him a scandal he committed in recompense for what befell him in the first. This is a matter that only the Lord does.

When the Almighty, glory be to Him, alerts the mind and stirs it, saying: reflect, ponder, use your reason, so that it may comprehend the cosmic things around it, this is evidence that He, glory be to Him, is confident of His workmanship and the originality of His creation. Therefore He stirs minds to examine and reflect upon this workmanship.

We observe this matter in men who display their craftsmanship: the one who perfects his craft displays it and invites you to test it and make sure of its quality, unlike the poor craft which its maker wraps up for you and diverts you from examining, so that you will not discover its defect.

So when your Lord alerts you to reflect upon His workmanship, you must understand the purpose of this stirring, so that you may reach what He, exalted, wills for you.

1 - Related by al-Bukhari in his Sahih (5624) and Ahmad in his Musnad (3/388), from the hadith of Jabir ibn 'Abd Allah; the wording is al-Bukhari's.

Then the Truth, glory be to Him, says:

﴿Rather, they said the like of what the ancients said.﴾ (81)

That is: they did not take heed from all these signs; rather, they said the like of what the ancients said:

﴿They said, "When we have died and become dust and bones, shall we indeed be raised up again?"﴾ (82)

They said, "When we have died and become dust and bones, will we indeed be resurrected?"

Whether this was their own statement or the statement of their predecessors from earlier generations, doubt about the resurrection after death was present among those who lived at the time of the Muhammadan call, and all of their speech leads to that. They were astonished at the occurrence of this matter.

For this reason one of them said: ﴿And he presents to Us an example and forgets his own creation. He says, "Who will give life to bones when they are decayed?" Say, "He will give them life who produced them the first time, and He is Knowing of all creation."﴾ [Ya-Sin]

﴿Indeed, we and our fathers were promised this before. This is nothing but the fables of the ancients.﴾ (83)

Do you think that when Allah, exalted is He, promised you death and then resurrection, this would happen in this world? That is why you say: "We were promised this before, and it did not happen." Many of us have died and did not return or get resurrected. So who told you that you will die today and be resurrected tomorrow?

Resurrection will not take place until all creation has died, and then they will all be resurrected at once.

So this speech of theirs is merely ﴿sophistry﴾ (sofastah, specious argument) and disputation with no meaning.

As for the word ﴿promised﴾ (waʿadnā) in ﴿Indeed, we were promised...﴾ (83) [al-Muʾminūn], it means the resurrection. A promise (waʿd) is customarily of good, just as a threat (waʿīd) is of evil, as in the words of the poet:

"Indeed, when I threaten him or promise him, I break my threat and I fulfil my promise."

That is: he is a noble man who abandons the evil he threatened and does the good he promised. The scholars have said that one may be used in place of the other.

But does promising the disbelievers resurrection and what follows of punishment and retribution count as a promise? They said: Yes. This evil and this punishment that awaits them is considered a promise of good, because it warns them and draws their attention to its danger so that they do not fall into it. So it is good for them now, since it cautions them, just as you warn your son against failing if he neglects his lessons.

Also in this matter is what we pointed out regarding the repetition of His words, exalted is He: ﴿So which of the favours of your Lord will you two deny?﴾ (13) [al-Raḥmān], in Surat al-Raḥmān. It came after the mention of Allah's blessings as a reproach to whoever denies these blessings or rejects them, and it was repeated with every blessing to emphasise this reproach. But what is remarkable is that this verse is mentioned even after the punishments, as in His words, exalted is He:

﴿There will be sent against you both a flame of fire and molten brass, and you will not be victorious. So which of the favours of your Lord will you two deny?﴾ (35–36) [al-Raḥmān].

Is there any blessing in fire and flame? We say: Yes, there is a blessing in it, because it is advice to you before you fall into this fate, and a warning to you at a time when you can still correct yourself, so that you may review yourself.

As for their words: ﴿This is nothing but the fables of the ancients﴾ (83) [al-Muʾminūn], and ﴿This is...﴾ (83), the meaning is: "What is this?" Asāṭīr (fables) is the plural of ustūra (asṭūrah), like aʿājīb (marvels) and aʿjūbah (a marvel). Some say asāṭīr is the plural of saṭr (line), with asṭār, and then asāṭīr, like shakl (form) and ashkāl (forms), so it is a plural of a plural. Whether it is the plural of ustūrah or of saṭr, the meaning does not differ, because a written thing may be regarded by people as superstition and speech with no meaning.

Asāṭīr is false speech with no basis. Speech is not called an ustūrah unless its time has come and it has not occurred. So you may say that the resurrection of which you speak is ﴿fables of the ancients﴾ (83) [al-Muʾminūn]: its time has not yet come, since all creation has not yet died so that they may be resurrected. You have erred in timing and thought that you would die and be resurrected in this world just like that, before witnesses, while people are still in the expanse of this world.

Then: the resurrection is not as you say; rather it is true, but you have not applied to it the appropriate word. Therefore He directs to them these questions of affirmation which establish the proof against them:

﴿Say: "To whom belongs the earth and whoever is in it, if you should know?"﴾ (23:84)

It comes in the question with "in" (in), the conditional particle, which indicates doubt as to whether they have knowledge.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 23, verse 85:

﴿They will say, "To Allah." Say, "Will you not then remember?"﴾ :

Since you have acknowledged that the earth and whoever is in it belong to Allah, ﴿Will you not then remember?﴾ [al-Mu'minun]: meaning, what has turned you away from the Owner of the earth and its Creator?

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 23, verse 86:

Then the Truthful (al-Haqq) — glorified is He — says:

﴿Say: Who is the Lord of the seven heavens and the Lord of the Mighty Throne?﴾

We note that they did not dispute this matter, and they did not say, for example, that there is only one heaven, the one we see. This indicates that it was not something they denied; the earlier prophets must have informed them of the report of the heavens, that they are seven heavens, and it became for them a rational matter they knew. Otherwise they could have objected, since they see only one heaven. So: they did not dispute this subject.

And His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And the Lord of the Mighty Throne﴾ [al-Mu'minun]: the Throne (al-'Arsh) is a great creation whose true nature none knows except God, who said concerning it: ﴿Then He established Himself upon the Throne﴾ [al-A'raf: 54], and said: ﴿And His Throne was upon the water﴾ [Hud: 7].

No one has seen the Throne; rather, its Lord who created it informed about it, saying: "For Me is such-and-such, and for Me is such-and-such." It suffices that God, exalted is He, described it as great. Also in this, they did not dispute with the Messenger of God, nor did they say, "We have not seen the Throne," which indicates that they had a store of the heritage of the earlier prophets, which passed to them as one of the natural inclinations of human creation, through hearing from those present.

The Throne is also described as great among humans. In the story of Solomon and the Queen of Sheba, the hoopoe said: ﴿And she has a mighty throne﴾ [al-Naml: 23]. This is because the throne is a symbol of the stability of rule and the settling of authority for a king who is not disputed in his kingship by anyone, and whom no enemy assails for it. Therefore, when Solomon, peace be upon him, first spoke about her affair, he said: ﴿Which of you will bring me her throne?﴾ [al-Naml: 38]. It is as though he wished to strip her first of the symbol of greatness, security, safety and stability in her rule.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1–53, fragments of 54–66) on surah 23, verse 87:

Then the Truth, glorified is He, says:

﴿They will say, "To Allah." Say, "Then will you not fear Him?"﴾ (87):

Since the matter is so, and since you acknowledge that to Allah belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth, and that He is Lord of the Mighty Throne, why do you not fear this God? Why do you rebel against His method? This whole universe, with everything in it, was created for your service. Does this not draw your attention to the Maker, the Bestower of favours?

Therefore, He, exalted is He, says in the sacred hadith: "O son of Adam, I created all things for your sake, and I created you for My sake, so do not busy yourself with what is for you in place of that for which you were made." (1) That is: do not let the blessing distract you from the Bestower. The servant must first look to his Creator and Owner, so that he renders what is due to Him, and then look to what he himself possesses.

As for the meaning of ﴿Then will you not fear Him?﴾ [al-Mu'minun]: taqwa (God-consciousness, fear of Allah) is that you place between yourself and the attributes of majesty of Allah a shield (wiqayah). We have previously said: among the wondrous verses of the Qur'an is that it says once "Fear Allah" (ittaqu Allah) and once "Fear the Fire" (ittaqu al-nar), and there is no contradiction in it, as some suppose; rather the meaning is one. For the Fire is among the hosts of Allah and among the attributes of His majesty. So the intended meaning is: fear the punishment of Allah, and fear the attributes of subjugation and might by placing between yourself and them a shield.

1 – Ibn Kathir cited in his tafsir (4/238): "It is reported in some divine books: Allah, the Exalted, says: 'O son of Adam, I created you for My worship, so do not play; and I have undertaken your provision, so do not toil. So seek Me and you will find Me. For if you find Me, you have found everything, and if you miss Me, you have missed everything, and I am more beloved to you than everything.'"

Then the Truth, blessed and exalted, says:

﴿Say: "In whose hand is the dominion (malakut) of all things, who protects, and against whom there is no protection, if you know?"﴾ [23:88]

The meaning of "in whose hand" (bi-yadihi): it indicates control over a thing, as you say, "This matter is in my hand," meaning it is within my capacity and disposal, and I turn it however I wish. "Dominion of all things" (malakut kull shay'): the root m-l-k gives rise to mulk, to malk, and to malakut.

Al-mulk (dominion) is what you own, so that even if you have nothing but one garment, it is your mulk. As for malk, it means that you possess one who possesses, and this is apparent. As for malakut, it refers to the created things that your senses do not perceive and about which you can know nothing except through the information of their Creator. A human being does not see everything in the universe; rather, within his own self and being there are things he does not know. All of this belongs to the realm of malakut.

Indeed, a person does not even see the apparent, perceptible dominion, for he sees only as far as his gaze extends, and what lies beyond this range he does not see, though another may see it. This dominion that you do not see can enter the circle of malakut in its broad sense.

So, malakut is applied to things that are hidden and which no one sees, or to things that one person sees and another does not.

When a person goes deep in the worship of God and in obeying Him, there is poured upon him from the manifestations (tajalliyat), and He gives him from this malakut a direct gift, as He said: ﴿from Our presence﴾ [4:27].

Do you not see that Abraham, peace be upon him, was described by his Lord: ﴿And Abraham, who fulfilled [his covenant]﴾ [53:37], and He said of him: ﴿And when Abraham was tried by his Lord with words, and he fulfilled them﴾ [2:124]. That is: he discharged what was due to God with precision and in the most perfect manner. Therefore his Lord entrusted him to be an imam for the people: ﴿He said, "Indeed, I will make you an imam for the people"﴾ [2:124].

When Abraham perfected what was between him and his Lord and reached this station, his Lord said of him: ﴿And thus did We show Abraham the malakut of the heavens and the earth﴾ [6:75].

Because he excelled in the first, he was elevated to a higher one. It is like a man who enters your house and sees the blessings you have, and he rejoices in what you have, and says: "Mashallah, blessed is Allah," and prays for you to be increased. When you see that from him, you say to him: "Then come, let me show you what is greater."

Likewise the righteous servant who worshipped God and drew near to Him through the method of Moses, peace be upon them both: when he remained steadfast upon this method and went deep in the worship and obedience of God, God gave him of His knowledge that is from Him (ladunni), without intermediary and without a messenger, to the extent that he became a teacher to Moses, peace be upon him.

Then He, glorified is He, says: ﴿and He protects, and against Him no protection is given﴾ [23:88]. Yujir: you say, "He sought protection from so-and-so, and he granted him protection," meaning he sought help from him and he helped him. Among its uses is His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And indeed, I am a protector for you﴾ [8:48]. A person does not seek protection from another except when his strength is too weak to defend him, so he takes refuge in a strong one who protects him and defends him.

Thus this matter has three elements: the mujir (protector), who accepts to aid you, embrace you and defend you; the mujar (one protected), who is the weak one seeking protection; and the mujar 'alayhi (one against whom protection is sought), who is the strong one who wishes to seize. It is well known that the Messenger of God (ﷺ), on his journey to Ta'if, after what they did to him (ﷺ), sought protection and entered under the protection of an unbeliever.

So the Truth, glorified and exalted, protects whoever seeks His protection, and aids whoever calls upon Him for help, but ﴿against Him no protection is given﴾ [23:88]: because the one who protects you only protects you from one who is equal to him in strength, so he can prevent you from him and shield you from his seizure. Then who can protect you from God? And who can protect you if God is the one seeking you?

For this reason, He, glorified is He, says regarding the son of Noah: ﴿He said, "There is no protector today from the command of God, except for whom He has mercy"﴾ [11:43]. So God, mighty and majestic, grants protection in everything, and whoever begins his day and ends it in the protection of his Lord has nothing to fear.

Notice here the relationship between the beginning of this verse and its end: God, in His hand and under His control, is all things, and the affair is entirely His. So beware lest you think you escape His grip by the blessing He has given you, for He, glorified is He, is able to strip it from you, and at that time no one will protect you, no helper will aid you against God, and no protector will shield you from God.

Then read His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Say: "O Allah, Owner of sovereignty, You give sovereignty to whom You will and take sovereignty away from whom You will. You honor whom You will and You humble whom You will. In Your hand is all good. Indeed, You are over all things competent"﴾ [3:26].

And here too He, glorified is He, says: ﴿if you know﴾ [23:88]: that is, if you have knowledge of this matter, and it has reached you and you have witnessed it.

Then Allah, glory be to Him, says about them:

﴿They will say, "To Allah." Say, "Then how are you deluded?"﴾ (89)

In this verse too they say "To Allah," because it is a tangible reality that cannot be denied. And since the matter is so, ﴿then how are you deluded?﴾ (89): how are you bewitched, or how have you been turned away from this reality and diverted to this false speech?

These are three matters that came in the form of a question, because of how clearly you acknowledge faith in the Supreme Being, the clear proofs of the inimitability of the message from Allah, and the clear signs in the signs of the method (manhaj). Allah, the Exalted, wanted the speech to come from them and by their own acknowledgment against themselves, so that it would be a proof and a witness of truth against them.

It is well known that acknowledgment (iqrar) is the master of proofs. Therefore He asked them:

﴿Say, "To whom belongs the earth and whoever is in it?"﴾ (84)

﴿And say, "Who is the Lord of the seven heavens and the Lord of the Great Throne?"﴾ (86)

﴿Say, "In whose hand is the dominion of all things?"﴾ (88)

And they say in all of this, "To Allah." So what then remains for you? What prevented you from being mindful of Him whom you believe to be the owner of the earth and the heavens and in whose hand is everything? It is nothing but arrogance, obstinacy and insolence. Otherwise, what does the word "Allah" that you pronounce mean?

You know Allah, and you know the meaning of this word, because the meaning of a word precedes its existence in human language. Language is customarily words placed to signify meanings: the meaning exists first, then we assign to it the word that signifies it. Since the word "Allah" circulates on your tongues, you must know its referent, and it is a linguistic matter you have already settled. Otherwise, a non-existent thing has no name. Take the television, for example: what was its name before it was invented? It had no name, because it had no meaning; when it came into existence, a name was given to it.

Since the tongues revolve around the word "Allah," this means that He, may He be exalted, existed before the existence of the name. So the matter is, then, a proof against you.

Therefore, the Truth, glory be to Him and exalted, presented these matters in the form of a question in order to extract their acknowledgment of them, just as if a person denied your favour to him. If you said to him, as a statement of information, "I have done for you such and such," the statement may be true or false, and he may admit or deny it.

But when you say to him, as a question, "Did I not do for you such and such?", he has no recourse but to acknowledge it, and he speaks the truth and the reality to you, and through his acknowledgment you reach what testimony or evidence would not achieve.

1 - Al-Qurtubi said in his tafsir (6/4679): "That is: how are you deceived and turned away from obeying Him and affirming His oneness? Or: how does it occur to you that you should not associate with Him what neither harms nor benefits?"..

Then the Truthful Lord says:

﴿Nay, We have brought them the truth, and indeed they are liars.﴾ (23:90)

That is, let me tell you about their affair, and why they rejected the truth and did not speak it. They deny the truth because they are liars, and they want to establish that what they are upon is a normal matter. Why? Because they profit from deviation and from falsehood. Therefore they stand against the message that came to correct the balance and to eliminate deviation and falsehood, and they resort to denying it and turning people away from it, so that they themselves may continue to benefit from falsehood.

So reflect: why do people lie? They lie because they profit from lying, while truthfulness wearies them and constricts them.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 23, verse 91:

Then the Truth, glory be to Him, says:

﴿Allah has not taken any son, nor was there any god with Him. Otherwise, each god would have taken away what he created, and some would have overcome others. Glory be to Allah above what they describe.﴾ (23:91):

Would that the matter had stopped with them at mere disbelief in Allah! Rather, it went further, to their describing Allah, exalted is He, with attributes that are not fitting. Since Allah, exalted is He, negates from Himself the taking of a son, saying ﴿Allah has not taken any son﴾ (23:91) [al-Mu'minun], then they must have said: Allah has taken a son. So they advanced in their wickedness and transgression, and became bold even against the sublime station of might.

We say first: What is a son (walad)? The son is what a human begets, whether male or female. We have heard these people say: Jesus is the son of Allah, and Ezra is the son of Allah, and they said of the angels: they are the daughters of Allah. Allah, exalted is He, said ﴿Allah has not taken any son﴾ (23:91) [al-Mu'minun], so as to include sons and daughters.

The meaning of ﴿taken a son﴾ (23:91) [al-Mu'minun] is: Allah, exalted is He, existed, then He took for Himself a son. Taking a son is therefore something new, and this means that a period passed in which Allah had not taken a son for Himself. So we ask: What has the existence of a son added to Allah's dominion? Have the heavens become eight? Has another sun or moon been added to the universe? The universe is as Allah created it, and He placed in it its necessities, its roots and its branches; nothing has been added to it. So taking a son is then vain, bringing nothing into being.

They say: Allah took a son so that His creation would be comforted by the presence of His son and something of his fragrance among the creatures. They said this at the council of (Nicaea), as if he held, in their view, the station of divinity. But how long did he remain among you? Christ remained on earth about thirty-odd years before he was raised. How then is the comfort of his company denied to those who came before his birth, peace be upon him? And how is it denied to those who came after him?

Does this not contradict the justice of lordship, since all creation is the creation of Allah, and they are equal before Him?

Some of them say: He came to remove sin, but sin remained on earth after he did what he did. So all these are feeble proofs.

If we discuss this matter in a logical and philosophical manner: Why does a person take a son? A person takes a son because he loves life, and his death cuts this life short, so he wants a son to be an extension of his life, and to secure the continuation of his memory through a generation after him. If the son has a son, he secures two generations. Therefore they say: "Dearer than a son is a son's son." But which memory is this to which they cling? The true memory is what you leave behind of righteous deeds that precede you before Allah.

The Truth, glory be to Him, has no need of a memory after Him, because He is everlasting and does not die, so this matter is impermissible with respect to Him.

A son may also be taken to be a support and helper for his father when he grows old and his strength weakens. Therefore they say: "The best marriage is early marriage, because it helps you beget a father who will sustain you in the childhood of your old age, for you beget a child while you are young, and he accompanies you for the longest span of time, and your eye is comforted by him, unlike one who begets in old age." Hence the phrase "a father who will sustain you in the childhood of your old age," and it did not say "a son," because in that state you need the tenderness of a father.

This too is impermissible with respect to Him, exalted is He, for He is the Strong, who needs no helper and no support.

Another matter: a person loves a son because he is part of him, and is the cause of his existence, so he loves to have a son from his own loins. This is a branch of his love of possession. A person first loves to have land, then to cultivate it and eat of its produce, then to have animals whose milk he drinks and from which he benefits, and when all this is his, he then aspires to a son. It is as if he progresses from loving inanimate matter, to plants, to animals, to humans.

This matter too is not permissible with respect to Him, exalted is He. If you love a son so that he may be a part of you and of your loins, of whom you take pride in his sonship, then all creation is the dependents and children of Allah, so how would He need a son after that?

So these are all arguments and false matters. Therefore Allah answered them: ﴿Allah has not taken any son﴾ (23:91) [al-Mu'minun]. He brought the particle "min" (of), which indicates generality, meaning: Allah has not taken anything at all that can be called a son, even an adopted one, just as you say: "I have no money," thereby negating that you have any money of worth or value; yet this does not prevent you from having a few pounds or piasters. If you say "I have no money at all," you have negated that you possess even the least thing that can be called money.

With this matter we respond to those who say that "min" here is superfluous, because the speech of Allah is precise and contains no superfluity; superfluity is in human speech, and the Truth, glory be to Him, is exalted above this.

Then the Truth, glory be to Him, elevates us in refuting them, saying: ﴿nor was there any god with Him﴾ (23:91) [al-Mu'minun]: meaning, a deity worthy of worship in truth or in falsehood. Therefore he named idols "gods" (ālihah), but the word "Allah" became specific to the one truly worshipped, glory be to Him. Thus the Truth negated partners with Him in worship, as came in another place: ﴿Had there been in them gods other than Allah, they would have been ruined﴾ (21:22) [al-Anbiya'].

That is: if there were gods in them other than Allah, the heavens and the earth would have been corrupted, and likewise if there were gods alongside Allah, both would have been corrupted as well, because "illa" here is not exceptive; rather it is a noun meaning "other than," and its case-ending appears on the word of majesty after it, "Allah" (Allah being in the genitive, as the word after "ghayr"/"other than" in this sense).

And if you reflect on the multiplicity of gods, its falsehood becomes clear to you. If there were gods with Allah, they would have divided this universe among themselves and made it into sectors, each taking a sector: one for the earth, another for the heavens, a third for what lies between earth and heaven, and so on.

But would any sector of the universe be independent of the others? Would the earth be independent of the heavens? Then there would arise a conflict under which the state of the universe could not be upheld.

Likewise we say: The god who took the earth, for example, why did he not take the heavens? He must have taken the earth by his strength and left the heavens out of his inability, and one who has such a description is not fit to be a god. If they say: They are all strong, and each one of them can create creation alone, we say: Then what is the use of the others?

Then He says, glory be to Him: ﴿Otherwise, each god would have taken away what he created, and some would have overcome others﴾ (23:91) [al-Mu'minun]: meaning, if each of them were to be independent with a sector of the universe apart from the others, affairs would be corrupted, as we see in the human world, where a king tries to seize a part of the earth to which he has no right, and we see the corruption he causes on earth. This is an example of His saying: ﴿and some would have overcome others﴾ (23:91) [al-Mu'minun], and it is one of the forms of corruption.

Therefore the Truth, glory be to Him, addresses this issue and proclaims it before the assembly: ﴿Allah bears witness that there is no god but He, and the angels and those of knowledge...﴾ (3:18) [Al 'Imran].

This is not our speech, nor is this our testimony, but the word of Allah and His testimony to Himself, glory be to Him. But do those gods know of this testimony? If they know of it, then their silence about it and their failure to object is incapacity; and if they do not know, then they are heedless and asleep. In both cases it is not right that they should be gods.

In another place the Truth, glory be to Him, refutes them: ﴿If there were with Him gods, as they say, then they would have sought a way to the Lord of the Throne﴾ (17:42) [al-Isra']: meaning, in this case, they would have gone searching for the god who took from them the universe and transgressed upon their authority, either to confront him and bring him to judgment, or to draw near to him.

Therefore He will say of those you claim to be gods besides Allah: ﴿They seek the means of access to their Lord, which of them is nearest, hoping for His mercy and fearing His punishment﴾ (17:57) [al-Isra']: meaning, Jesus, Ezra, and the angels whom you said were daughters of Allah, all of them seek a means of access to Allah and draw near to Him.

In another place He says: ﴿The Messiah will never disdain to be a servant of Allah, nor will the angels who are near [to Him]﴾ (4:172) [al-Nisa'].

They do not disdain their servitude to Allah; rather they take pride in this servitude, and it angers and grieves them that we should call them gods, or give them more sanctity than they deserve. That is because their loyalty and zeal for Allah, exalted is He, is greater than their loyalty and zeal for themselves.

Therefore, these things they take as gods besides Allah are the first to curse them. The stones they worshipped besides Allah, though the word "worship" here is an error and we use it loosely, since worship is the worshipper's obedience to the command of the one worshipped, and his halting at its prohibition, and stones have no commands and no prohibitions, these stones are more obedient to Allah than they are, and more knowing of Allah than they are. Therefore the stones hate them and curse them, and on the Day of Resurrection they turn against them into a fire that burns them.

Read this exchange, in which the Cave of Hira, which witnessed the beginning of revelation and where the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) found comfort in the first verses of the Qur'an, and the Cave of Thawr, in which the Messenger of Allah sought refuge during the Hijra, vie with one another, and both are stones. The poet says:(1)

How often we envied Hira when you see the spirit, the trustworthy one, nourishing you with lights.
Hira and Thawr became equal; through them, intercede for the state of stones.
They worshipped us, while we are more devoted to Allah than those who stand in the pre-dawn hours.
They made our silence a proof against us, so we became fuel for their fire.
They transgressed in ignorance, as they transgressed against the son of Mary and the disciples.
For the extremist is his recompense, and the one who exceeds in him is saved by the mercy of the Forgiving.

Therefore Allah said to Jesus, peace be upon him: ﴿Did you say to the people: Take me and my mother as two gods besides Allah?﴾ (5:116) [al-Ma'idah].

Jesus says: ﴿If I had said it, You would have known it. You know what is within myself, and I do not know what is within You. Indeed, You are the Knower of the unseen.﴾ (5:116) [al-Ma'idah].

Yes, Allah, exalted is He, knows what His servant and prophet Jesus said, but He wishes to establish against them that He abhors this statement of theirs.

When the Prophet (ﷺ) was saddened by the defeat of the Romans at the hands of the Persians, why? Because they were People of the Book who know God and know the message from God, even though they were disbelievers in it; whereas the Persians were Magians who worshipped fire. So his Lord reassured him, saying: ﴿Alif, Lam, Mim. The Romans have been defeated in the nearest land, but after their defeat they will overcome within a few years. To Allah belongs the command before and after; and on that day the believers will rejoice in the victory of Allah...﴾ (30:1-5) [al-Rum].

If they do not believe in Muhammad, they believe in the Lord of Muhammad. Thus partisanship for Allah is greater than partisanship for the Messenger who conveys from Allah.

Then He, glory be to Him, says: ﴿Glory be to Allah above what they describe﴾ (23:91) [al-Mu'minun]. "Describe" here means "lie," but it is expressed by description, as if the meaning were: if you want to know falsehood, listen to their speech, for it is its precise description. He says elsewhere: ﴿Their tongues describe the lie﴾ (16:62) [al-Nahl]. Their speech is falsehood itself, and it is the truest description of it, because falsehood is that which contradicts reality, and they say nothing but what contradicts reality.

As if you asked: What is foolishness? And I said to you: Look at the conduct of so-and-so. That is, it is the truthful description of foolishness and its clear translation, as if the description has reached a point that gives you the meaning you want in bodily form.

The meaning of ﴿Glory be to Allah﴾ (23:91) [al-Mu'minun] is: He is exalted above all imperfection. It is a verbal noun that existed before Christ existed, so it is an eternal attribute of Allah, since the glorification of Allah was established before He created creation. When Allah created the heavens and the earth, they glorified Allah: ﴿Whatever is in the heavens and the earth glorifies Allah﴾ (57:1) [al-Hadid]. The glorification did not cease after that. The Truth, glory be to Him, said: ﴿Whatever is in the heavens and whatever is in the earth glorifies Allah﴾ (62:1) [al-Jumu'ah].

Since everything glorifies Allah, and He is still being glorified, then glorify, O Muhammad: ﴿Glorify the name of your Lord, the Most High﴾ (87:1) [al-A'la].

How can the whole universe be glorifying while you do not glorify, when you are the master of this universe?

1 - From the poetry of the honourable Shaykh al-Sha'rawi, may Allah have mercy on him.

Then the Truthful, glorified be He, says about His exalted Self:

﴿Knower of the unseen and the witnessed, so exalted is He above what they associate with Him (92).﴾

Knowledge ('ilm): the apprehension of a proposition or of a fact that is established, held with certainty, and supported by evidence. Knowledge is not attained except with these conditions. If the proposition is held with certainty and is factual, but you cannot demonstrate it, as with a child who says, "God is One," this is imitation (taqlid), just as a child imitates his father or his teacher. He imitates another in this matter until he develops his own independent reasoning (ijtihad) on it and is able to demonstrate it himself.

If the proposition is held with certainty but is not factual, this is ignorance (jahl). Ignorance is not, as some think, not knowing; rather, ignorance is that you hold with certainty a proposition that contradicts reality.

For this reason you will find the ignorant person more difficult and more exhausting for those who call to faith and for teachers than the empty-minded person who knows nothing, who has no initial proposition in his mind. The latter awaits you to teach him, whereas the ignorant person first needs you to remove the mistaken proposition from his mind, and then to put the correct one in its place.

The unseen (al-ghayb): what is meant is the absolute unseen, that is, what is hidden from you and from everyone else. We are now a witnessed matter for those who attend this gathering of ours; we are unseen only to those who are absent from it. This is a restricted unseen (ghayb muqayyad), and it includes electricity, gravity, and other such things, because these things were unseen to those before us even though they existed. When we reached their causes, they became manifest to us and became witnessed. For this reason the Exalted said: ﴿And they do not encompass anything of His knowledge except what He wills..(255)﴾ [al-Baqarah].

So He affirmed for people encompassment, but on the condition of His will, exalted is He. If He wills, He makes them aware of the unseen and brings them to knowledge of it at the time of its birth and manifestation.

Thus: what is known to others is not unseen to you, and likewise the unseen to you that has preliminaries leading to it is not unseen. The unseen is rather the absolute unseen, which is hidden from you and from everyone else, and of which God the Exalted said: ﴿Knower of the unseen, He does not reveal His unseen to anyone (26), except to a messenger whom He has approved..(27)﴾ [al-Jinn].

The witnessed (al-shahadah): meaning the witnessed matter. But since the Truthful, glorified be He, knows the unseen, it follows by a fortiori reasoning that He knows the witnessed. Why then mention the witnessed here? They said: the meaning is: He knows the unseen which is hidden from me, and He knows the witnessed for others.

From another angle: since God the Exalted is hidden and concealed from us, while there is an apparent creation, some may think that the hidden is known only as unseen. So He, glorified and exalted, wished to emphasize this matter: He is unseen, yet He knows both the unseen and the witnessed.

We see some people who try to tear away the veil of the unseen and strive to uncover what is concealed from them, going to fortune-tellers, astrologers, and their like, not realizing that the unseen is among the greatest blessings of God upon His creatures. The unseen is the reason for the building of the universe, and by it people deal with one another. This is because man is a son of changing states, greatly fluctuating; if each of us knew and had revealed to him what his brother holds in his heart, people would cut off ties with one another, and some would not benefit from others.

For this reason they say: "If you were to uncover one another, you would not bury one another." That is, if what is in your brother's heart were revealed to you, you would begrudge him even burying him after his death.

Thus, making these matters a concealed unseen softens hearts and enriches goodness among people, so that each benefits from the other. Otherwise, if you knew that someone harbored evil toward you and learned of his hostile stance, you would come to hate even the good that reaches you from him, your heart would be stirred against him with rancor and spite, and you would not benefit from the good deeds within him.

Therefore, we say to the one who seeks the unseen of others: if you wish to know the unseen of another, allow him to know your unseen. But you will not allow him that. So leave the matter as God wills it, and do not seek the unseen of others, so that the course of life may be set straight.

Your Lord always draws your attention to looking at the counterpart. In the sacred hadith: "O son of Adam, you prayed against one who wronged you, and he prayed against you, one whom you had wronged. If I wish, I will answer you and answer him against you; and if I wish, I will leave you both until the Hereafter, where My pardon will suffice you both." (1)

So the Truthful, blessed and exalted, wishes to purify the souls of creation, and that people stop at the limits of what God has made you aware of, and not seek what is concealed, so that you do not tire yourself, and so that you face the troubles of life with a pure soul, content with you and with people.

Then He, exalted, says: ﴿so exalted is He above what they associate with Him (92)﴾ [al-Mu'minun]: because what you associate with God does not know anything of all this, neither the unseen nor the witnessed. Therefore it does not benefit you if you worship it, nor harm you if you do not worship it.

1 - Recorded by Imam Abu Hamid al-Ghazali (3/183) as a saying of Yazid ibn Maysarah: "If you keep praying against one who wronged you, God the Exalted says: another is praying against you because you wronged him. If He wills, We will respond to you and answer him against you; and if He wills, We will delay you both until the Day of Resurrection, where My pardon will suffice you both..."

Then the Truthful Lord says to His Messenger (ﷺ):

﴿Say: "My Lord, if You should show me that which they are promised, / My Lord, then do not place me among the wrongdoing people."﴾

﴿Say..﴾ [al-Mu'minun]: a command from Allah Most High to His Messenger (ﷺ). ﴿My Lord..﴾ [al-Mu'minun]: a vocative in which the particle of address has been omitted, meaning: "O my Lord." ﴿If You should show me that which they are promised﴾ [al-Mu'minun]: meaning, the punishment. ﴿My Lord, then do not place me among the wrongdoing people﴾ [al-Mu'minun]: i.e., if You decree to punish them during my lifetime, then do not punish them while I am among them.

This is from the tenderness of his heart (ﷺ). When the harm and obstinacy of the disbelievers grew severe at the beginning of the call, Allah sent the angels to him offering him revenge upon his people who denied him, but he refused that and said: "O Allah, guide my people, for they do not know" (1).

And he said: "Perhaps Allah will bring forth from their loins someone who will say: There is no god but Allah" (2).

Likewise, his position on the day of the Conquest of Makkah is clear and well known, because he (ﷺ) was sent as a mercy to the worlds.

But did the Messenger say this supplication because he believed that Allah would place him with them when the punishment descends upon them? We say: No, because he did not say this sentence of his own accord; rather, Allah commanded him with it, and the Messenger of Allah would not hold such a belief. Thus, the matter is a revelation from Allah which had to be conveyed to him, and he had to say it just as Allah said it, because its implication is mercy towards him, in that he would not see those being punished; or it is in the manner of the saying of the Exalted: ﴿And beware of a trial which will not afflict those who wronged among you in particular..﴾ [al-Anfal]. This supplication which the Messenger of Allah made repels from him any danger that might befall him and reassures him that this matter will not occur.

As for His saying: ﴿If You should show me..﴾ [al-Mu'minun]: it is composed of (in) and (ma), and both indicate the meaning of conditionality and temporality, as if he said: "Say: at the moment the punishment descends upon them: My Lord, do not place me among the wrongdoing people."

(1) Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ahmad in al-Zuhd, Abu Nu'aym and Ibn 'Asakir reported through the route of Mujahid from 'Ubayd ibn 'Umayr who said: "Noah, his people would strike him until he fainted, then he would recover and say: 'O Allah, guide my people, for they do not know.'" Shaqiq said: 'Abdullah said: "I saw the Prophet (ﷺ) wiping blood from his face while he related the account of one of the prophets, and he was saying: 'O Allah, guide my people, for they do not know.'" [Cited by al-Suyuti in al-Durr al-Manthur 3/481]. See also Ahmad ibn Hanbal's Kitab al-Zuhd (278, 280).

(2) Al-Bukhari in his Sahih (3231), and likewise Muslim in his Sahih (1795), Kitab al-Jihad, from the hadith of 'A'ishah (may Allah be pleased with her) that she said to the Prophet (ﷺ): "Did there come upon you a day harder than the day of Uhud?" He said: "You have suffered from your people what you suffered, and the hardest I suffered from them was the day of al-'Aqabah, when I presented myself to Ibn 'Abd Yalil ibn 'Abd Kulal, and he did not answer me to what I wanted. So I departed, and I was overcome with distress, and I did not come to myself until I was at Qarn al-Tha'alib. I raised my head, and behold, a cloud had shaded me; I looked and in it was Jibril, who called out to me and said: 'Indeed Allah has heard the words of your people to you and their reply to you, and Allah has sent to you the angel of the mountains so that you may command him regarding them as you wish.' Then the angel of the mountains called out to me, greeted me, and said: 'O Muhammad!' He said: 'That is as you wish. If you wish, I will close the two mountains upon them.' The Prophet (ﷺ) said: 'Rather, I hope that Allah will bring forth from their loins those who worship Allah alone, associating nothing with Him.'"

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 23, verse 94:

Repeated text, because it shares wording with verse 93: Then the Truthful One (Al-Haqq), glory be to Him, says to His Messenger (ﷺ):

﴿Say: "My Lord, if You show me that which they are promised, (93) My Lord, then do not place me among the wrongdoing people." (94)﴾

﴿Say..﴾ (93): a command from Allah, exalted is He, to His Messenger (ﷺ). ﴿My Lord..﴾ (93): a vocative from which the particle of address has been omitted; it means: O my Lord. ﴿If You show me that which they are promised﴾ (93): meaning: of the punishment. ﴿My Lord, then do not place me among the wrongdoing people﴾ (94): meaning: if You have decreed that You punish them during my lifetime, then do not punish them while I am among them.

This was from the tenderness of his heart (ﷺ). When the harm and obstinacy of the disbelievers grew severe against him at the beginning of the call, Allah sent the angels to him offering him revenge upon his people who denied him, but he refused that and said: "O Allah, guide my people, for they do not know." (1)

And he said: "Perhaps Allah will bring forth from their loins someone who will say: There is no god but Allah." (2)

Likewise, his position on the day of the Conquest of Makkah is clear and well known, because he (ﷺ) was sent as a mercy to the worlds.

But did the Messenger say this supplication because he believed that Allah would make him with them when the punishment descends upon them? We say: No, because he did not say this sentence of his own accord; rather, Allah commanded him with it, and the Messenger of Allah would not hold such a belief. So the matter is a revelation from Allah which had to be conveyed, and he had to say it as Allah said it, because its meaning is mercy toward him, in that he would not see those who are punished; or in accordance with the saying of the Most High: ﴿And beware of a trial which will not afflict those who have wronged among you exclusively..﴾ (25) [al-Anfal]. And this supplication which the Messenger of Allah made repels from him any danger that might arise, and reassures him that this matter will not happen.

As for His saying: ﴿If You show me..﴾ (93): it is an expression composed of (in) and (ma), and both indicate the meaning of conditionality and temporality, as if he said: "Say: at the moment the punishment descends upon them: My Lord, do not place me among the wrongdoing people."

1 - Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ahmad in al-Zuhd, Abu Nu'aym and Ibn 'Asakir reported through the route of Mujahid from 'Ubayd ibn 'Umayr who said: Noah, when his people would strike him until he fainted, would then recover and say: "Guide my people, for they do not know." Shaqiq said: 'Abd Allah said: "I saw the Prophet (ﷺ) wiping the blood from his face while he related of one of the prophets, and he was saying: 'O Allah, guide my people, for they do not know.'" [Cited by al-Suyuti in al-Durr al-Manthur 3/481]. See also Ahmad ibn Hanbal's Kitab al-Zuhd (278, 280).

2 - Al-Bukhari in his Sahih (3231), and likewise Muslim in his Sahih (1795), Kitab al-Jihad, from the hadith of 'A'ishah, may Allah be pleased with her, that she said to the Prophet (ﷺ): "Has there come upon you a day harder than the day of Uhud?" He said: "I met from your people what I met, and the hardest of what I met from them was the day of 'Aqabah, when I presented myself to Ibn 'Abd Yalil ibn 'Abd Kulal, but he did not respond to what I wanted. So I departed, distressed upon my face, and I did not recover until I was at Qarn al-Tha'alib. I raised my head, and behold, a cloud had shaded me, and I looked and in it was Jibril, who called out to me and said: 'Indeed Allah has heard the words of your people to you and their reply to you, and Allah has sent to you the angel of the mountains, so that you may command him concerning them as you wish.' Then the angel of the mountains called out to me, greeted me, and said: 'O Muhammad.' He said: 'That is according to what you wish; if you wish, I will bring down the two mountains upon them.' The Prophet (ﷺ) said: 'Rather, I hope that Allah will bring forth from their loins someone who worships Allah alone, associating nothing with Him..'"

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 23, verse 95:

﴿And indeed, We are able to show you what We promise them.﴾:

That is: We are able to show you some of the punishment We promised them, but it is not the punishment of total annihilation (isti'sal), because Allah, the Exalted, has honoured your nation, even its disbelievers, by sparing it from this punishment, since it descends upon the disbelievers and leaves none of them behind, and prevents there being among their descendants a believer in Allah. Suppose the punishment of annihilation had descended upon them at Badr, for example: would we have seen believers among them and among their descendants after Badr?

So, the punishment of annihilation occurs only when Allah, the Exalted, knows that there is no benefit in them, nor even in their descendants after them, as happened with the people of Noah. Do you not see Noah, peace be upon him, saying about them: ﴿Indeed, if You leave them, they will mislead Your servants and will not beget except wicked disbelievers.﴾ [Nuh: 27].

Noah could not have said this, or passed this judgment upon his people, except by revelation from Allah, because no one can judge this cosmic matter, which none knows except the Supreme Creator, glory be to Him. For we see the most obstinate of disbelievers and the leaders of misguidance, and then they all believe afterwards and excel greatly in Islam.

Consider 'Ikrimah, Khalid and 'Amr ibn al-'As. How much the believers grieved and were saddened because they escaped being killed, but Allah, the Exalted, has another plan, as though He was saving them to serve Islam and protect the call.

'Ikrimah ibn Abi Jahl displayed rare courage at the Battle of Yarmouk until he was struck a mortal blow, and he leaned on 'Umar and said while giving up his soul in the way of Allah: "Is this a death that pleases Allah and His Messenger with me?"

This was on the day of al-Khandama(1), of which the poet(2) said:

If you had witnessed the day of al-Khandama,
when Safwan fled and 'Ikrimah fled,
and the Muslim swords chased us,
cleaving every forearm and skull,
striking such that you heard nothing but murmuring,
I cried out and neighed around them,
you did not utter a single word of blame.

As for 'Amr ibn al-'As and Khalid ibn al-Walid, what happened with them is known to all of us.

1 - Ibn Kathir said: It is a well-known mountain near Makkah. Ibn Barri said: There was a battle there on the day of the Conquest of Makkah, and from it comes the day of al-Khandama. Khalid ibn al-Walid met them there, defeated the polytheists and killed them. [Lisan al-'Arab, entry: khandama].
2 - Lisan al-'Arab states that this verse was attributed by Ibn al-Sayyid al-Batalyawsi in al-Muthallath to al-Ra'ish al-Hudhali, and Ibn Barri mentioned that it is by Hammas ibn Qays ibn Khalid al-Kinani. It is also said that this verse belongs to Huraym ibn al-Hatim.
3 - Al-nahit: shouting. It is also said: it is the sound from the chest at times of hardship. [Lisan al-'Arab, entry: nahata].
4 - Ibn Manzur cited these verses in [Lisan al-'Arab, entry: khandama] from the words of al-Ra'ish al-Hudhali to his wife, who was blaming him for fleeing, and he said these verses. He had said before that:
If they come today, I have no excuse:
this is complete armour and its weapon,
and a double-edged sword, quick to draw.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi (surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66)) on surah 23, verse 96:

﴿Repel evil with that which is better; We are most knowing of what they describe.﴾ (96):

﴿Repel...﴾ (96) [al-Mu'minun]: indicates repelling. That is: before you is an adversary who attacks you and wants to harm you, and you must repel him from yourself. But "repel with that which is better" means: with the manner or state that is best. If he takes you with harshness, meet him with gentleness, for this is the method that gathers people around your call and wins their hearts to be around you.

As the Most High said: ﴿And had you been harsh, hard-hearted, they would have scattered from around you...﴾ (159) [Al 'Imran].

So if you wish to bring them toward you, repel with that which is better. From this is the position that occurred from the Messenger of Allah on the day of the Conquest, the day his Lord empowered him over the necks of his enemies. He stood before them and said: "O assembly of Quraysh, what do you think I will do with you?" They said: "Good. A noble brother and the son of a noble brother." He said: "Go, for you are the freed ones (al-Tulaqa')." (1)

We notice that they spoke to him in a way that would win his heart and incline him toward them. They reminded him of the bonds of kinship and family, and spoke to him in a way that would soften his heart, and they suggested to him what would benefit them: "A noble brother and the son of a noble brother." They did not say, for example: "You are a victorious commander who can do with us whatever you wish."

Indeed, from these people and their descendants came supporters of Islam and helpers of the call of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ).

And the story of Fudala (2), who used to hate the Messenger of Allah so much that he said before the Conquest: "By Allah, no one is more hateful to me than Muhammad." His rage at the Messenger of Allah increased when he saw him entering Makkah and smashing the idols, so he wanted to push through the ranks to reach him and kill him. Afterward he said: "By Allah, I had not put my hand on him before he became the dearest of Allah's creatures to me." (3)

But what do we repel? We repel (the evil deed). We notice here that our Lord, blessed and exalted, calls us to repel evil with that which is better, not with what is good, because evil is answered by good. Rather, your Lord wants to elevate you in this domain, so He says to you: repel evil with what is better.

In another place He gives us the fruit of this believing conduct: ﴿Then one who is between you and between him enmity [will become] as though he were a devoted friend﴾ (34) [Fussilat]. If you reflect on the meaning of this verse, you will find that the recompense is from Allah, not from the one you treated in this manner, because Allah the Most High says: ﴿as though he were...﴾ (34) [Fussilat], and did not say: "he will become a devoted friend to you."

That is because when you repel with that which is better, your companion becomes ashamed before you, regrets his offense against you, tries to compensate you for it afterward, and does not return to its like again. Yet despite all this, he is not called a devoted friend; rather he is a friend and a near one, because he was the cause of your Lord taking you to His side, supporting you and defending you.

Therefore, when someone insulted al-Hasan al-Basri and reviled him in one of the gatherings, and it was the season of fresh dates, al-Hasan sent him a tray of fresh dates and said to his servant: "Go with it to so-and-so and say: 'My master did not find anything more precious than this to present to you, and it has reached him that you presented him with your good deeds yesterday, and these are without doubt greater than this gift of mine.'" (4)

So, it is foolish for us to attack others with slander, backbiting, defamation and gossip, for by this act it is as though you gave your enemy your good deeds, and gave the greatest of what you possess to the person you most hate.

Do you not see the situation of a father who is harsh with his child, so the child submits and yields, or whose brother wrongs him, so he bears the wrong and does not return it in kind? Then the father is tender toward his child and his compassion increases, and he eagerly seeks to satisfy him. Likewise the Truth, blessed and exalted, deals with His servants in their mutual dealings, and to Allah belongs the highest likeness. Therefore we have said: if the wrongdoer knew what Allah has prepared for the wronged as recompense, he would begrudge him the wrong, for he would wrong him on one hand, and Allah would satisfy him on the other.

It is said that a king had a man with whom he would vent his anger. If the king became angry, he would summon this man and begin to revile and insult him before the people until he calmed down. When the man wished to leave, the king would take him aside and give him a bag of money. One day this man needed money to accomplish a matter he had, so he tried to ingratiate himself to reach the king, then said to him: "Do you not need to insult me today?"

So our matter in this form is: you have only to repel with that which is better. If you find affection and purity from your companion, well; otherwise, Allah's recompense for you is wider and His bounty greater. How beautiful is the poet's saying (5) when he expressed this meaning:

O you whom the deeds of the one and the other distress,
Repel with that which is better, may I be your ransom, until you see
That the one between you and him is enmity, as though he were a devoted friend.

That is: if you wish that the one between you and him is enmity to become as though he were a devoted friend, then act with that which is better.

Then He, glorified, says: ﴿We are most knowing of what they describe﴾ (96) [al-Mu'minun]: its meaning is: you, O Muhammad, take your right from these people, while We do not know what they do to you? Rather, the matter is that We know it well and reckon it against them, and We have prepared for them a fitting recompense. So leave this matter to Us and do not occupy yourself with it.

It is as though the Truth, blessed and exalted, wants to free the person of His Messenger (ﷺ) from the agitations of anger, and that he not be preoccupied even with mere agitation. For when someone confronts you with an evil, you want to gather yourself to respond to him, especially if this response contradicts your good nature and beautiful character, so it is as though He is burdening you with something beyond your capacity.

So Allah the Most High wants to show mercy to His Prophet and to comfort him: leave them alone, and entrust their affair to Us, for We are most knowing of what they describe, that is, of what they lie about concerning you.

1 - Ibn Ishaq said: Some people of knowledge related to me that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) stood in his address at the door of the Ka'bah and said: "There is no god but Allah alone, without partner; He fulfilled His promise, supported His servant, and defeated the confederates alone," until he said: "What do you think I will do with you?" They said: "Good. A noble brother, and the son of a noble brother." He said: "Go, for you are the freed ones." [Cf.: al-Sirah al-Nabawiyyah of Ibn Hisham 4/412].
2 - He is: Fudala ibn 'Umayr ibn al-Mulawwah al-Laythi (al-Isabah, no. 6988).
3 - Ibn 'Abd al-Barr mentioned in his book al-Durar fi al-Siyar that the Prophet (ﷺ) passed by him on the day of the Conquest while he was resolved to assassinate him, and he said to him: "What were you saying to yourself?" He said: "Nothing; I was remembering Allah, exalted." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) laughed and said: "I ask Allah's forgiveness for you," and then placed his hand on his chest. He said: Fudala would say: "By Allah, he did not remove his hand from my chest until there was nothing on the face of the earth more beloved to me than him." Ibn Hajar al-Asqalani mentioned it in al-Isabah (entry 6988).
4 - Abu Hamid al-Ghazali mentioned (3/154) that a man said to al-Hasan: "So-and-so has backbitten you," so he sent to him a tray of fresh dates and said: "It has reached me that you presented me with some of your good deeds, so I wished to reward you for them; excuse me, for I cannot fully repay you."
5 - The Shaykh, may Allah have mercy on him and pardon him.

Then the Truth, glorified is He, says:

﴿And say, "My Lord, I seek refuge in You from the incitements of the devils. (97)"﴾

Why did the seeking of refuge from the incitements of the devils come after this matter? They said: Because Satan wants to interfere, and to appear to you as though he is with you and jealous on your behalf, so that he incites you against them, spurs you on against them, and pushes you towards avenging yourself on them and dominating them.

Hamazat (incitements) is the plural of hamzah, which is the prick or goad by which Satan stirs up a person. From it is the saying of Allah, exalted is He: ﴿And if an incitement from Satan incites you, then seek refuge in Allah... (200)﴾ [al-A'raf].

The Qur'anic verse ﴿And I seek refuge with You, my Lord, from their presence﴾ (98).

Meaning: if Satan enters upon you with his prodding (hamz) and his whisperings, then say: "I seek refuge in Allah from the prods (hamazat) of the devils." Moreover, go beyond that and keep to the side of caution with them: say, "I seek refuge in Allah from their mere presence," even if they do not prod me. For I do not want them in my presence, nor do I want to sit with them.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 23, verse 99:

﴿Until, when death comes to one of them, he says: "My Lord, send me back,"﴾ (99):

That is simply because the agonies of death attend him and he becomes certain that he is dead. The realities are unveiled to him, and he sees what we do not see, as Allah the Exalted says: ﴿So We have removed from you your covering, and your sight today is sharp﴾ (Qaf 22).

So a person wishes to return to the world while he is still in the throes of dying. Why? Because he has seen the reality that he used to deny and disbelieve in. Those who witness the state of the dead at the moment of dying see from them signs indicating that they see things we do not see, each according to his state and his final end.

I recall that when my father died, and he was on my chest at that moment, he said to me: "Amin" (and this is my name in my country), "how are all these palaces being built while you do not tell me about them?"

And the soldiers who cried out in the battle: "Rise up, O breeze of Paradise!" Surely they saw it and smelled its fragrance; otherwise, what made them eager for death and longing for martyrdom, except that they saw a state awaiting them better than what they were in?

Among these is the noble Companion to whom the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) spoke about the reward of the martyrs with Allah, and he had some dates in his hand or was chewing them in his mouth. He said: "O Messenger of Allah, is there nothing between me and Paradise except that I enter this battle and be killed in the way of Allah?" He said: "Yes." So he threw the date from his mouth and went forward to the battle.(1)

It is as if he considered it too much to sit idle from seeking Paradise for the duration of chewing these dates. To this degree the certainty of these men in Allah and in the Messenger of Allah had reached.

We note in this verse: ﴿Until, when death comes to one of them...﴾ (99), in the singular form; then ﴿He says: "My Lord, send me back"﴾ (99), where the plural was used as a form of exaltation, and he did not say "My Lord, send me back" (singular), as in the Exalted's saying: ﴿Indeed, it is We who sent down the Reminder, and indeed, We will be its guardian﴾ (al-Hijr 9).

Here, the Truth, blessed and exalted, magnifies His Essence. But this one magnifies Allah now, while he is in the state of dying, having been a disbeliever in Him, while he was in the ease of the world and the comfort of living.

Or: he repeated the request, "Send me back, send me back, send me back," and Allah gathered them together. Or: he sought help from Allah, saying "My Lord," then addressed the angels: "Send me back" to the world.

(1) It is related that a man came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) on the day of Uhud and said to him: "Tell me, if I am killed, where will I be?" He said: "In Paradise." So he threw some dates from his hand, then fought until he was killed. Related by al-Bukhari in his Sahih (4046) and Muslim (1899) in his Sahih, from the hadith of Jabir ibn Abdullah.

Yet why return?

﴿Perhaps I may act righteously in what I have left behind. No! It is but a word he speaks, and before them is a barrier until the day they are resurrected.﴾ (23:100)

Meaning: I have neglected much of the good deeds, so perhaps if I return after witnessing the reality, I will make up for the righteous deeds I missed. Or perhaps I will act righteously in what I left behind, because I was stingy with my wealth, my effort and my favour toward people; I hoarded much money and left it behind me, and then I am held accountable for it. So if I return, I will present it and spend it on what will be stored up for me for the Day of Resurrection.

Then comes the answer: ﴿No! It is but a word he speaks...﴾ (23:100). That is, his saying: "Send me back, perhaps I will act righteously in what I have left behind" is merely a word with no reality behind it, a word said at a time of distress and hardship. God the Exalted will not return them; and even if He returned them, they would not do it. Therefore He negated it with His saying "No" (kallā), which is used to reject claims that one wants to establish, and God wants to negate them, as occurs in Surat al-Fajr:

﴿As for man, when his Lord tries him and honours him and bestows favours upon him, he says, "My Lord has honoured me." (15) But when He tries him and restricts his provision, he says, "My Lord has humiliated me." (16)﴾ (89:15-16)

So the Truth, glory be to Him, responds: "No" (kallā). Neither are you right, nor is he. Wealth, riches and abundance are not proof of honour, and poverty is not proof of humiliation. Both claims are mistaken, as is evident from the fact that when God gives you wealth but you do not discharge its due to God and the due of His servants, and it does not help you perform what has been enjoined upon you, the wealth becomes a burden on you and a humiliation, not an honour. What is the benefit of wealth if you fall under His saying: ﴿No! Rather, you do not honour the orphan (17)﴾ (89:17)? At that point your wealth will be a proof against you.

Likewise the situation of one who thinks poverty is humiliation: if God strips you of the wealth that makes you rebellious, then He has honoured you, even if you do not perceive this honour.

Then He, glory be to Him, says: ﴿And before them is a barrier until the day they are resurrected.﴾ (23:100). That is: how can they wish to return when between them and it there is a barrier that prevents them from going back to the world? For this reason the interval between the life of this world and the Hereafter is called the barrier life (al-hayat al-barzakhiyya); it is not of this world, and it is not of the Hereafter.

In another place the Truth, glory be to Him, depicts this situation with His saying: ﴿Had they been returned, they would have gone back to what they were forbidden.﴾ (6:28). That is: if We had returned them from the Hereafter, they would have gone back to the disobedience of God in which they were. Although this is a rational proposition, their own reality confirms its truth. Read about them God's saying: ﴿When We bestow favour upon man, he turns away and withdraws to one side...﴾ (17:83). He takes God's blessing and revels in it, then disowns obedience to God.

He also says, in the same sense: ﴿When harm touches man, he calls upon Us, lying on his side, or sitting or standing; but when We remove his harm from him, he passes on as if he had never called upon Us regarding the harm that touched him...﴾ (10:12).

So then: the matter is one of compulsions; whenever they are compelled, they call upon God, seek refuge in Him and implore Him. So take from the reality of their lives what proves the truth of my judgement upon them, were they to return from the Hereafter.

The barrier (al-barzakh) is the partition between two things, and this partition draws its strength from its builder. If this partition is of His making, glory be to Him and exalted is He, then no one will pass through it.

Among this is His saying: ﴿He released the two seas, meeting together (19). Between them is a barrier they do not transgress (20)﴾ (55:19-20). Since they meet, what is the use of the barrier here?

They said: Yes, they meet, and neither of them transgresses against the other, because the matter is not a dam or an engineered construction; rather it is a special barrier that none can bring about except the unrestricted power of God, which breaks the laws of nature, making flowing water like a mountain after Moses struck it with his staff, so that every separation became like a great mountain — the power that caused the rock to gush forth springs.

So the matter is not "mechanics" as some imagine. The barrier between salt water and fresh water is a sign of God visible before us, which all of us can verify for the truth of this phenomenon.

But this barrier is in front of them, so why did He say: ﴿And before them is a barrier until the day they are resurrected﴾ (23:100)?

They said: Because a single word in the language is used with several meanings while the word remains one; therefore they call it the homonym (al-mushtarak). For example, the word ʿayn is applied to the eye that sees, to a spring of water, to a spy, to gold and silver, and to a distinguished man among his people. Context determines the intended meaning, so the listener must be alert to return the word to the meaning suited to its context.

Likewise the word al-najm means a star in the sky, and also a plant without a stem, the grass that livestock graze; from it is the poet's saying:
"I pasture upon the stars as I journey toward you, and my steed grazes upon them in the wilderness."

The word warāʾ is used with many meanings, sometimes opposite ones, which context determines. It may mean "after," as in His saying: ﴿And after Isaac, Jacob﴾ (11:71); it may mean "other than," as in His saying: ﴿Whoever seeks beyond that, those are the transgressors﴾ (23:7); and it may mean "in front of," as in His saying: ﴿And there was behind them a king who seizes every ship by force﴾ (18:79): the king was in front of them, waiting for every approaching ship. Likewise in His saying: ﴿Behind him is Hell﴾ (14:16).

So His saying: ﴿And before them is a barrier until the day they are resurrected﴾ (23:100) means: in front of them.

1 - Maraja al-bahrayn: that is, He sent them forth or released them, flowing while they meet at the mouth of the river. [al-Qamus al-Qawim 2/221].

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 23, verse 101 (part 1 of 2):

Then the Truth, glory be to Him, says:
﴿So when the Trumpet is blown, there will be no kinship among them that Day, nor will they ask one another.﴾

Al-Sur (the Trumpet): the horn into which Israfil blows. What is meant here is the second blast, for resurrection.

Al-Ansab (kinships) is the plural of nasab (lineage), which is a connection through a direct origin, such as the connection of a son to a father, or a father to a son, or a connection through an intermediary, such as paternal and maternal uncles. Lineage is the first bond in creation that ties people together in shared interests, and it is the necessary connection that exists for all people.
